source: Heliand. Trans. Mariana Scott (1966/1969). Via hieronymus.us.com. Public domain.

1.1: Many there were tensing their minds
1.2: … to relate the works wrought among us … so that they began to proclaim God’s word,
1.3: To say what was whispered: that Might-Wielding Christ
1.4: Had here among men done miracles many
1.5: With His words and His works. Wise men aplenty,
1.6: People of earth — all would praise the preachings of Christ,
1.7: God’s holy Word, and write with their hands
1.8: Bright in a book how best God’s bidding
1.9: They might carry out, the kith of mankind.
1.10: There were four from the many: they had might from the Maker,
1.11: Help, too, from Heaven and from the Holy Ghost,
1.12: Strength from the Savior: so were chosen for this.
1.13: Singly they were to inscribe the Gospel there in a book,
1.14: Committing to writing so many commandments of God,
1.15: Holy, heavenly Word: nor dared any here,
1.16: Any child of man, emulate them, these four,
1.17: Picked for the task by the power of God:
1.18: Matthew and Mark, as these men were called,
1.19: Luke, also John — they were beloved of God.
1.20: Worthy were they for the work. The Wide-Wielder
1.21: Had filled the hearts of the heroes with the Holy Ghost,
1.23: And wise words many and still more of wit,
1.24: That they should begin the goodly Gospel
1.25: With their holy voices, raise it on high —
1.26: The Word in this world which has nowhere a like:
1.27: That it praise him ever, the Prince All-powerful,
1.28: The Lord who layeth low the loathsome thing,
1.29: Withstandeth the strife. For He is strong of mind,
1.30: Mild, too, and good — He who is Master of these,
1.32: So were those four to inscribe with their fingers,
1.33: Set down and sing and say forth boldly
1.34: That of Christ’s might and His strength much had they heard
1.35: And had seen indeed, which He Himself had here spoken;
1.37: As He Himself had promised — He, Wielder of Power,
1.38: Wide Ruling Lord — when He first shaped world,
1.40: Surrounding it all with a single Word,
1.41: Heaven and earth and all that they held,
1.42: Full-worked or still waxing: with God’s Word
1.43: All was encompassed and set forth accordingly
1.44: Which world-men should rule over widest lands
1.45: And when each age of this earth should come to its end.
1.47: There was still one before them — for five had slipped by
1.48: For the kinsmen of earth — and now the sixth was to come,
1.49: Blessed by God’s strength and the birth of Christ,
1.50: Best of All Healers, and the Holy Ghost,
1.51: Come to this mid-world to help the many,
1.52: The world-children all ’gainst the wiles of the Fiend
1.53: And his secret snares. So to the Roman folk
1.54: Had Lord God granted the greatest of realms,
1.55: Had strengthened the heart of the crowds of the host,
1.56: So that they laid low much land-folk all over.
1.57: Their helm-wearers had rule from the city of Rome,
1.58: Their leaders had power in every land o’er the people there
1.60: Over the heathens all. Herod was chosen
1.61: King of Jerusalem over the Jew-folk.
1.62: Caesar in Rome’s city, the mighty ruler,
1.63: Had set him there ’mid his thanes. Verily, though,
1.64: He was not kin to the clanships of Israel, not come
1.65: From their best-born; but his bounty he had
1.66: Through the grace of Caesar straight from the Rome-burg,
1.68: So that then the fighting men, famed for their fierceness,
1.69: The children of Israel, friends changeless in strength,
1.70: Were subject to him, since he held sway —
1.72: Of Israel’s landsmen. There lived there then
1.73: An aged man, a wise man of reasonable mind:
1.74: He was come from the people of the clan of Levi,
1.75: The famed son of Jacob of a very fair family:
1.76: Zachary he was hight, was so holy a man,
1.77: For he gladly did give service unto God,
1.78: Worked to His will. So did his wife —
1.79: She was already a very old crone, and no offspring
1.80: Had been granted to them in their youth.
1.81: They lived without fault, warding God’s love,
1.82: Were humbly submissive to the King of Heaven,
1.83: Praising our Prince; nor practiced they evil
1.84: Among mankind; nor did any meanness,
1.85: Neither fault nor sin. Still were they sorrowed of soul,
1.86: Since not ever could they be granted an heir:
1.87: Bereft they of bairns. The bidding of God
1.88: He did in Jerusalem. As oft as his duty
1.89: And the rightness of time did remind him thereof,
1.90: So oft did he hie himself to the holy place,
1.91: To the High One’s temple, to the Heaven-King’s house,
1.92: To serve Him all selfless and make sacrifice,
1.93: Yearning to work with a God-wise mind.

2.94: The time was then come — as they did tell it,
2.95: Wise men with words — that Zachary should stand watch
2.96: There in God’s temple. Many were gathered
2.97: In Jerusalem there of the folk of the Jews,
2.98: Hordes in the holy place. Most humbly they begged
2.100: The Lord of All Heaven to release them from evil.
2.101: The folk stood around by the holy house, and the high-born man
2.102: entered the temple. The others all,
2.103: The folk stayed outside of the sanctuary,
2.104: The host of the Hebrew, till the holy man
2.105: Had worked and had done the All-Wielder’s will.
2.106: As he took the incense, the sage in the temple,
2.107: Round the altar the censer, to serve his Liege —
2.108: Piously labored for his own dear Lord;
2.109: And gladly he served in God’s thralldom
2.110: With a generous heart, as one should joyously
2.111: Follow one’s master There a fright befell him,
2.112: Terror there in the temple. Trembling he espied
2.113: God’s angel inside there in the sanctuary.
2.114: And he spake to the sage, and with words not to fear
2.116: Nor to have any dread. “For thy deeds,” quoth he,
2.117: “Are of worth to the Wielder and thy words as well.
2.118: Thy thralldom has earned thee His thanks, since thou hast believed in Him
2.119: And in His strength alone. I am His angel,
2.120: And Gabriel I am hight. Ever I stand before God,
2.121: Stand in the Almighty’s sight, except that He send me forth
2.122: On some errand for Him. And now He hight me fare forth,
2.123: Bade me to tell thee, that to thee a babe will be born
2.124: From thine aged wife. In this world shall be given unto thee:
2.126: Wise he of word. Of wine he shall never partake,
2.127: In life neither of wine nor of cider. So have the Weird Ones set down:
2.128: The Measurers have marked it and the might of God.
2.129: He bade that I tell thee: he shall be thane
2.130: To the Heaven-King’s Self; bade that ye hold him
2.131: And faithfully foster him. Quoth that he would find
2.132: Honors so many up in God’s kingdom.
2.133: Quoth that the good man should be called John.
2.134: Commanded that ye so call it, that child
2.135: When it doth come. Quoth that Christ’s thane
2.136: It was to become in this wide, wide world,
2.137: Thane of His Own Son. And quoth that they both
2.138: Betake themselves here swiftly for tidings.”
2.139: Zachary then spake and said to God’s angel,
2.140: Beginning to wonder about his deeds and hs words:
2.141: “How can that so come to pass?” quoth he,
2.142: “So late in our lives? For us ’tis too late
2.143: To win such rewards as thy words have spoken.
2.144: For we two were equal of age: twenty winters
2.145: Here in this world, when this woman did come unto me;
2.146: And together we have shared for seventy winters
2.147: Both board and bed, since I chose her my bride.
2.148: In our youth we acquired no offspring, no heir,
2.149: Could beget no babe in our bedchamber —
2.150: Now that we are old, and age has robbed us of deed-strength —
2.152: Dulled is our sight and slow are our loins,
2.153: Our flesh falleth away, our skin in unfair,
2.154: Our limbs unlithe, withered our once-live bodies,
2.156: Mind both and might: so many a day
2.157: We have wandered this world. Methinks ’twere a wonder
2.158: If it ever so happed, as thou hast said with thy words.”

3.159: Then the Heaven-King’s herald was hurt in his mind
3.160: That Zachery should wonder so at His Works
3.161: And would not believe that Holy Lord God,
3.162: If he so willed it, could make him young,
3.163: As once he had been. So the angel chastised him,
3.164: The sage, so that he could not say e’en a single word,
3.165: Nor speak with his mouth “until thy son is come,
3.166: Sprung from thine old wife, an earl and shining,
3.167: Until a young bairn is born to the best of clans
3.168: Here in this world. Then shalt thou again speak words.
3.169: Thy voice shall have strength. Nor shalt thou be silent
3.170: For any time longer.” And straightway it was
3.171: What the Almighty’s angel had there uttered,
3.172: Had told in the temple: that became true.
3.173: Bereft of speech was the sage,
3.174: Though a clear mind he bore in his breast.
3.175: All day they bided before the God-house, the folk —
3.176: And they wondered all, why this praiseworthy man,
3.177: This sage should need so long to serve his Master,
3.178: As never did other thanes in the Lord’s thralldom
3.179: Make such sacrifice with their hands there in the sanctuary.
3.180: Lo: the ancient sage did leave the temple.
3.181: The earls thronged nearer. There was longing in them,
3.183: To hear what he would say most soothly to them,
3.184: How wise he would guide them. But no word could he speak
3.185: Nor say to his retainers; but with his right hand
3.187: He instructed the folk to follow God’s teachings.
3.188: The folk understood that verily he had seen
3.189: Some token from God, though he could not tell them
3.190: Nor show them the truth. There in his turn
3.191: He had worked full well our Wide-Wielder’s service,
3.192: As ’twas marked among men. Soon God’s might was made known,
3.193: God’s strength and His skill: for the crone so aged,
3.195: The wife was with child. Offspring was granted unto them,
3.196: Bairn in the bastion — a so God-like babe.
3.197: And the woman awaited the workings of Weird.
3.198: The winter wore on, the year fell away. John came,
3.199: A light to the earth-folk: fair was his flesh,
3.200: Seemly his skin, and shimmering was he of cheek,
3.201: And the hair of his head and his nails. Now the hoary,
3.202: the wise gathered quickly, the closest of kinsmen,
3.203: Wondering much at the work, how well it could happen
3.204: That a couple so aged could still bear a child,
3.205: a babe in the bastion, unless at God’s bidding.
3.206: They well understood that unless this was so,
3.207: It could never have been — this babe — quite so fair.
3.208: Then an old man spake, one of learned and reasonable mind,
3.209: Who knew wise words. With zeal he did ask
3.210: What the babe’s name should be here below in this world:
3.211: “Methinks in his way and his bearing he is greater than we.
3.213: So I wean that verily God from Heaven hath sent him Himself.”
3.215: Then the child’s mother did straightway speak. She who had borne him did say
3.216: With the babe on her lap: “Last year God’s bidding
3.217: Did come unto us, commanded with words of great weight
3.218: That he be called John, according to the teaching of God.
3.219: Even, indeed, if I might, in my mind I cannot,
3.220: I dare not so change it.” Then spake thereupon
3.221: A most haughty man: From her homeland he was,
3.222: “No aethling is named so, quoth he, “no kith of our clan.
3.223: Now then! Let us choose us another, a nicer name.
3.224: Later indeed he will like it, if he is so able.”
3.225: Again spake the elder, who there could say much:
3.226: “I can never counsel any knight whatever
3.227: To alter God’s word. Let us ask the old man,
3.228: The father, who sitteth wisely in his wine-hall there.
3.229: Though he cannot speak, say a single word,
3.230: He may with his book-letters make us some writing,
3.231: May spell us a name.” Now he came nearer,
3.232: Laid a book on his lap and bade him to write,
3.233: To set down wisely with work-mark and sign
3.234: What they were to name him, that holy babe.
3.235: He took the book in his hand, thought in his heart
3.236: Right gladly of God and writ the name John —
3.237: Wisely he worked it: and with words thereupon
3.238: He did speak unto them, and shrewdly indeed
3.239: Once more he had power to speak, had wisdom and way.
3.240: His pain was now past, his punishment dire.
3.241: God had so made it that in his mind
3.242: He could not so soon forget Him, should he again send His herald.

4.243: ’Twas not long thereafter that all came to pass,
4.245: As Almighty God had promised mankind:
4.246: That He would send the Son of Himself,
4.247: The Heavenly Bairn, here to this world,
4.248: So that He might save the folk all from sin,
4.249: The clansmen from hell-pangs. There came His herald,
4.251: The All-Wielder’s angel, where he knew a woman of worth,
4.252: A maiden right mild. She was called Mary.
4.253: The girl was grown. To a man of good clan,
4.254: To a thane hight Joseph her troth she had given,
4.255: The daughter of David. A dear wife was she,
4.256: A graceful woman and good. There the angel of God
4.257: In Nazareth-burg did greet her by name;
4.258: Stood there before her and spake to her for Lord God:
4.259: “Hail to thee, Mary!” quoth he, “Loved by the Maker art thou!
4.260: Aye, worthy art thou of the Wielder, for thou hast wisdom,
4.261: Lady, gifted with grace. Glorified art thou ever
4.262: Above all women. Be thou not weakly of mind,
4.263: Nor fearful of heart. I come not to hurt
4.264: Nor to bring thee a gull-thing. Thou shalt be our God’s,
4.265: Be our Master’s mother here among men, bearing a man-child,
4.266: Son of the Heaven-King. His name shall be Healer
4.267: Here mid the earth-folk. His end cometh not,
4.268: Nor hath whereover He ruleth ever an end — His realm —
4.269: He, Finest of Folk-Leaders.” The fairest of women,
4.270: The maiden then answered unto God’s angel,
4.271: The loveliest among ladies. “Lo, how may that be?” quoth she,
4.272: “That I shall bring forth a son? Never knew I man in my life.”
4.273: The All-Wielder’s angel had ready his word
4.274: To answer the maid. “From the meadows of sky
4.275: The Holy Ghost shall descend through the strength of God.
4.276: From Him will a Wee One be granted thee here in this world.
4.277: The Wielder’s strength will o’ershadow thee,
4.278: The Heaven-King All High with His shade.
4.279: Below was never a birth so fair,
4.280: Never so wonderous down among men. For from God’s might
4.281: It cometh here to this world.” The heart of the woman was again
4.282: Utterly turned to God’s will at these tidings.
4.283: “All ready stand I,” quoth she, “for such service,
4.284: If He will so have me. His handmaid am I.
4.285: I trust in these things. Therefore let it then hap,
4.286: As thou sayest with thy word, as is His will,
4.287: My Lord’s, my God’s. My mind doubteth not,
4.288: Nor my word nor my way.” So I heard that the woman
4.289: Received God’s tidings all gladly indeed
4.290: With a shimmering soul, with bright shining truth
4.291: And faith clear and fair. The Holy Ghost became
4.292: The Babe in her womb; and in her breast,
4.293: In her heart itself she understood. She said to all whom she wished,
4.294: That she had conceived through the All-Wielder’s strength,
4.295: Holy from Heaven. Then was Joseph’s heart,
4.296: His mind right worried. For this maiden,
4.297: This pious woman, this high-born wife
4.298: He had bought as his bride. He knew she had bairn within her,
4.299: Yet he thought not a whit but that his wife
4.300: Had kept herself carefully. He could not yet know
4.301: The Wielder’s blithe tidings. But to make her his bride.
4.302: He no longer wished, his wife in his halls.
4.303: And thus he began to think in his mind
4.304: How he might forsake her, yet cause her no hardhship nor sorrow.
4.305: He wanted it not noised nor known about
4.306: Among the many. He feared that the children of men
4.307: Would bereave her of life. For this was the land-way,
4.308: The hallowed, old law of the Hebrew folk:
4.309: Whensoever a woman was unrightly wed,
4.310: She must pay with her life for this bedship.
4.311: Never was lady so good that she could long live
4.312: Mid the land-folk, could live ’mid the world-lords.
4.313: Then in his mind the wise man, the good man, Joseph,
4.314: Began to bethink himself of these things,
4.315: How he might slyly forsake the girl.
4.316: ’Twas not long thereafter that the Almighty’s angel
4.317: Hurried to him in a dream, the Heaven-King’s herald,
4.318: And love her, too, in his mind. “At Mary,” quoth he,“thy maid,
4.319: Be not thou wrathful; she is a right good wife.
4.320: Scorn her not sternly. Thou shalt hold her
4.321: And ward her well in the world, as before,
4.322: Fostering thy love-pledge and thy friendship as well.
4.323: Nor let her be loathsome to thee, though she hath Bairn ’neath her limbs,
4.324: A babe in her womb. Through God’s bidding It cometh,
4.325: Through the Holy Ghost from the Heaven-heath here.
4.326: Jesus Christ is that Babe! God’s own Bairn shall He be,
4.327: The All-Wielder’s Son. Thou shalt hold Him well
4.328: With holiness, too. Nor let thy heart doubt,
4.329: Nor thy mind be disturbed.” Then the man’s heart
4.330: Was turned by these words, so that he again won love for this woman,
4.331: For the maid, Marie. God’s might he now understood,
4.332: The Wielder’s bidding. Great was his will,
4.333: That he should hold her, in holiness keep her.
4.334: He cared for her in his home. And she carried all cleanly
4.335: The Holy Ghost — all for God’s glory,
4.336: The Man of Goodness, until God’s fate-word
4.337: Reminded her mightily that unto the light of mankind
4.338: She should bring Him, the Best of all Bairns.

5.339: There came from Rome-burg from the mighty man
5.340: Over the earth-folk, from Octavian himself,
5.341: Ban and bidding over his broad fealty;
5.342: This was come from Caesar unto every king:
5.343: To the home-sitting ones as far as the war-lords
5.344: Wielded their power o’er the people and land.
5.345: ’Twas hight that all men habited outside their own boroughs
5.346: Should seek now their homeland, all heroes their heritage,
5.347: To bide their lord’s heralds; each landsman should go
5.348: To the burg of his birth. The ban was proclaimed
5.349: Over this wide, wide world. And the world-folk did gather,
5.350: In every bastion the men all. The messengers fared forth,
5.351: Those come from Caesar, book-learned thanes.
5.352: And neatly they wrote each name on a scroll,
5.354: Both land and the man, so that no lord could avoid it,
5.355: No man his tax; but all most pay tribute,
5.356: The heroes each for his head. So to his homeland
5.357: Came Joseph, the good man, as God the Almighty,
5.358: The Wielder had willed it; with his family he came,
5.359: Sought his shining castle, his lordly seat,
5.360: The bastion at Bethlehem, where they both did dwell,
5.361: Hero and holy maid, Mary the good.
5.362: There stood in earlier days the shining throne
5.363: Of the high-born king, of the earl of the Hebrews,
5.364: Of David the good, as long as he governed
5.365: And kept lofty seat. They were his kith,
5.366: Were come from his clan, were of good kin all,
5.367: Both through their birth. Then I heard that the bright tidings
5.368: Admonished Mary, and the might of God:
5.369: That on this site a Son should be hers,
5.370: Born here in Bethlehem, the Mightiest of Bairns,
5.371: The Strongest of Kings. Come was the Shining One,
5.372: Mighty here to man’s light, as for many a day
5.373: Pictures of Him and tokens aplenty
5.374: Had foretold in this world. So all had turned true,
5.375: As the sages had spoken it in the long, long ago.
5.376: Through His Own Self’s strength, how most surely He would
5.377: To this earth-realm here — with humility — He,
5.378: Protector to many. Then His mother did take Him,
5.379: And she swaddled Him well, the fairest of women,
5.380: With garments and goodly gems. With her two gracious hands
5.381: She lovingly laid Him, the Little Man,
5.382: The Child in the crib, though He had God’s strength,
5.383: The Master of Men. There His mother sat by Him,
5.384: The woman there waking; she herself warded Him,
5.385: Held there the Holy Bairn; and her heart doubted not —
5.386: The mind of the maid. It became known to the many
5.387: Over this wide, wide world. The warders did hear it:
5.388: Grooms were they there, keeping guard outside,
5.389: Were war-men on watch; with the horses they were,
5.390: With the beasts in the field. And lo: before them they saw
5.391: The darkness divide in the air. Down came God’s light —
5.392: Through the clouds came shining, surrounding the grooms
5.393: Afar in the fields. And sorely they feared,
5.394: These men, in their minds. Then God’s mighty angel
5.395: They saw coming afar. To them together he spake,
5.396: Hight that the grooms not dread any grief
5.397: From the light. “For lo!” quoth he, “A glad thing
5.398: I tell you and truly, long longed-for tidings
5.399: Bespeaking great power: for in this selfsame night
5.400: Christ, Blessed Bairn of our own God, is born in the bastion of David,
5.402: He — our Master All Good. That is joy to mankind,
5.403: The weal of all folk. So that ye may find
5.404: The Mightiest of Babes in Bethlehem-burg,
5.405: Take this as a token that I now tell unto you
5.406: With soothy words: that He lieth swaddled,
5.407: A Child in a crib, though He be King
5.408: Over earth and heaven and the children of men,
5.409: All-Wielder o’er World.” Verily as he spake this word,
5.410: There was come with this single one of the angels
5.411: A multitude down from the meadows of Heaven —
5.412: A holy host, the fair folk of God.
5.413: They spake, lauded greatly the Lord of Mankind.
5.414: They raised holy song, as they returned through the clouds
5.415: To the meadows of Heaven. And the warders did hear
5.416: How the great host of angels gave praise unto Almighty God
5.417: With these words most reverently: “Honor be” quoth they,
5.418: “To our Lord Himself in the highest, to the King of Heaven —
5.420: And on earth be peace to all children of men,
5.421: To folk of good will who accept their God
5.422: With hearts ever pure.” The herdsmen understood
5.423: That a mighty thing had admonished them:
5.424: Blithe tidings there. They turned back to Bethlehem
5.425: That selfsame night, for their spirits longed
5.426: Most greatly to see Christ Himself.

6.427: The angel of God had shown unto them the shining token,
6.428: So that they themselves — they could wander forth
6.429: To the Bairn of God. Straightway they found Him, the Babe,
6.430: The Lord of Mankind, the Master of Peoples.
6.432: They praised God the Wielder, and with their words
6.433: They made known far and wide in the shining castle
6.434: What tokens holy they had seen indeed from the meadows of Heaven
6.435: What signs there, fair in the field. The woman full well
6.436: Kept these things in her heart, the holy virgin,
6.437: The maid in her mind: whatever she heard the men there saying.
6.438: Fittingly she reared Him, the fairest of women;
6.439: With her love the mother did raise the Master of Men,
6.440: The Holy Heavenly Bairn. The heroes did speak
6.441: On the eighth day, the earls of the kingdom,
6.442: Very wise men all, with the handmaid of God:
6.443: That His name should be “Healer,” as the Heaven King’s herald,
6.444: As God’s holy angel, Gabriel had spoken,
6.445: Had bade the woman with words of truth,
6.446: When she first conceived Him, so fair in this world.
6.447: God’s angel she followed, and right gladly, too.
6.448: For great was her will to hold Him in holiness.
6.449: The year strode on, till the Peace-Child of God
6.451: Had forty days and as many nights, too. There a deed needed doing;
6.452: To Jerusalem they must take Him, to the Wielder’s temple.
6.453: That was the way then, the world-folk’s custom,
6.454: Which no Hebrew woman would dare to neglect,
6.455: But that when she had brought forth her first-born son
6.457: She needs must take him to the Lord God’s temple.
6.458: So they did travel, Mary and Joseph, the good folk twain,
6.459: Both from Bethlehem. The Babe they had with them,
6.460: The Holy Christ. They sought then God’s house
6.461: In Jerusalem; they accomplished the custom of Jew-folk,
6.462: Made sacrifice unto the Wielder there in His sanctuary,
6.463: To God in His Temple. There they found them a good man,
6.464: An old one, hard by the altar — aethling-born he —
6.465: So many summers and winters had he spent in the temple,
6.466: Lived in the light, working God’s love
6.467: With a clean soul. Holy spirit he had
6.468: And a joyous heart. Simon was he hight;
6.469: Long had the Lord’s power pointed out to him
6.470: That he would not leave the light of this world,
6.471: Until ’twould be granted him to see with his eyes
6.472: Holy Christ Himself, the King of the Heaven.
6.474: His heart was most blithe in his breast, when he saw the Bairn
6.475: Coming into the temple. He gave thanks to the Wielder,
6.476: To Almighty God, that with his eyen he had seen It.
6.477: To Him he did go and gladly received Him,
6.478: The old man with his arms: all well he did know
6.479: The sign and the symbol, and the Child of God,
6.480: The Heaven-King Holy. “Now, Lord,” quoth he,
6.481: “I gladly shall bid Thee, since aged I be,
6.482: To let me, Thy most humble thane, take leave from here,
6.483: To fare forth in Thy peace to where my forebears did dwell,
6.484: Folk in this world, since my wish is fulfilled —
6.485: The dearest of days: I did see my Liege,
6.486: The Loveliest of Lords, as long, long ago
6.487: It was promised unto me. To all peoples
6.488: Thou art the Light — great Light to all heathen lands,
6.489: Who have not yet accepted the All-Wielder’s power.
6.490: Thy coming, o Master of mine, O my Lord, my dear Lord,
6.491: Is glory and honor to Israel’s children,
6.492: To Thine own landfolk, Thy beloved people.”
6.493: Secretly then the old man there at the altar
6.494: Spake to the good woman, truly did tell her
6.495: How her Son would become to some certain ruin,
6.496: To some consolation, to the children of men —
6.497: A love-thing to those who list to His teaching,
6.498: But harm yet to them, refusing to hearken
6.499: To the gospel of Christ. “Thou shalt suffer,” quoth he, “great care
6.500: And hurt in thy heart, when the earth-children here
6.501: Will kill Him with weapons. This thy great work will be:
6.502: To suffer this sorrow.” The Maid understood all,
6.503: The wise man’s words. There came, too, a woman
6.504: From inside the temple. Anna was she called,
6.505: Was Phanuck’s daughter. Full well her Lord had she served
6.506: With a grateful heart, was an excellent woman.
6.507: After her maidenhood, when a man’s wife she became,
6.508: An earl’s on his estate, this excellent girl,
6.509: With her husband she had held sway
6.510: Seven years o’er his lands. I heard that she then suffered grief:
6.511: That the great might of the Measurer
6.512: Did divide them, Weird most woeful. A widow,
6.513: She dwelt in the temple eighty and four
6.514: Winters here in the world. Well she had served Him, her God
6.515: And her Lord, day and night, never leaving the temple.
6.516: She, too, came to this selfsame place. Straightway she saw —
6.518: She knew God’s Holy Bairn, to the heroes announced it,
6.519: To the folk at the altar, this spell all welcome.
6.520: Said that so near was the Savior’s salvation,
6.521: The help of the Heaven King. “Now Holy Christ,
6.522: The All-Wielder Himself, is come to the sanctuary
6.523: To deliver the folk who have bided so long,
6.524: So many a while in this mid-world here —
6.525: Poor people they — so that in this present thing
6.526: Mankind all may rejoice.” Many were joyous,
6.527: The world-folk there in the temple: they heard the glad tidings
6.528: Spoken by God. The woman had ended the sacrifice,
6.530: As her vow and the book in the shining bastion had told her,
6.531: Her handwork most holy. They went on home
6.533: The Holy Family. They had the Heaven-King
6.534: At their landhouse ever, the Son of the Lord,
6.535: Protector of many. Thus to the people it was not made known —
6.536: Not further known in the world; but so was His will,

7.538: Recognized Christ, at the court of the king
7.539: It was not yet known to the men who in their minds
7.540: Were not rightly inclined; rather concealed from them
7.541: With words and with works, until the wise ones,
7.542: Those men from the East did come to the folk,
7.544: Swift lords on the long way over the land.
7.545: Bright beacon they followed and sought God’s Bairn;
7.546: And with pureness of soul they purposed to kneel
7.547: And confess themselves as His thanes.
7.548: When they found Herod enthroned on high,
7.549: King, speaking slime-words, as mighty he sat
7.550: Mad with his men, ever anxious for murder —
7.551: They addressed him gravely in kingly wise,
7.552: In his house the sages; and straightway he asked them
7.553: What business had brought them out here,
7.554: These war-men from far, far away. “Whether ye carry wound gold
7.555: To give to some man? To whom are ye going,
7.556: Traveling on foot? What? I know not whence ye come from afar,
7.557: Earls of another folk. I see ye are aethling born,
7.558: Kin of good clan. Never before are come here
7.559: Such envoys from another land, since over this folk of men
7.560: I have wielded my power in this great, wide realm.
7.561: Ye shall tell me truly before these retainers
7.562: They answered in turn, the men from the East,
7.564: “Most easily tell thee our business with truth,
7.565: Rightly reveal why we are come here on this road
7.566: From the east of this earth. Aethlings were there,
7.567: Good speaking men, who promised us good
7.568: And help aplenty from the King of Heaven
7.569: Verily with their words. There was a wise man there,
7.570: Hoary and sage — so long ago was that now —
7.571: Our ancestor there in the East — nor has any man since then
7.572: Ever spoken so sharply. God’s spell he could tell,
7.573: For the Lord of the Land-people had lent him the gift
7.574: To hearken up from the earth
7.575: To the All-Wielder’s word. His wisdom was great,
7.576: The thoughts of that thane. Then when he was to depart,
7.577: To forfeit his home and the crowd of the human folk,
7.578: Forsaking the life of the landsmen — and seek the other light;
7.579: Then he called his followers all to come closer —
7.580: His heirs were they there — and to the earls
7.581: He most soothly said what is since then come,
7.582: Hath happed in this world: A Wise King would come here,
7.583: Might and shining come to the mid-world,
7.584: Best by His birth; quoth that God’s Bairn He would be;
7.585: Quoth that in this world He would wield power
7.586: Eternally through all of time over heaven and earth;
7.587: Said that on the selfsame day, when He —so blessed —
7.588: Was born to His mother on this mid-world here —
7.589: So quoth he — in the East would shine a single white star,
7.590: In the heavens on high, such as never before we have had
7.591: Between earth and heaven or anywhere else:
7.592: Neither such Bairn nor such beacon bright;
7.593: That three men from the people should go offer prayer;
7.594: Hight them think well when they would see God’s beacon
7.595: Rise in the East, hight they should ready themselves straightway;
7.596: Hight that we should follow where’er it might fare
7.597: Westward over the world. Now well it hath happed,
7.598: Come through God’s power: a King is born,
7.599: Bold He and strong. We have seen the beacon shining bright
7.600: Over Heaven’s stars. So I know Holy God,
7.601: The Mighty One, hath marked it Himself. Every morn we did see it,
7.602: This brilliant star shining. So we followed the beacon here,
7.603: The while through ways and through woods. That was our greatest wish —
7.604: To see Him ourselves, to know where to seek Him,
7.605: The King in this kingdom. Tell us to which clan He is born.”
7.606: There arose in Herod’s breast a great rage ’round his heart.
7.607: Spirit and heart began to seethe with sorrow within him,
7.608: For he heard them say that he should now have a Head over him,
7.609: A mightier King and one of good clan,
7.610: Blessed ’mongst His folk. Then he ordered them all
7.611: To gather together, what good men there were,
7.612: In Jerusalem the wisest with their speech and their words,
7.614: And in their breasts in book-craft
7.615: Most verily learned. And he asked them with words,
7.616: Most anxiously asked them — this evil-souled man,
7.617: The king of the people — where Christ would be born
7.618: In this world-realm here, the Peace-Wielder Good.
7.619: Then the folk replied, the people most truly;
7.620: Quoth that they knew quite well that He
7.621: Would be born in Bethlehem. “So ’tis writ in our books
7.622: And wisely inscribed, as the truth-sayers,
7.623: Those full wise sages, have spoken it further:
7.625: That from Bethlehem the Herdsman of Bastions,
7.626: The Loved Warder of Land should come to the light;
7.627: The Counselor of Clans should come to His rule
7.628: O’er the hordes of the land-folk; and His grace will hover
7.629: Mild o’er this mid-world for the peoples many.”

8.630: There I heard that as soon as the evil-souled king
8.631: Told the truth-sayers’ word to the travellers, the earls from abroad
8.632: Those faring from far — he questioned them fully,
8.634: When first on the east-path they had then seen it —
8.635: The king-star acoming, the token all clear,
8.636: Bright and high in the sky. They wished to hide nothing from him
8.637: And truly they told him. He hight them travel,
8.638: Go forth on their way; hight that they fathom the news
8.639: Of the New Child’s coming; and the king himself,
8.640: The master of Jews, gave order most sternly
8.641: To the wise men three that when they fared from the West,
8.642: That they should give him account where he could seek that King
8.643: In His hall and His home. Quoth that he with his thanes
8.644: Wished to reverence the Bairn. But he thought to become
8.645: His slayer by the weapon’s edge. Yet All-Wielding God
8.646: Was minded elsewise. He could accomplish,
8.647: Could finish far more in this light; for that shines still long —
8.648: The prophesied power of God! There appeared the symbol
8.649: Clear ’neath the clouds. Those men, wise and clever, made ready
8.650: To travel. They fared forth now from there,
8.651: Bold on their mission. They would seek God’s Bairn,
8.652: They themselves and alone. No thralls had they with them,
8.653: But they were just three: well versed in such things,
8.654: Were indeed clever men, who came carrying their gifts.
8.655: Then they saw it so wisely shining forth ’neath the clouds,
8.656: High in the heavens, where fared the white stars.
8.657: They recognized clearly the beacon of God — through Christ it was worked
8.658: Here in the world. The world-men went following it,
8.659: Full piously thence. Those who could further them,
8.660: Until they well saw, these way-weary men,
8.661: The clear beacon of God bright in the heavens
8.662: Suddenly stop. The star shone light
8.663: And white o’er the house where for His will
8.664: Dwelt the Holy Bairn. And the wife did keep Him,
8.665: The Maid most fittingly. The minds, the hearts of the thanes
8.666: Became blithe in their breasts. Through the beacon’s light they well understood
8.667: That they had indeed found the Peace-Bairn of God,
8.668: The Holy King of the Heaven. When they entered the house,
8.669: Did go with their gifts, the great of the East,
8.670: The way-weary men — quickly the warriors
8.671: Did know Him rightly, All-Wielding Christ. In reverence now
8.672: They fell on their knees before Him, the Child. In kingly wise
8.673: They greeted the Good One and gave Him their gifts —
8.674: Gold and incense as tokens of God,
8.675: And myrrh with it. The men stood ready,
8.676: Fair before their Lord. And with their hands all fittingly
8.677: They took Him and held Him. They betook themselves then,
8.678: The wise men, into the house — way-weary were they —
8.679: The sages into the guest hall. There the angel of God
8.680: Did come to the sleepers, showed a dream in the night,
8.681: Revealed in a vision, as the Lord Himself,
8.682: The All-Wielder, did will it. They thought a man had commanded with words
8.683: That they seek them another way: the aethlings should
8.684: Leave and go to their own land and not seek the loathsome man,
8.685: Herod, the mad-minded king. Then morning did come
8.687: Shining down to the world. The wise men began
8.688: To tell each other their dreams. They did rightly fathom
8.689: The All-Wielder’s word. For great wisdom
8.690: They bore in their breasts. They bade the All-Wielder,
8.691: The Heaven-King on High, that henceforth they might still
8.692: Work His grace and His will; quoth that their souls were turned unto Him,
8.693: Their minds every morn. Then the men travelled hence,
8.694: The earls from the East, as the angel of God
8.695: Had told them with words. They took them another way,
8.696: Following God’s message. Nor would they give
8.697: The king of the Jews account of the birth of the Babe;
8.698: But as they did will it, they went on their way,

9.700: God’s angel did come and to Joseph did speak,
9.701: In a dream did say to the sleeper at night —
9.702: The Master’s own herald — that the slime-mouthed king
9.703: Would seek Him indeed, the Child of God:
9.704: He ws after His life. “Now thou shalt lead Him
9.705: Out into Egypt-land, live midst the land-folk
9.706: There with God’s Bairn; and with God’s handmaid as well
9.707: Thou shalt dwell with the folk, until unto thee cometh
9.708: The Word of the Master, that thou mayest lead
9.709: The Holy Bairn, lead the Lord back to this landscape.”
9.710: Then from his dream Joseph did awaken, jump up
9.711: In his great hall. God’s orders
9.712: He soon recognized; started out on his way,
9.713: The thane with the Maid. Over the mighty mountains
9.714: He sought other folk. For he wished to lead forth
9.715: God’s Bairn from His foes. Soon after the word
9.716: Came to Herod the king, as he sat in his kingdom,
9.717: That the wise men were gone from the West
9.718: Home to their Eastlands, had fared on another way.
9.719: He knew that they had not wanted to tell him the news
9.720: Here in his halls. Then his heart was troubled,
9.721: His mind most mournful; quoth that the men had done this,
9.722: The heroes, to scorn him. So he sat there and sorrowed,
9.723: Bitter rage in his breast. Quoth that a better idea,
9.724: Another he had now thought out. “I know His age now,
9.725: Know His winters’ number; thus I can now bring it to pass
9.726: That on this earth He shall never grow old,
9.727: Here ’mid my hosts.” So Herod sent harshly
9.728: A command o’er his kingdom. The king of the people
9.730: Hight his men go forth; hight them behead with their hand-strength
9.731: So many a babe, bairns born in Bethlehem
9.732: And bred these two years. The thanes of the king
9.733: Did evil deed. So had to die there,
9.734: Though sinless, many a man-child. Never since nor before
9.735: Such a pitiful killing of young kin was there,
9.736: Such a wretched death! The women wept.
9.737: Many mothers did see their sons killed and dead;
9.738: Nor might they help them a whit, with their two hands hold them,
9.739: With their arms embrace them, their own dear bairns,
9.740: Their loved and little ones. But life it had to relinquish —
9.741: The babe in front of its mother. Their misdeeds these rogues
9.742: Saw not, saw not their sins. With the sword’s edge
9.743: They committed great crimes. They cut down many
9.744: A child-young man. The mothers bewailed
9.745: The death of their babes. Care was in Bethlehem,
9.746: Loudest lamenting: if they had lashed
9.747: Their hearts with a sword’s edge, they could not have
9.748: Them worse in the world. The women many,
9.749: The brides there of Bethlehem: they saw before them their bairns,
9.751: Bloody they lay on their laps. The baneful murderers
9.752: Killed the innocent crowd. From their crimes
9.753: They refrained not a whit: it was their will
9.754: To kill Christ Himself. But God, strong and clever,
9.755: Saved Him from them and their hatred. In the night
9.756: He had the earls lead Him to Egypt-land,
9.757: The good men with Joseph to the green fields,
9.758: To the richest earth, where that river floweth,
9.759: The Nile-stream wide, north to the sea,
9.760: The fairest of floods. There the Peace-Bairn of God
9.761: Dwelled as He willed until Weird did remove
9.762: Herod the King. Hate-filled, forsook he the children of men,
9.763: The life of the earth-folk. O’er his lands
9.764: His heir was to rule. Archilaus
9.765: He was hight, hero of helm-wearers — he!
9.766: He was to rule o’er the Jewish folk there in Jerusalem,
9.767: Wield power o’er the people. Then the word did come
9.768: There in Egypt to the aethling man:
9.769: That he spake to Joseph — God’s angel himself,
9.770: The Lord God’s herald. Hight him again lead the Babe
9.771: Back to the land. “Now he hath left the light,”
9.772: Quoth he, “Herod the king. Once ’twas his will to kill Him,
9.773: Delivering Him from this life. Now in peace ye may lead
9.774: The Child to His kinsmen. Now the king liveth not,
9.776: God’s token completely. Straightway they readied themselves,
9.777: The thane with the Maid. They speedily sought to go thence,
9.778: Both with the Bairn. Bright fate they fulfilled,
9.779: The will of the Wielder, as He bade them with words.

10.780: Mary and Joseph were again come to Galilee-land;
10.781: The Holy Family of the King of Heaven
10.782: Were with Him at Nazareth-burg. There he waxed ’mid the folk,
10.783: Our saving Christ. He grew full of sense, full of knowledge,
10.784: And the grace of God was with Him, and great the love
10.785: Of His mother’s kin: like no other man was He,
10.786: This Youth in His goodness. When twelve years He did have,
10.787: When such an age He’d attained, there the time was then come,
10.788: When they in Jerusalem, the Jewish folk all,
10.789: Should serve their Lord, their God Himself
10.790: And should work His will. They were in the temple
10.791: There in Jerusalem, the Jews all together,
10.792: Mighty gathering of men. And Mary herself
10.793: Was there in the crowd; and her Son she had with her,
10.794: God’s Own Bairn. When they now had made sacrifice goodly,
10.795: The earls at the altar, as their law did order,
10.796: Had fulfilled their folk-way — the folk fared thence,
10.797: The world-men as they willed it, while in the temple
10.798: Stayed God’s Mighty Child, though His mother most truly
10.799: Knew nothing of it. Now, she weened He had left,
10.800: Had fared with her friends. She first found it out
10.801: On the day that came after, the aethling’s wife,
10.802: The holy Maid — that He was not ’mid the men-folk.
10.803: Then Mary’s spirit was deeply in sorrow,
10.804: Her heart most troubled, that she did not find the Holy Child
10.805: Among the crowd. Greatly she was grieved then,
10.806: The handmaid of God. She hied herself to Jerusalem once more
10.807: To seek her Son. And she found Him sitting
10.808: Inside the temple, where sat the sages,
10.809: The very wise men who verily read
10.810: And learned God’s law, how with their words
10.811: They could work the praise of Him Who created this world.
10.812: There sat in their midst God’s Mighty Bairn,
10.813: All-Wielding Christ — although those who there warded
10.814: The temple could not recognize Him even a whit.
10.815: And anxious for knowledge, He asked them questions
10.816: With wise words indeed. They wondered all
10.817: How so childlike a Man could utter such speeches,
10.818: He with His mouth. There His mother did find Him
10.819: Sitting down ’mongst the sages; and she greeted her Son,
10.820: The Wise ’mid the folk. And with her words she did speak:
10.821: “Why, dearest Man, hast Thou given Thy mother
10.822: Such sorrow indeed, that I needs must seek Thee —
10.823: I, worried wife, a woman so troubled,
10.824: Among these burghers?” Then answered the Bairn
10.825: With wise words, indeed: “What? Thou knowest right well,” quoth He,
10.826: “That I here belong; with happiness here
10.827: Most rightly dwell where My Mighty Father
10.828: Wieldeth His powers.” The woman understood not,
10.829: Nor the sages there in the temple, why He said such a word,
10.830: Did speak with His mouth such a sentence. Mary kept all
10.831: Concealed in her breast, what she heard her Bairn speak
10.832: With His wise words. Then they went from there,
10.833: Left Jerusalem both, Mary and Joseph.
10.834: They had with them the Son of the Lord,
10.835: The Best of all Bairns that was ever born,
10.836: Child from a mother: they had for Him mighty love
10.837: With pureness of heart, and He hearkened to them,
10.838: God’s Own Bairn to His blood-kin,
10.839: To His parents twain through His humble mind.
10.840: In His childhood He never sought to reveal
10.841: His greatness of strength, that so mighty a power
10.842: He did have in this world; but He bided His time —
10.843: In proper manner thirty years in the midst of the people,
10.844: Before He would show a single token,
10.845: Say to the people that He Himself was
10.846: Here in this mid-world the Master of Mankind.
10.847: To Himself He had kept it, God’s Holy Bairn —
10.848: The word and the wisdom and all His great wit,
10.849: His very wise mind. From His words no man would know,
10.850: From His speech, that such wit was His —
10.851: That this Hero harbored such thoughts. But as was proper to Him,
10.852: He awaited the shining token: His time was not come yet,
10.853: When He o’er this mid-world should make it wide known,
10.854: Should teach the folk to follow their belief
10.855: And to work God’s will. But many well knew,
10.856: Folk in the land, that He was come to the light,
10.857: Though they could not recognize Him all clearly as yet,
10.858: Until He Himself would indeed say the word.

11.859: John had grown up out of his earliest youth,
11.860: Had waxed in the wilderness. Nor was there any world-man
11.861: But him alone who so served All-Wielding Christ.
11.862: Faithful His thane, he forsook the multitude,
11.863: The company of men. Then came to him mightily
11.864: There in the wilderness word from Heaven:
11.865: God’s goodly voice gave John command
11.866: To proclaim Christ’s coming proclaim His great strength
11.867: Wide o’er this mid-world with words of truth;
11.868: Hight that he say that the true Kingdom of Heaven
11.869: Was close for them, the children of mankind,
11.870: In this landscape here was near for the land-folk,
11.871: The most wondrous riches. His will was great
11.872: To relate to them of such blessed raptures.
11.873: He set out and went where the water,
11.874: The Jordan did flow all joyfully there,
11.875: Made known through the land to the landsmen all day,
11.876: To the folk that with fasting they might atone
11.877: For many a wrong, make better their sins themselves.
11.878: “That ye may now become clean,” quoth he. “The Heavenly Kingdom is close
11.879: For the children of men. Ye yourselves in your minds
11.880: In your spirits, too, rue all your sins, rue
11.881: The hurts ye have done against folk, and hearken ye to my teachings,
11.882: Turn to my words. Into the water
11.883: I shall dip you all dearly, though from your deeds,
11.884: Your sins, though, themselves I cannot absolve you —
11.885: That ye through my handwork are henceforth cleansed
11.886: Of your loathsome deeds. But He is come to this light,
11.887: Mighty to mankind, and standeth right in your midst;
11.888: Though ye yourselves do not want to see Him,
11.889: He will baptize you both in the name of the Lord
11.890: And of the Holy Ghost. He is Lord High over all.
11.891: He can free each man from his misdeeds,
11.892: Shear him from sin, who would be blessed of soul
11.893: Here in this world, if such be his will:
11.894: To do what God’s Own Dear Bairn doth command
11.895: For these earth-folk here. As His herald now
11.896: I am come to this world and shall make Him His way,
11.897: Teaching the clansmen to keep their belief
11.898: Through pureness of heart, that they go not to hell
11.899: Nor face the fire. Full glad be his soul then,
11.900: Joyous so many an hour — whosoever forsaketh sin
11.901: And the devil’s ambush: he acquireth the grace
11.902: Of the Good One, the Heaven-King — he who hath a heart pure and loyal
11.903: For Almighty God.” Many an earl
11.904: Through these teachings, many folk truly,
11.905: World-men did ween that this was All-Wielding Christ,
11.906: Since he did so speak so much of soothness,
11.907: Such words of truth. Then wide and far it was known
11.908: To every man over the promised land,
11.909: To all kin in their courtyards: then there did come
11.910: Jewish folk seeking him out from Jerusalem,
11.911: Grooms from the bastions, and asked if he were God’s Bairn
11.912: “About whom so long,” quoth they, “the land-folk have spoken,
11.913: The world-men said verily, that he should come to this world.”
11.914: But John took the word and boldly did speak
11.915: To the heralds. “I am not,” quoth he, “God’s Bairn,
11.916: The Verily Wielding Christ. But I am here to make way
11.917: For Him, for my Lord.” The heroes then asked,
11.918: The earls who were hearing asked the herald then;
11.919: Those from the town asked him for tidings. “If thou art not truly God’s Bairn,
11.920: Art thou then Elias, who in earlier days
11.921: Was amid the folk? Certainly he is again
11.922: Come on in this mid-world. Say what manner of man
11.923: Art thou? One of those who was once here,
11.924: One of the soothsayers? What shall we say
11.925: To the folk, tell them of truth? Never was come
11.926: To this mid-world another man ever
11.927: So famous of deed. Why dost thou dip
11.928: These folk here, if the foretold Savior
11.930: Thou art not?” Then John the Good wisely gave answer:
11.931: “I am the foreboder, the envoy of Him, of my Master,
11.932: My beloved God. I am to make ready the land,
11.933: The world-folk right to His will. Through His word indeed
11.934: My voice is made strong, though few understand it,
11.935: The world-folk here in the wilderness. In no way am I like unto Him,
11.936: Like my Master and Lord. He is mighty of deed,
11.937: Is so noble and strong — that shall be soon known to the many,
11.938: The war-men here in this world — so that I am not worthy
11.939: Of tying the lace of His shoe, though His own slave
11.940: I be — and He so lofty a Lord; so much better
11.941: Is He than I. Nor herald on earth
11.942: Is His equal now nor ever shall be
11.943: On the face of this world. Keep ye your will with Him,
11.944: O ye folk, your belief, for long shall ye be
11.945: Then joyous of heart; for the forces of hell
11.946: Ye have forsaken and the evils of life; and seek ye then for yourselves
11.947: God’s light, home of all heavenly good, eternal kingdom,
11.948: High meadows of Heaven. Nor let ye your hearts be in doubt.”

12.949: So the young man told, as were God’s teachings,
12.950: Revelations to mankind. Many did gather
12.951: To Bethany there, the bairns of Israel —
12.952: Came there to John, the king’s underlings all,
12.953: People to learn, and received belief.
12.954: He dipped them each day and reproached them their deeds,
12.955: Their will to do wrong; and for them praised God’s Word,
12.956: The Word of his Lord: “The Heavenly Kingdom,” quoth he,
12.957: “Standeth ready and right for all men who are mindful of God
12.958: And believe in the Healer with pureness of heart,
12.959: And list to his teachings.” He was not long there,
12.960: That from Galilee came God’s Own Bairn,
12.961: Our Dear Lord’s Son, seeking to be dipped.
12.962: Our Good Wielder’s Bairn was now so grown
12.963: That among the land-folk He had lived
12.964: Thirty winters here in this world. As was His will,
12.965: He came there, when John baptized them in Jordan’s stream,
12.966: Dipped the folk right dearly and all day long.
12.967: Straightway when he saw his Master Sweet,
12.968: His Lord, his heart grew blithe, for that was his wish,
12.970: And with words he addressed Him: this goodly man, John, spake to Christ:
12.971: “Now Thou art come to my dipping, my Lord, O my God,
12.972: Thou Best of Folk-Rulers. So I shall do for Thee,
12.973: Since Thou art the strongest of kings.” Christ Himself hight him,
12.974: The Wielder verily, that he utter such words no more.
12.975: “Knowest thou that it is fitting,” quoth He “that we now fulfill
12.976: Forthwith all that is right, as is truly His will?”
12.978: John stood and dipped much folk all the day,
12.979: Many world-men in water; and also All-Wielding Christ,
12.980: The High King of Heaven, with his hands he baptized
12.981: In the best of baths; and he bent his knee
12.982: To pray, strong as he was. And Christ arose,
12.983: Fair from the flood, Peace-Bairn of God,
12.984: The Lord of all Land-Folk. When He entered the land,
12.985: Heavens door did ope, and from the All-Wielder above
12.986: Came the Holy Ghost, came down to the Christ.
12.987: He came in the likeness of a lovely bird,
12.988: A strong, fair dove, and He sat Him down upon our sweet Lord’s shoulder,
12.989: Hovered over the Wielder’s Bairn. Then word came from Heaven,
12.990: Loud from the high, cloudless vault, and greeted the Healer Himself,
12.991: Christ, the Best of All Kings. Quoth that He Himself had chosen
12.992: Him from His kingdom. Quoth that He loved His Son
12.993: Best of all born men. Quoth that He was His all-dearest Bairn.
12.994: As God willed it for him, John verily saw this
12.995: And heard it as well. Soon after this he did make known
12.996: To the children of men that they had a Mighty Lord,
12.998: The One All-Wielder. Of this I will be witness
12.999: Here in the world: for God’s word did tell it,
12.1000: The voice of my Lord, when He hight me dip them,
12.1001: The world-folk in water, when I truly did see
12.1002: The Holy Ghost mightily coming down from Heaven’s meadows,
12.1003: Seeking a single Man in this mid-world here.
12.1004: ‘That,’ quoth the voice, ‘that will be Christ,
12.1005: The Fair Son of the Lord. He shall dip the folk
12.1006: In the Holy Ghost and heal many a man
12.1007: From his dire misdeeds.’ This power He doth have from Lord God;
12.1008: That He can remove from all mankind
12.1009: Their blame and their sins. This is Christ Himself,
12.1010: God’s Own Bairn, the Best of all Men,
12.1011: Bulwark against the baleful fiend. Well — ye may be joyous of mind
12.1012: Here in this world. As it was your will,
12.1013: While still alive, to see your Land-Ward
12.1014: Himself. Released from its sin, many a soul,
12.1015: Many a ghost will go to his God, will be
12.1016: Freed from his misdeeds, which here toileth loyally with friends
12.1017: And firmly believeth in All-Wielding Lord,
12.1018: In Christ Himself. That will be of great help,
12.1019: Of goodly avail to all men, whosoever gladly so do.”

13.1020: Then I found this to be: that to all folk,
13.1021: To all peoples, John praised Christ’s teachings,
13.1022: Those of his Lord, through which they could win
13.1023: The Kingdom of Heaven, the holiest of goods,
13.1024: Blessed life eternal. But He Himself, our Lord so good,
13.1025: The Son of the Wielder went in the wilderness
13.1026: After the dipping. He was there in the desert,
13.1027: Our Lord of Earls, a long, long while,
13.1028: Nor had He more folk about Him, more men in His following.
13.1029: He Himself chose it to be even so. He wished
13.1030: To be tempted by the most terrible of demons,
13.1031: Strong Satan Himself, who drives folk to sin,
13.1032: Drives men to their misdeeds. He knew Satan’s mind,
13.1033: The evil will of the varlet, who once in this world
13.1034: At its very beginning betrayed them, the earth-folk,
13.1035: Seduced them with sinfulness, since he caused those two,
13.1036: Partners in wedlock, Adam and Eve, to become untrue
13.1037: Through deceit — so that the children of men
13.1038: After their earth-trip must travel to hell,
13.1039: The ghosts of all folk. This God Almighty —
13.1040: All-Wielder, He — wanted to change; He wanted to give to the earth-folk all
13.1041: The high realm of Heaven. Therefore He sent here a Holy Herald,
13.1042: Sent His Son Himself. Then Satan was filled
13.1043: With hate in his heart. He begrudged Heaven’s kingdom
13.1044: To the children of men. He aimed to cheat Him, the Mighty,
13.1045: Cheat the Son of the Lord with the selfsame tricks
13.1046: With which he had once so treacherously
13.1047: Gulled Adam himself, so that he grew hateful to God —
13.1048: He deceived Him with sin: the same he minded to do
13.1049: To All-Healing Christ. But He kept steadfast His heart
13.1050: ’Gainst the wicked wight — the All-Wielder’s Bairn
13.1051: Kept hardened His heart. He wished Heaven’s kingdom
13.1052: Secure for the land-folk. The Land-Warden lay lonely
13.1053: For forty nights. He did fast there,
13.1054: The Master of Mankind. As long as He partook not of meat,
13.1055: Then they did not dare, those devilish wights,
13.1056: The hate-minded fiends, fare nearer unto His face
13.1057: Or greet Him. He weened that that long He was truly as God,
13.1058: Unmixed with something of mankind — the Mighty One
13.1059: Heaven’s Holy Warder. As He let Himself hunger,
13.1060: So that He began to want meat because of his manliness,
13.1061: There came closer the Fiend after the forty days,
13.1062: The murky misdoer. He weened that surely He was simply a man.
13.1063: Then he went and spake unto Him with these words.
13.1064: The spear-foe did greet Him: “If Thou art God’s Son,” quoth he,
13.1065: “Why hast Thou not, if Thou has the power,
13.1066: Ordered these stones to be bread, and, Best of all Bairns,
13.1067: Hast not healed Thyself of Thy hunger?” Then spake again Holy Christ:
13.1068: “The children of men,” quoth he, “may not live alone
13.1069: By bread, the earth-folk all, but they shall be
13.1070: In this world for the teaching of God and shall do the works
13.1071: Which have been proclaimed aloud by the Holy Tongue,
13.1072: The gums, the voice of Lord God: that is a good man’s life,
13.1073: For the kinfolk all, that they accomplish
13.1074: What they are bidden by the world of the Wielder.”
13.1075: The noisome fiend came nearer then
13.1076: For another time and slyly tempted
13.1077: And baited his Master. The Peace-Bairn of God suffered
13.1078: The will of the Evil One and indeed gave him power
13.1079: That he might try himself against His great might.
13.1080: He let him lead Him — the scourge of the land-folk —
13.1081: And take Him on to Jerusalem there to the temple of God:
13.1082: High over all on the very highest of houses
13.1083: He did set Him up and spake scorn-words to Him,
13.1084: The Evil One with such mockery. “If Thou art the Almighty’s Son,”
13.1085: Quoth he, “glide down to earth. Long hath it stood
13.1086: Written in books that He hath bidden —
13.1087: The Almighty Father — bidden His angels
13.1088: That they be Thy warders on all of Thy ways,
13.1089: Hold Thee under their hands. Why then? Thou mayest never
13.1090: Stub even Thy foot on any hard stone.”
13.1091: Then spake again Holy Christ, the Best of Bairns:
13.1092: “So it is also most rightly written in books,” quoth He,
13.1093: “That thou shalt not try Him, shalt not tempt thy Master,
13.1094: Thy Liege Lord ever. That befits thee not in the least.”
13.1095: For a third time then He let the scourge of the land-folk
13.1096: Take Him up high on a mountain. There the treacherous Fiend
13.1097: Let Him look over all of the land-folk,
13.1098: Over winsome goods and the worldly kingdoms
13.1099: And all such possessions as the earth surrounds
13.1100: For fairer use. And there spake the fiend once again to Him,
13.1101: Quoth that He would give unto Him all those goodly things,
13.1102: These noble fiefdoms, “If Thou wilt kneel before me,
13.1103: Fall in front of my feet, confess me Thy lord,
13.1104: And pray at my lap: then will I let Thee enjoy
13.1105: All these possessions, which I have here placed before Thee.”
13.1106: No longer would He listen to the loathsome word;
13.1107: Holy Christ no longer would hear, but He drove him forth,
13.1108: Away from His favor; swept Satan away, and then spake:
13.1109: The Best of All Bairns bade that men all should pray
13.1110: To Almighty God; and Him alone
13.1111: Should they serve — the many thanes,
13.1112: The heroes hoping for grace, “There help will reach
13.1113: Every man whosoever he be.” Then the menace of men,
13.1114: Satan himself became saddened of mind;
13.1115: The devil went down to the dales of hell.
13.1116: There came much folk from the Almighty above down to Christ:
13.1117: God’s angels did come to give unto Him
13.1118: Friendship and following and to serve Him faithfully, humbly
13.1119: As one should one’s God, one’s Liege, the King of Heaven Himself, for His grace.

14.1121: For a long while the, God’s Blessed Bairn dwelt in the wilderness,
14.1122: Till it seemed to Him better for the benefit of all
14.1123: That He show His great strength to the folk. Thus He forsook
14.1124: The shade of the forest, the spot in the wood,
14.1125: And again He did seek the company of earls,
14.1126: The illustrious thanes and the throngs of men,
14.1127: And He betook Himself to Jordan’s shore. There John found Him,
14.1128: The Peace-Bairn of God, his Master all good,
14.1129: The Holy Heaven-King. And he said to the Hero,
14.1130: John, His disciple, when he saw Him coming:
14.1131: “That is the Lamb of God, who shall release the folk
14.1132: In this wide, wide world from their wicked sins,
14.1133: All men from their misdeeds: glorious Master,
14.1134: Most Strong of All Kings!” Christ then went forth
14.1136: Fared to His Friends, where fair He was born
14.1137: And most rightly reared; and relatd with words,
14.1138: Christ ’mongst His kinfolk, the Richest of Kings,
14.1139: How they themselves should atone for their sins;
14.1140: Hight them to rue their harmful works many,
14.1141: To let fall their false deeds: “Now ’tis fulfilled,
14.1142: As the old men have said, as the sages did speak,
14.1143: Promised help unto you from the Heavenly Kingdom.
14.1144: Now it is near through the Savior’s strength. And ye shall rejoice therein,
14.1145: Each of you will gladly give service to God
14.1146: And will work His will.” There arose joy ’mid the world-folk,
14.1147: ’Mid the gathered crowd. Christ’s teachings became sweet
14.1148: To the followers all. He began to gather together
14.1149: Youths for disciples, young men and good,
14.1150: Word-wise warriors. He went to the shores of a water,
14.1151: There where the Jordan had spread to a sea
14.1152: On the border of Galilee-land. There He saw sitting
14.1153: Andrew and Peter, found the two by the flowing water.
14.1154: The brothers both down by the broad stream
14.1155: Were very neatly throwing their nets,
14.1156: Fishing in the flood. There first the Peace Bairn of God
14.1157: Himself did greet them on the shores of the sea.
14.1158: Hight that they follow Him, quoth that He would give them
14.1159: Much of God’s kingdom. “As ye here catch fish,
14.1160: So shall ye both with the force of your hands fetch the children of men,
14.1161: So that they may enter the Kingdom of Heaven,
14.1163: People aplenty through your message and word.” Much pleased of spirit were they,
14.1164: Both of the brothers. They perceived God’s Bairn,
14.1165: Their beloved Lord. They left all things,
14.1166: Andrew and Peter, whatever they owned by the flood,
14.1167: Had won by the water. Truly the will was great in them
14.1168: To go along with the Bairn of God,
14.1169: To be in His retinue and to reap blessed reward.
14.1170: So do all folk who would earn their Lord’s favor
14.1172: And would work His will. As they went along
14.1173: The shores of the water, they met a sage
14.1174: Sitting by the sea and his sons twain,
14.1175: Jacob and John, young men on the Jordan.
14.1176: Sons and father, they sat on the sands;
14.1177: Neatly they knotted and mended their nets
14.1178: With both their hands, the nets which the night before
14.1179: They had slit in the sea. Then He spake unto them;
14.1180: God’s Blessed Bairn bade them be on their way now with Him.
14.1181: Jacob and John, they both did go,
14.1182: The child-young men. Christ’s word was for them
14.1183: So worthy here in this world, that on the shores of the water
14.1184: They forsook their father alone by the flood,
14.1185: The ancient alone, and all that they owned,
14.1186: Their nets and their well nailed ships. They chose All-Nurturing Christ,
14.1187: Holy Savior and Lord. To earn His help
14.1188: Was the need they felt. So feel all thanes,
14.1189: All warriors here in this world. Then the All-Wielder’s Son
14.1190: Went forth with the four. And He chose the fifth;
14.1191: Christ picked at a market place a king’s young vassal,
14.1192: A wise-minded man: Matthew was he hight.
14.1193: A thane was he to an aethling born.
14.1194: There he was to take with this hands tithe and toll
14.1195: For his lord; loyal he was to his task,
14.1196: Noble his looks and his bearing. But he left them all —
14.1197: Gold and silver and gifts so many,
14.1198: Treasures most dear — and became our Lord’s man.
14.1199: The king’s thane chose Christ for his Lord,
14.1200: A more generous Gift-Giver than ever his master
14.1201: Had been in this world. He received a worthier thing,
14.1202: Longer lasting gains. It became known to the land-folk,
14.1203: To each in his bastion, that the Bairn of God
14.1204: Was gathering disciples, and He Himself spake
14.1205: So many a wise word and such words of truth,
14.1206: That shining wonders He did show them and tokens
14.1207: Did work in this world. Through His works
14.1208: It was visible, through His deeds as well, that he was the Master,
14.1209: The Heavenly Lord who had come to help
14.1210: The children of men in this mid-world here —

15.1211: To the land He oft made this clear;
15.1212: For He worked there so many a wonderous token,
15.1213: As He healed with His hands the halt and the blind,
15.1214: Relieved many land-folk from loathsome ills,
15.1215: From such sickness as at that time Fiend Satan
15.1216: Had thrown on the children of men — the hardest of all,
15.1217: Long lasting illness. The land-folk came there
15.1218: Day after day, where our Dear Lord was
15.1219: Himself with His faithful, until many folk
15.1220: Were gathered together, a very great crowd
15.1221: Of land-folk, though they were not all come with a like belief,
15.1222: World-men all with one will: some sought the All-Wielder’s Bairn —
15.1223: Poor men were they and in want of food —
15.1224: So that they might beg Him amid the multitude
15.1225: For meat and for drink, amid the crowd; for there was many
15.1226: A goodly thane who gladly did give
15.1227: Of his alms to the poor. And again there were some,
15.1228: Clans of the Jews, sly folk were they. They were come to this place,
15.1229: So that they might discover our Master’s deeds
15.1230: And His words as well. Stealthy of mind were they,
15.1231: Wrathful of will. They wanted to make All-Wielding Christ
15.1232: Loathed by all land-folk. Thus would they not list
15.1233: To His teachings nor turn to His will. Some others were sages,
15.1234: Wise men indeed and worthy of God:
15.1235: Among the people the pious. They were come for the preaching of Christ,
15.1236: So that they might hear the Holy Word
15.1237: And learn and listen. Their belief they had firmly established —
15.1238: They had pious hearts; and straightway they became his thanes,
15.1240: So that on the day of their death He would take them to the dearest of goods —
15.1241: The Kingdom of Heaven. Christ gladly received
15.1242: So many of mankind and granted unto them His merciful rule
15.1243: For a long, long time — for that so well He could do.
15.1244: There was a great crowd gathered round glorious Christ:
15.1245: So much of the folk was assembled. He saw them come from all lands,
15.1246: From all the wide ways, the world-men together,
15.1247: Fine folk and strong. His fame was spread far
15.1248: To many a man. Then the Mighty Christ
15.1249: Went up on a mountain, the Mightiest of Bairns;
15.1250: And He sat aside from the rest. There He chose for Himself
15.1251: Twelve specially picked, men true and loyal —
15.1252: Good folk whom He wished with Him as His vassals,
15.1253: Disciples of Him, their Master, each day.
15.1255: He called them by name and bade them come nearer:
15.1256: First surely Andrew and Peter also,
15.1257: The brothers twain, and these two with them,
15.1258: Jacob and John — they were worthy of God.
15.1259: Mildly inclined was His mind unto them. They were one man’s sons
15.1260: Both through their birth. The Bairn of God chose them,
15.1261: These fair ones, as followers; and much folk, too,
15.1262: Most famous men; Matthew and Thomas,
15.1263: The Judases twain and the other Jacob;
15.1264: He was a cousin of His — they were come from two sisters,
15.1265: Come from the same clan, Christ and Jacob, very good kin.
15.1267: Now All-Healing Christ counted nine of His men,
15.1268: Loyal hearted thanes they. Then He hight the tenth also come
15.1269: And join His disciples: Simon was he called.
15.1270: And He called Bartholemew, too, to fare up the mountain
15.1271: Away from the folk. And Philip was with them.
15.1272: True hearted men were they all. The twelve went together,
15.1273: The fighters all to the confab, there where the Councillor sat;
15.1274: The Protector of Many made known unto them
15.1275: How He planned to help mankind ’gainst the pangs of hell,
15.1276: ’Gainst the infernal flame — help those who would follow
15.1277: The fair, sweet message, as He sought to reveal it
15.1278: There in His wisdom to the world-folk many.

16.1279: Then they stepped nearer to All-Saving Christ,
16.1280: Such disciples, as He had chosen Himself,
16.1281: The Wielder amid His vassals there. And the wise men
16.1282: The heroes, stood all gladly about God’s Son,
16.1283: The war-men most willingly; they awaited His word,
16.1284: Thought and were silent, longing to hear what the Lord of the Land-folk,
16.1285: The Wielder Himself, would make known with His words
16.1286: For love of the land-folk. There sat the Shepherd of Lands
16.1287: Across from His good men, God’s Own Bairn.
16.1288: With His talk ’twas His will to teach them — the people —
16.1289: Wise words aplenty: how in the realms of this world
16.1290: They could best bring about bounteous praise of our Lord.
16.1291: He sat there, was silent — our Holy Savior —
16.1292: And looked at them long. Our Lord was gracious of spirit,
16.1293: Mild was His mood; and as He unlocked His mouth,
16.1294: The All-Wielder’s Son did show them with words
16.1295: Many a marvelous thing; and to the men He said
16.1296: Such wise words — to them, whom He, All-Wielding Christ
16.1297: Had chosen here for this speech; those of the children of earth
16.1298: Who were worthiest of God, men of good clan.
16.1299: He spake to them soothly; and said those were blessed,
16.1300: The men on the mid-earth, who in their minds,
16.1301: Their hearts, were poor for humility’s sake. “For to them is given
16.1302: The Eternal Kingdom, the holiest of Heaven’s meadows,
16.1303: Life without end.” And He also told them,
16.1305: That blessed were, too, the gentle and mild. “They may inherit this glorious earth,
16.1306: The very same kingdom.” Quoth that those, too, were blessed
16.1307: Who bemoan here their misdeeds. “Await joy they may,
16.1308: Consolation perfect in their Master’s kingdom.
16.1309: Blessed be those who have done good, heroes who justly have judged:
16.1310: For their piety they will be plenteously filled
16.1311: In the kingdom of God: such good things will greet them,
16.1312: These world-men who have judged well and justly Nor will they be cheated
16.1313: Whose hearts are mild in their heroes’ breasts. For them will the Holy Lord,
16.1314: The Mighty, be mild. Blessed those ’mid the folk
16.1315: Who have cleansed their hearts: They will see the Heaven-Wielder
16.1316: In His own kingdom.” Quoth that they, too, were blessed
16.1317: Who live in peace ’mid the folk. “Have started no feud, no affair,
16.1318: With their doing. Sons of the Lord indeed they’ll be called.
16.1319: For He Himself will be gracious to them, Most gladly will they
16.1320: Long enjoy the Lord’s kingdom.” Quoth that they, too, were blessed,
16.1321: Those war-men who ever will right, “and through this willingly suffer
16.1322: The harm and hatred of richer men. To them is the Meadow
16.1323: Of God’s Heaven then given, and the spirit’s good life
16.1324: Forever, for all days, and the end never cometh
16.1325: Of the winsome possessions.” So All-Wielding Christ
16.1326: Had told the earls ’round about Him of eight blessed states;
16.1328: Through these shall each one straightway find Heaven, if that be his wish;
16.1329: Or he shall be deprived of joy and possession
16.1330: For eternal times, as soon as he exits this world,
16.1331: Life’s fate on this earth, and seeketh another light,
16.1332: Either a fair one or a foul — even as he hath lived ’mid the folk,
16.1333: Worked with them here in the world. Thus He spake with His words.
16.1334: All-Wielding Christ, the Richest of Kings,
16.1335: The Own Bairn of God did say to His disciples;
16.1336: “Ye shall also become blessed,” quoth He, “because the people,
16.1337: The folk of the land will fight you, speak evil of you all,
16.1338: Hold you up to scorn and harm you muchly
16.1339: Here in this world; and working worse wrong,
16.1340: Condemn you with sinful speech and so much of hatred;
16.1341: Denying your teachings and doing loathsome deeds,
16.1342: Harm for your Lord’s sake. But let ye your hearts still be happy,
16.1343: Your lives ever, too, since reward standeth ready for you
16.1344: In the kingdom of God; and every good, also,
16.1345: Great and manifold: that is given unto you as a gift,
16.1346: A treasure, since here first ye have toiled, have endured
16.1347: Pain in ths world. It is worse for those others:
16.1348: Grimmer judgment awaits them who have goods here on earth,
16.1349: Wide worldly treasure. They waste here their pleasure,
16.1350: Enjoy them enough. These men shall suffer
16.1351: A harrowing judgment after their journey.
16.1352: They shall bemoan their misery, who are now so merry
16.1353: And living in lust, nor let go willingly
16.1354: Their sinful thoughts, which tempt their spirits,
16.1355: Their loathsome wrongs. For them shall come as reward
16.1356: An evil most painful. These people will see sadly their plight,
16.1357: Face troubled their end. All sore shall their spirits be,
16.1358: For too much in this world they followed their will,
16.1359: These men, as they were minded, indeed. Now for their misdeeds ye shall
16.1360: Reproach them, rise against them with words, as I now shall reveal unto you
16.1361: And most soothly say, O ye, My disciples,
16.1362: With words of truth: that of this world
16.1363: Ye shall henceforth be the salt of sinful mankind,
16.1364: Absolve them from bad deeds, so that to a better thing
16.1365: They may turn the land-folk: to forsaking the Fiend’s work,
16.1366: The deeds of the devil; and to seeking their dear Lord’s realm.
16.1367: So with your lessons ye shall turn the land-folk
16.1368: To My will. However, if any of you fade away,
16.1369: Turn aside from the teachings which are entrusted to you,
16.1370: Then ye are like unto salt which is scattered
16.1371: Wide on the seashore; then it is of worth to none,
16.1372: And the bairns of the land-folk will walk on it with their feet,
16.1373: Men grind it in grit. All who are to proclaim it, God’s Word,
16.1374: Will thus suffer: if he permitteth his spirit to doubt,
16.1375: If he is not bent to spur men to the blithe realm of Heaven,
16.1377: But wavereth in his word — then the Wielder groweth grim,
16.1378: The Almighty is enraged, and the children of men, also.
16.1379: To the bairns of the earth he will become hated,
16.1380: To all the land-folk, if his lesson be not of worth.”

17.1381: So spake He wisely and said God’s spell.
17.1382: The Land-Warder taught them, His people with pureness of mind.
17.1384: The heroes stood gladly ’round the Son of God,
17.1385: World-men to His will. They longed for His words;
17.1386: They thought and were silent. They heard Him say it —
17.1387: The Lord of the Land-folk give God’s law to the children of men:
17.1388: He promised the Heaven and thus spake to the heroes:
17.1389: “This, too, I may tell you, My disciples, most truly
17.1390: With soothy words: that ye henceforth shall be
17.1391: The light in this world to the bairns of the landsmen,
17.1392: Friend to all people and over much folk,
17.1393: Shining and winsome: nor may your great works
17.1394: Remain hidden, nor yet with what hearts ye proclaim them —
17.1395: No more than a castle can remain ever concealed
17.1396: Which standeth on a mountain or steep on a cliff,
17.1397: A giant-made work. No more can your words
17.1398: In this mid-world, your deeds be hidden to men. Do as I teach you:
17.1400: Let your light shine forth large to the land-folk,
17.1401: To the bairns of men, that they may know your minds and your souls,
17.1402: Your words and your will, and thus praise All-Wielding God,
17.1403: Their Father in Heaven, With pureness of heart;
17.1404: Here in this light praise Him who gave this lesson to you.
17.1405: Let him who hath light leave it not hidden from the land-folk,
17.1406: Nor cover it heavily; rather high in his great hall
17.1407: He shall set it up, so that all within shall have sight thereof,
17.1409: The heroes in the great hall. Even so may yet not hide
17.1410: The Holy Word from the folk here in this land,
17.1411: Keeping it from man’s kind; but the commandment of God
17.1412: Ye shall spread abroad so that all the bairns
17.1413: Over this large landscape, the folk shall indeed understand.
17.1414: And so do ye that which in former days
17.1415: The wisest men did speak with their words,
17.1416: When they then, the earls, did follow the old law,
17.1417: And for this reason as well, as I now say unto you:
17.1418: That all men may serve God as the only law doth bid them.
17.1419: Never ween for one instant that I come to this world
17.1420: To lay low and destroy the old law
17.1422: Among the people, or to contradict the word of the prophets,
17.1423: Who, as men of truth, gave clear commandments
17.1424: In days of yore. Sooner shall both fall apart,
17.1425: Heaven and earth, which are held bound together,
17.1426: Before any word which verily the wise men
17.1427: Commanded the folk remaineth one whit unfulfilled
17.1428: Here in this light. I came not to World
17.1429: That I should fell it, the prophets’ word, but to fulfill it rather —
17.1430: To enlarge it and make it anew for the aethling bairns,
17.1431: For the good of this folk. That was formerly written
17.1432: In the old law: ye have oft heard it spoken
17.1433: By word-wise men: whosoever doth act thus here in this world,
17.1434: That he berefts another of his old years,
17.1435: Whosoever cheats him of life: to him shall the children of men
