17.1436: Deal out death; and now I shall tell you more deeply,
17.1437: Shall discuss it still further: whosoever shall foster hatred,
17.1438: One man ’gainst another, deep in his mind —
17.1439: Who beareth a grudge in his breast, though they be all brothers,
17.1440: God’s blessed folk, bound together in kinship,
17.1441: Men into clans. And still a one becometh so grim of mood
17.1442: ’Gainst the other, that he would rob him of life, if he could right well do it,
17.1443: Then he is straightway doomed — deprived of his life,
17.1444: Is indeed so judged, as was the other
17.1445: Who through the might of his hands cut off the head
17.1446: Of another earl. Also in the law it is written
17.1447: With words of truth: and yet all know it well —
17.1448: That with all one’s heart one should love one’s neighbor,
17.1449: Most zealously love those closest, be kind to one’s kinsmen,
17.1450: Good to all kith, and mild in one’s gift-giving;
17.1451: Have love for his friends and hate for his foes,
17.1452: Withstand them with a strong, with a strife-eager heart,
17.1453: Ready ’gainst their evil and wrath. But I relate yet another law,
17.1454: A fuller one still for the folk: that ye have fondness now for your foe,
17.1455: In your heart love him well as ye would your kin —
17.1456: And in God’s name ye so do it. Do ye much good unto him,
17.1457: Show him pureness of spirit and loyalty sweet;
17.1458: In return for his loathsomeness do ye love him. That is long lasting counsel
17.1459: For every man whose mind hath been turned
17.1460: In hate ’gainst his foe. Ye shall all gain from this,
17.1461: For ye shall be called the Heaven King’s sons,
17.1462: His bairns all blithe. Nor may yet find better counsel
17.1463: Anywhere in this world. I verily tell you,
17.1464: Say to each bairn, that ye may not bring
17.1465: Your goods with an angry heart into God’s temple,
17.1466: Into the Wielder’s house; it be not worthy
17.1467: For Him to accept, as long as ye harbor anger,
17.1468: Foster fiendishness, one to another, far deep in your hearts.
17.1469: First shalt thou be reconciled with him who opposeth thee,
17.1470: Shalt be tranquil of spirit; then mayest thou offer thy treasures,
17.1471: On God’s altar give them — worthy they be of our good Lord,
17.1472: Of the Heaven King worthy. For His kindness shall ye serve Him more,
17.1473: For His favor follow God’s will more, than most of the other Jews do,
17.1474: If ye would someday own the Eternal Kingdom,
17.1475: See life without end. I shall still say unto you,
17.1476: As the old law once bade you:
17.1477: An earl should never covet another man’s wife,
17.1478: Seduce her with sin. This I also say unto you now,
17.1479: Soothy words: that a man’s eye may quickly lead him astray
17.1480: Into murky misdeeds, if he letteth his mind be driven,
17.1481: So that he beginneth to yearn for her who may never be his.
17.1482: Then he hath straightway done sin unto himself,
17.1483: Hath loaded hell-pangs upon his heart.
17.1484: If then a man’s eye or again his right hand
17.1485: Or some limb lead him along the loathsome way,
17.1486: Then ’would indeed be better for yon earl,
17.1487: Better for that bairn of men, that from his body he loose it,
17.1489: Cast it from him afar, coming to Heaven without it —
17.1490: Than that he flee with all to Inferno,
17.1491: That with a whole body he go to the grounds of hell.
17.1492: Human frailty so willeth, that no man shall follow his friend,
17.1493: Though a dear friend he be, if he driveth him on to sin,
17.1494: Draweth him down to guilt. ’Tis no matter then, how close they do stand in the clan,
17.1495: How mighty their kinship, if he maketh him murder,
17.1496: Draweth him down to misdeeds. Better he do this:
17.1497: That he cast his friend far away from him
17.1498: And lose all his kinsmen and have no love for a one,
17.1499: That he may alone mount on high
17.1500: To the kingdom of Heaven, than in the pangs of hell
17.1501: Both would suffer broad punishments, too,

18.1502: Here in the law it also
18.1503: Standeth written with soothy words, so that yet may all understand it:
18.1504: That all people should ever avoid perjury,
18.1505: Nor themselves swear falsely, since that is great sin,
18.1506: Leading much folk astray along loathsome ways.
18.1507: Then I shall also say unto you, that no one should swear,
18.1508: No child of man swear any such oath,
18.1509: Neither by Heaven on high (since that is the Lord’s throne)
18.1510: Nor by the earth here below (since that is All-Wielder’s
18.1511: Footstool so fair), nor should any child of the folk
18.1512: Swear by his own head, since he may turn not a single hair,
18.1513: Either black or white, but as Holy God
18.1514: Hath mightily marked it. Therefore the many,
18.1515: The earls should avoid every oath-word. He who oft
18.1516: Sweareth becometh steadily worse, since no longer can he ward for himself.
18.1517: Therefore I say unto you with soothy words
18.1518: That ye shall never swear any stronger oaths,
18.1519: Mightier ones with men except as with My words
18.1520: I most verily here do command you:
18.1521: If a man hath trouble with another, let him speak the truth;
18.1522: Say ‘yea,’ if it be so, confess that it is true;
18.1523: Say ‘nay,’ if it be not, and let that be enough.
18.1524: If a man sayeth more, much beyond that,
18.1525: It becometh a bad thing for the bairns of men,
18.1526: So that earls, all disloyal, will not believe
18.1527: One another’s word. Then I also verily tell unto you:
18.1528: As by the old law ye were so bidden:
18.1529: Whosoever taketh the eye of another man,
18.1530: Looseneth it from his body, or some limb indeed —
18.1531: That he shall pay to the person for the loss
18.1532: With a like limb of his own. Now I give you this lesson:
18.1533: Ye shall not wreak vengeance for deeds done wrong.
18.1534: Instead shall ye suffer most humbly all things yourselves,
18.1535: The pain and the wrong that people will do you here in this world.
18.1536: Let each earl do unto another whatsoever is good and is useful,
18.1537: If he so willeth, that the children of men
18.1538: Do good unto him; that God will be mild unto him,
18.1539: Mild unto each man who doeth the Master’s will.
18.1540: Respect ye the poor and divide ye your riches,
18.1541: Among those who are needy. Nor be ye troubled, if ye receive no thanks,
18.1542: No reward in this passing world. But well may ye hope
18.1543: Will reward you with gifts, grant you good pay
18.1544: For what ye have done for your love of Him.
18.1545: If thou wouldest give to good men all
18.1546: Fair shining coins, and thinkest thereby
18.1547: To reap a reward, how wilt thou then have return from God,
18.1548: Or largess here in the light? For these are brief-lasting goods.
18.1549: So it is for all that thou doest for others,
18.1550: For love of the land-folk — if thou thinkest to receive the like
18.1551: In word and in work: why should the Wielder know thanks,
18.1552: Since thou givest to them and gettest from them in return?
18.1553: Give thou thy riches to the poor men, who give unto thee
18.1554: No rewards in this world; and strive then for the Wielder’s realm.
18.1555: But act thou not loudly, when thou givest thine alms
18.1556: To the needy of men; but be thou meek all of mind,
18.1557: Glad for God’s thanks; for a goodly reward wilt thou take,
18.1558: Find a fair return, where far longer
18.1559: Thou shalt use it. That which thou givest with a pious heart,
18.1560: And sharest in secret, is esteemed by our Lord.
18.1561: Nor boast of thy giving — let no great lord do so either —
18.1562: Lest through idle boasts the gift is made naught
18.1563: And forlornly lost. Before the eyes of the Lord
18.1564: Shalt thou receive thy reward for thy work right and good.
18.1565: Also shall I bid thee, when thou bendest thy knee
18.1566: In prayer, begging help from the Lord, begging
18.1567: That He grant thee release from the loathsome thing,
18.1568: From sin and from shame, which ye yourselves
18.1569: Have wrongfully wrought — ask not before others
18.1570: Nor make it known to the many, lest men extol you
18.1571: And give praise to you; and the prayer to your Lord
18.1572: You lose most forlornly for idle fame.
18.1573: But if ye do ask help from your Lord on high,
18.1574: Praying most humbly to Him — that must ye surely here do —
18.1575: That your Battle-Lord befree you from sin,
18.1576: Do ye so in the darkness: yet your Lord doth know,
18.1577: He, Holy in Heaven, since nothing is hidden to Him,
18.1578: Neither of words nor of works. Thus will He make it,
18.1579: As ye have bidden of Him — if unto Him ye have bent
18.1580: Your knee, your hearts being pure.” The heroes all rose,
18.1581: The men stood gladly around God’s Son,
18.1582: The world-men to their will. They longed for such words,
18.1583: Pondered and kept their peace. The people had need
18.1584: To think over again all that the Holy Bairn
18.1585: Had told unto them on this first time,
18.1586: Had all clearly proclaimed. Then spake one of the twelve;
18.1587: Of the goodly men one began to ask of God’s Bairn:

19.1588: “Master good,” quoth he, “we are in need of Thy grace
19.1589: To work Thy will and Thy word as well,
19.1590: Best of All Bairns, and we bid Thee teach us
19.1591: To pray, Thy disciples, as doth John,
19.1592: The dear Baptist, on every day,
19.1593: Teaching his world-folk with words how to greet the Wielder,
19.1594: To speak to their God. For Thy disciples do Thou the same.
19.1595: Reveal Thou the runes.” Then the Ruler had ready
19.1596: His answer for them, the Son of the Lord,
19.1597: For them His good word. “If ye would greet God,” quoth He,
19.1599: The King Full of Strength, speak ye then as I teach you:
19.1600: Father of us, who art all Thy folk-bairns,
19.1601: Thou who art on high in the kingdom of Heaven,
19.1602: Hallowed Thy name here in every world,
19.1603: Thy kingdom come in strength and craft,
19.1604: Thy will be done over all the world;
19.1605: As here on earth; so there above
19.1606: On high in the kingdom of Heaven.
19.1607: Give us each day, good Lord, Thy gracious guidance,
19.1608: Thy holy help, and absolve us, O Warder of Heaven,
19.1609: From the manifold mischief we do against mankind,
19.1610: Let not loathsome wights lead us astray,
19.1611: As is their will and as we are worthy;
19.1612: But help us against all our evil deeds.
19.1613: So shall ye bid Him, when ye bend for prayer,
19.1614: Ye men, with your words, that the Mighty Wielder
19.1615: Release you from the loathsomeness that is in all land-folk,
19.1616: If ye then would forgive the land-folk all
19.1617: Of their sins and their selfishness, such wrongs as they
19.1618: Have done against you — The Great Wielding God will absolve you,
19.1619: The Father forgive you your frequent faults
19.1620: And your heavy sins. But if ye harden your hearts,
19.1621: Are not willed to absolve other earls, other men from their wrong,
19.1622: Then Almighty God will not forgive you your grim sins,
19.1623: But ye shall receive from Him just reward,
19.1624: Payment most pain-filled throughout plenteous time,
19.1625: For all the unrightness ye have done against others
19.1626: In the light of this world, without that ye have willed
19.1627: To make peace in your matters with the children of men
19.1628: Before ye shall wander, O ye men, out of this world.
19.1629: Today I shall also tell you how ye shall bring My teachings to pass:
19.1630: For if ye would indeed keep a fast
19.1631: To make little your misdeeds, make it not known
19.1632: To the many, but hide it from all; yet Almighty God knoweth well,
19.1633: The Wielder, your will; if other world-bairns,
19.1634: Other land-folk fail to laud you, yet lovely reward He will give,
19.1635: Your Holy Father, in Heaven’s kingdom,
19.1636: Since ye have served Him, ye men, so humbly here,
19.1637: So piously all ’mid the people. Unright possessions,
19.1638: O my earls, covet them not; but care for rewards above
19.1639: With All-Wielding God. That is a weightier thing
19.1640: Than if a man liveth richly here on this earth,
19.1641: Winning the goods of this world. If ye would hear then My word,
19.1642: Gather ye not great treasures, neither silver nor gold
19.1643: In this mid-world here, nor hoards of riches;
19.1644: For it reddens with rust here, and robbers will steal it.
19.1645: Worms gnaw it away; the garments wear threadbare,
19.1646: The gold-wealth is gone. Do ye good works
19.1647: And gather in Heaven a hoard far greater,
19.1648: Riches fairer by far. Your foe cannot rob you,
19.1649: Can take nothing from you. For treasures stand ready
19.1650: For you up yonder, as much as ye there
19.1651: Have gathered in Heaven riches and goods,
19.1652: Heroes, ye, through your hand-gifts. And keep ye steadfast your hearts
19.1653: For this; for there lie the thoughts of men,
19.1654: Their minds and their hearts; there lieth the hoard,
19.1655: The goods all gathered. Nor is any man so greatly blessed,
19.1656: That both he may do in this broad, wide world:
19.1657: That on this earth he may live richly indeed
19.1658: In all of his world-lusts, yet thankfully serve All-Wielding God
19.1659: At the selfsame time: but he shall ever
19.1660: Forsake wholly one or the other,
19.1661: Either the lusts of the body or life everylasting.
19.1662: Therefore grieve ye not for your garments, but hold ye fast unto God,
19.1663: Nor mourn in your minds, how on the morrow
19.1664: Ye may find eat and drink, or, ye aethlings,
19.1665: What weeds ye will wear; for All-Wielding God
19.1666: Knoweth the needs of hem who now serve Him well,
19.1667: Following the will of their Liege. Why, by the winged birds
19.1668: Ye may verily see it: they that are in this world
19.1669: Flitting about in their feather-dress. Though they have won no fortune,
19.1670: Yet the Lord, our God, giveth to them each day
19.1671: Help against hunger. Ye may in your hearts
19.1672: Eke gaze at the flowers, when ye think of your garments,
19.1673: How fairly they are garbed, as they stand in the field
19.1674: Brightly blowing. Nor did that warder of bastions,
19.1675: Solomon the King, who had costlier treasure,
19.1676: Greater gold-hoards than any had e’er gained,
19.1677: Had won more wealth, the choicest of weeds —
19.1678: Still in this life, though he was lord of these lands all —
19.1679: He never found raiment as fair as this flower hath on,
19.1680: Which here in the field standeth ready and fair,
19.1681: Lily with so lovely a bloom. The Wielder of Lands hath so garbed it
19.1682: From the high fields of Heaven. But this folk is far dearer,
19.1683: The men mean far more, those whom He hath made in this land,
19.1684: Wielding o’er them, as He willed. Therefore may ye not worry concerning your dress,
19.1685: Grieve over your garments so much; God will give counsel,
19.1686: Help from Heaven’s meadow, if ye willingly serve for His favor,
19.1687: Always yearn for God’s kingdom; then act ye according to those, His good works.
19.1688: Strive ye for right things. Then will our Rich Lord
19.1689: Gift you with all goods indeed, if ye so willingly go,
19.1690: Following Him, as I tell unto you with soothy words.

20.1691: Ye shall never speak an unjust, a wrong judgment
20.1692: Over any man, or accuse him falsely;
20.1693: For doom falleth over him, so that the cares full well,
20.1694: The worries wax large of him who did speak such words
20.1695: Of wrong against others. Not a one of you
20.1697: Shall give wrong measure to another man,
20.1698: Being feloniously bent in buying or selling
20.1699: While on this earth here; for to each earl will hap
20.1700: Even as he hath done unto others — even there where he would dearly
20.1701: Not see his sins. Eke must I say yet unto you
20.1702: Where ye must guard against the greatest of evils,
20.1703: Against wrong-doings many: Why wilt thou reproach a man?
20.1704: He is thy brother. Thou seest under his brow
20.1705: A wisp in his eye, but art not willing by one whit
20.1706: To think of the beam which thou hast in thine own,
20.1707: A hard tree and heavy. Into thy heart let it
20.1708: First fall: how to remove it. Then wilt thy light shine forth,
20.1709: Thine eyen will be opened. Thus mayest thou later
20.1710: Make better the sight of thy sweet friend,
20.1711: Heal it, lo, in his head. Let each in his heart,
20.1712: Each man in this mid-world, think more of his own misdeeds
20.1713: Than he thinketh of the sins of another,
20.1714: The faults of a friend — and hath himself done far worse,
20.1716: Far greater wrongs. If to himself he would do good,
20.1717: Then shall he first make himself free of all sin,
20.1718: Loose of all loathsome deeds. Later may he then with his teachings
20.1719: Be a help to the people, when he knoweth himself to be pure
20.1720: And safe from sin. Nor shalt thou strew
20.1721: Thy sea-pearls down before swine, nor scatter thy jewels,
20.1722: Nor thy neckband holy; for they will trample it now in the mire,
20.1723: Besmirch it in sand. For they know nothing, the swine, of cleanness,
20.1724: Of sea-pearls so fair. Here there are many such folk
20.1725: Who will not hear thy holy word
20.1726: Nor follow God’s teachings, and know of no good.
20.1727: They would far liefer have low, useless things,
20.1728: Have empty words, than the work and the will
20.1729: Of your Wielder and God. They are not worthy,
20.1730: That they hear your holy word. For in their hearts they do not think,
20.1731: Do not want to learn it nor do it. Say ye naught of your words unto them,
20.1732: Lest ye squander God’s speech and many a spell.
20.1733: Lose ye not your word ’mid the land-folk, who do not want to believe it,
20.1734: The great and true word. Eke shall ye guard against
20.1735: The wiles of this folk, as ye wander, ye earls, through the land,
20.1736: Lest the teachers of lies lead you astray
20.1737: With words and with works. They come wearing such garbs,
20.1738: To you wearing fairer jewels: but their hearts are wily.
20.1740: They speak wise words, but their works are worth naught,
20.1741: The thoughts of these thanes. For ye know that thorns never grow
20.1742: On the wineberry nor on that which is worthy,
20.1743: On the fairer fruits. Nor does a man gather figs
20.1744: From the hawthorn tree. Keep ye this truth in your hearts:
20.1745: That the bad tree which standeth there in the earth
20.1746: Never giveth forth good fruit; and that God hath not shaped it,
20.1747: That the good tree of the bairns of men bear bitter fruit;
20.1748: But from every tree whatsoever there cometh forth only
20.1749: Such fruit to this world as was born from the root,
20.1750: Either bright fruit or bitter. That is the feeling in the breasts,
20.1751: In the hearts of so many of the kinfolk of man,
20.1752: Wherever each one of the earls showeth himself all openly,
20.1753: Maketh known with his mouth of what mind he is,
20.1754: The thoughts in his heart; nor may he hide them ever;
20.1755: But from an evil man cometh unwise counsel,
20.1756: Words bitter and blameworthy, such as he hath in his breast,
20.1757: Harboring them ’round his heart: here his thoughts become known,
20.1758: His will along with his words; and his works follow, too.
20.1759: There cometh from a good man an answer, gracious and clear,
20.1760: Wise in his wit, that he ever speaketh with words —
20.1761: The man with his mouth; such words as he hath in his mind,
20.1762: Hoarded round his heart. Thence cometh the Holy Gospel,
20.1763: That most Winsome Word, and his works shall thrive
20.1764: For the good of men for many a thane,
20.1765: As indeed is his will, even as the Wielder
20.1766: Did grant unto good men, God Almighty
20.1767: The High Liege of Heaven, since without His will
20.1768: Neither with words nor with works can they do one whit
20.1769: Of good in this world-garden here. Therefore all the bairns of mankind should most gladly
20.1770: Believe in the strength and the might of the One Single Lord.

21.1771: Here I must tell you, too that pathways twain
21.1772: Lie in this light. Thereon the land-bairns
21.1773: Must travel, the children of earth. One of the twain
21.1774: Is a street broad and wide: much folk wandereth on it,
21.1775: Of mankind so many; for their mind doth drive them —
21.1776: The world-lust, these war-men. On the worse side
21.1777: It doth lead them, the landsmen where they are lost,
21.1778: The heroes in hell fire; there it is swarthy and hot,
21.1779: horrible within. Easily may the children of earth
21.1780: Travel thereto. Still in the end it availeth them not.
21.1781: Then lieth again another and narrower path,
21.1782: A way in this world, on which do wander
21.1783: But few of the folk. The bairns of men follow it
21.1784: Ungladly, though it goeth on to God’s kingdom,
21.1785: Leadeth all aethlings into eternal life.
21.1786: But take ye the narrow one; though it be never so easy
21.1787: For world-folk to wander on, it availeth well
21.1788: Whosoever trespasseth it; he hath bounteous pay,
21.1789: Long-lasting reward and life never ending,
21.1790: The dearest of doing. And do ye so pray
21.1791: To your Lord, the Wielder, that this be the way
21.1792: Ye follow forthwith, and going further along this path
21.1793: Into God’s realm. For He is ready ever
21.1794: To give in return, if a man biddeth rightly,
21.1795: If the folk-bairns do ask him. Seek ye your Father,
21.1796: Which is in the kingdom unending. There can ye find Him
21.1797: For your welfare eternal. Make ye known your travels
21.1798: At your Master’s door; for you they may open,
21.1799: Heaven’s portals unlock, so that to the holy light,
21.1800: To God’s realm itself, now ye may go,
21.1801: Seeing life everlasting. Lo, I shall say unto you,
21.1802: Tell you one token more truly for the earth-folk all,
21.1803: That every man whosoever keepeth My teachings
21.1804: Held in his heart, who thinketh of them in his mind,
21.1805: And worketh them in this world — he worketh indeed
21.1806: Like a wise man having great wit,
21.1807: A head that is clearer. And he chooseth his homestead
21.1808: On right fast ground, and upon a rock
21.1809: He worketh the walls, where neither the wind
21.1810: Nor the wave nor the water’s stream can harm it a whit,
21.1811: But it standeth there strong ’gainst all storms
21.1812: High on the rock, since right firmly it was
21.1813: Set on the stone. From beneath, the spot holds it steady,
21.1814: True and straight ’gainst the wind, that it cannot topple.
21.1815: Thus doeth each man, who willeth not
21.1816: To hear these, my teachings, or to carry them out:
21.1817: He acteth indeed like the unwise earl,
21.1818: Like the witless world-man, who on the water’s shore,
21.1819: On the sand itself, would set up his great halled house,
21.1820: Where the western wind and the waves of the stream,
21.1821: The tides of the sea do tear it, sand and grit cannot
21.1823: Hold it up ’gainst the flood, since it stood not fast,
21.1824: Firmly timbered in earth. So shall the work of each earl
21.1825: Strive for this, each aethling who followeth My Word,
21.1826: Holdeth My holy commandments.” In their hearts they began,
21.1827: The many children of men, to wonder: they heard the Almighty God’s
21.1828: Love-filled lessons. In this land they were truly not wont
21.1829: To hear such things being said ever before,
21.1830: Either of words or of works. But wise men understood,
21.1831: That He so taught unto them words of great truth,
21.1832: The Liege of the Land-folk, since He, lo, had power
21.1833: Unlike unto others, who in earlier days
21.1834: Were chosen to teach from the children of men
21.1835: From the clans themselves. Never had of Christ’s words
21.1836: The like been heard ’mid the land-folk when He set down His law

22.1838: Not only should they say and spread His word,
22.1839: How one should reach the realms of Heaven,
22.1840: The Farspreading Fiefdom; but first He did lend
22.1841: Unto them the power to heal the halt and the blind,
22.1842: The ills of the world-folk, their manifold weakness
22.1843: And terrible plagues; and He bade them, too,
22.1844: Never to garner money from any man
22.1845: Or to take treasured pay. To them He did tell this:
22.1846: “Keep ye well in mind, how this wit and this wisdom were come unto you,
22.1847: And the Father of all Folk hath lent you the force. Ye need not buy it
22.1848: With goods nor pay for it with gold. Therefore be ye gracious unto men;
22.1849: Mild in your hearts and ready to help,
22.1851: Enduring deeds. Deal ye right heavily still with their wrongs,
22.1852: With their swarthy sins. Let not silver nor gold
22.1853: Be of such worth unto you, that ye would e’er own them,
22.1854: Fair glimmering gold-pieces; for they will give you no joy,
22.1855: Be useless to you. Ye shall own no more garments,
22.1856: My earls, no more weeds, than those which ye wear,
22.1857: Ye good men, to garb you, when ye do go forth
22.1858: Among the many. Ye shall not think of your meat,
22.1859: Not long of your body’s food; for the folk shall feed
22.1860: Them that are teaching. That shall be of use,
22.1861: Which ye say to the folk — of right fair reward.
22.1862: Worthy is the workman, that he be fed well,
22.1863: The man given meat, who shall care for so many,
22.1864: The souls of the folk, making firm the way
22.1865: For the ghosts to God’s meadow. That is a greater thing,
22.1866: That a man should make ready for the souls of the many,
22.1867: Should keep them all for the kingdom of Heaven,
22.1868: Than that he careth for the bodies of folk
22.1869: With meat, for the children of men. Therefore should mankind
22.1870: Keep fondly and sweetly those who show them
22.1871: The way to Heaven’s kingdom and hold the harm-doer,
22.1872: The Fiend far from them; who give them blame for their faults,
22.1873: For their sins dire and swarthy. Now I shall send you
22.1874: Throughout the landscape, like a lamb among wolves.
22.1875: So shall ye fare ’mid the foe, amid world-folk many,
22.1876: Amid unlike men. Keep ye your minds toward them
22.1877: So clear and clever as the bright-colored worm,
22.1878: The slyly wise serpent, when it doth suspect
22.1879: A deadly foe. Then men of the folk
22.1880: Cannot lead you astray. Ye shall take care
22.1881: Lest men turn away the thoughts of your mind
22.1882: And destroy your will. Be ye wary of them,
22.1883: Of their furtive deeds again like the dove;
22.1885: Having toward all folk a simple heart,
22.1886: Meekness of mind, so that no man can be cheated,
22.1887: Be ever deceived by your deeds,
22.1888: Led astray by your sins. Now shall ye fare
22.1889: On your way with these tidings: much toil shall ye bear
22.1890: Amid the people and oppression together,
22.1891: Much and varied, if in My name
22.1892: Ye do teach the land-folk. Ye shall yet receive much of evil
22.1893: From the people of world and still worse pain
22.1894: For this, My right word; before the kingdoms of World
22.1895: Shall ye oft stand bound and suffer both
22.1896: Mockery and scornful speech: but let not your spirits feel doubt,
22.1897: Nor your souls ever err; nor need ye ever
22.1898: Harbor care in your heart — when they call ye forth from the crowd,
22.1899: Bid you go with them to the guest hall —
22.1900: What ye will say unto them with your good words,
22.1901: How ye will speak to them wisely; for success will come unto you,
22.1902: Help come from Heaven, and the Holy Ghost will speak
22.1903: Mightily our of your mouth. Therefore dread ye not the hatred of men,
22.1904: Fear not their fiendishness. For though they have power
22.1905: Over your life, may rob your body of breath,
22.1906: Slay you with swords — yet not a whit of your soul
22.1907: Can they e’er destroy. Dread ye All-Wielding God,
22.1908: Fear ye your Father. For Him gladly
22.1909: So ye His commandment, for He hath might and power
22.1910: Over both, o’er the life of a man, o’er his body as well,
22.1911: Yea, even o’er the soul itself. If for the sake of these teachings
22.1912: Ye lose your life on the way, then in the light of God
22.1913: Ye shall find it again, for the Father,
22.1914: The Holy Lord God, hath kept it in the kingdom of Heaven.

23.1915: Not all will reach Heaven who here hail me Protector,
23.1916: Their Master and Lord. There are many of them
23.1917: Who willingly kneel to the Liege every day,
23.1918: Calling on Him for help, but have other thoughts in their hearts,
23.1919: Working dastardly deeds; they win no gain from their words.
23.1920: But those may hasten toward Heaven’s light,
23.1921: Go on to the kingdom of God, who gladly here
23.1922: Accomplish the work of the Wielder, and His will as well.
23.1923: They need not call unto Him, their Master, with words so many,
23.1924: Hailing Him for help, since All-Holy God,
23.1925: Knoweth of every man the thoughts in his mind,
23.1926: His word and his will, and payeth him right for his work.
23.1927: As ye fare on your way, let this be your worry
23.1928: And your task as well: to fulfill my tidings,
23.1929: As ye fare on your path, far o’er the landscape
23.1930: Through the wideness of world, where your ways will lead you,
23.1931: The broad street to the borough: straightway seek ye the best
23.1932: Men among the multitude, and make ye known unto them
23.1933: With words of truth what lieth in your minds. If they be worthy
23.1934: Of this: that they gladly give help to your good works
23.1935: With pureness of heart, then may ye dwell in the house
23.1936: With them as ye will, rewarding them well:
23.1937: Pay them with goodness — give them to God Himself
23.1938: With your words, foretelling the Wielder’s sure peace,
23.1939: The holy help of the King of Heaven.
23.1940: Yet if they cannot become blessed
23.1941: By their own deeds, cannot do your works,
23.1942: Carry out your message: then leave ye these men,
23.1943: Fare forth from this folk; and your peace will fare forth with you
23.1944: Once more on the very same way; and leave ye them in their wickedness,
23.1945: In their works of sin, and seek for yourselves another way,
23.1946: A much larger gathering; nor leave ye of dust one single grain
23.1947: To follow your feet from there, where one hath received you unfairly;
23.1948: But shake ye that dust from your shoes, so that it becometh a shame,
23.1949: A witness there to the world-folk, that their work is worth naught.
23.1950: Then I tell unto you and in truth: that when this world doth come to its end
23.1951: And that Famous Day fareth over all mankind,
23.1952: That the city of Sodom, which for its sins
23.1953: Was felled to its fundament by the force of the flame,
23.1954: The power of fire — it will have more peace,
23.1955: A milder protector than shall have those men
23.1956: Who cast you aside, were unwilling to accomplish your word.
23.1957: Whoever receiveth you with a pious soul
23.1958: And mildness of mind, he hath done so for Me,
23.1959: Hath accomplished My will, accepted All-Wielding God,
23.1960: Your Mighty Father, Master of Mankind,
23.1961: The Rich Giver of Truth, who knoweth all right.
23.1962: The Wielder Himself doth know and reward the work
23.1963: Of each earthling, if to any man ever
23.1964: He doeth some good for the love of God:
23.1966: That the needy man is healed of his thirst
23.1967: From the cold well-spring. The word will come true.
23.1968: It will never fail, that he find fair
23.1969: Reward in the eyes of God, receive recompense
23.1970: Of many a sort for that which he doeth in God’s sweet love.
23.1971: But whosoever of the bairns of men doth deny Me here,
23.1972: Of the warriors before the host, In Heaven I shall likewise do unto him
23.1973: Far above before the All-Wielding Father and before the strength of His angels,
23.1974: Before their multitude. Whosoever of the children of men
23.1975: Doth not with his words deny Me here in this world,
23.1976: But before the kinship of men confesseth he is My disciple,
23.1977: Him will I vouch for before God’s very eyen,
23.1978: Before the Father of All, there where so many folk
23.1979: Wend their way to the All-Wielder
23.1980: To justify their deeds before the Great Judge. There will I be
23.1981: As is meet, a mild Protector for whosoever hearkeneth unto Me,
23.1982: Who hath heard My word, and accomplished the work,
23.1983: Which I have commanded of you up here on the mountain.”
23.1984: So the Son of the Wielder verily taught the world-folk
23.1986: How they should work God’s love. Then He sent them away,
23.1987: The men of His host, each to his own home.
23.1989: They had heard the Word, the Heaven King’s holy Spell.
23.1990: Whosoever in this world was wiser in word and in deed,
23.1991: Many of mankind over the face of this mid-world,
23.1992: Smarter in speech — he heard the Spell
23.1993: Which the Richest of Men spake on the mountain.

24.1994: It was three nights later, that the Lord of the Land-folk
24.1995: Went into Galilee-land there to a wedding feast:
24.1996: God’s Bairn had been bidden. A bride would be given,
24.1997: A most lovely maid. Mary was there,
24.1999: The Mighty One’s mother. The Lord of the Many,
24.2000: God’s Own Bairn, did go with His followers
24.2001: To the high house, where the hordes were drinking,
24.2002: The Jews in the guest-hall. He did go to the feast,
24.2003: Made known to the guests, that He had God’s power,
24.2004: Help from the Heaven-Father and the Holy Ghost
24.2005: The All-Wielder’s wisdom. The warriors were blithe,
24.2006: The land-folk together loud in their joy,
24.2007: Glad-hearted the guests. The grooms went about
24.2008: Pouring from pitchers; the pure wine they
24.2009: carried in jugs and in cups. The crowd’s tumult
24.2010: Was gay in the great hall, when the folk began, one ’mid the other,
24.2011: To feel their best blitheness; there on the benches
24.2012: In rapture were they, when the wine ran out,
24.2013: The fruit drink of the folk — for naught was there left,
24.2014: No drop in the house, which to the hordes
24.2015: The butlers might bear, when all of the vessels
24.2016: Were empty of mead. ’Twas not long after that
24.2017: That the fairest of ladies did find this out,
24.2018: The mother of Christ. She went to speak to her Kin,
24.2019: To her Son Himself; she said with her words
24.2020: That the host of the house had no more of wine,
24.2022: Hight the Holy Christ, that He find some help
24.2023: For the joy of the many. There again God’s Mighty Bairn
24.2024: Had ready His word: with His mother He spake:
24.2025: “What doth the mead of these men,” quoth He, “mean to Me,
24.2026: The wine of this world-folk? Why, O goodwife, speaketh thou
24.2027: So much, admonishing Me before these many?
24.2028: My time is not come yet!” Yet she still trusted well
24.2029: Deep in her heart, the Holy Maid,
24.2030: That the Wielder’s Bairn — even after these words —
24.2031: Would help indeed, the Best of All Healers.
24.2032: Then the sweetest of ladies hight all the servants,
24.2033: The butlers and cup-bearers who had here been serving,
24.2034: That they omit not a whit either of words or of works
24.2035: Of that which the Holy Christ would hight them do
24.2036: For the people there. The pots all stood empty,
24.2037: Stone vessels six. Quite softly He bade them —
24.2038: God’s Mighty Bairn — so that many a man
24.2039: Was verily all unaware what He said with His words.
24.2040: He hight that the butlers should fill the barrels,
24.2041: The cup-bearers there, with clearest water; with His fingers He blessed it,
24.2043: With His hands turned it to wine; and He hight the vessels be filled,
24.2044: The pitchers be poured from; and He spake to the servants,
24.2045: Hight that they give with their hands to the foremost guest
24.2046: Who was here at the feast: for him pour a fulsome jug,
24.2048: Who next to the host was the noblest there. When he now drank the wine,
24.2049: He was loathe to keep still; but before the many he spake
24.2050: To the bridegroom then; quoth that the best mead should have been brought,
24.2051: The finest of the fruit-wines given first to the earls
24.2052: At once at the wedding. “So is a man’s wit
24.2053: Awakened by the wine, and he waxeth blithe,
24.2054: Maketh merry with drink. Then mayest thou bring on
24.2055: The worser wines. That is the way of this folk.
24.2056: But most strangely indeed hast thou marked thy hostship
24.2057: Among the multitude here; thou hast hight thy serving men,
24.2058: Thy butlers and cup-bearers bring out at the banquet
24.2059: Of all the wines the very worst forsooth,
24.2060: Serving that first at the feast. Now that thy guests are filled,
24.2061: The dear banqueteers are already most drunk,
24.2062: The folk feeling merry, thou hightest brought forth
24.2063: The loveliest of all wines which I ever saw lifted
24.2064: Anywhere in this earth-light. Thou should’st have given that earlier,
24.2065: Have served us sooner. Such thanks would’st thou then
24.2066: Have garnered from all the good men.” Many a thane grew
24.2067: Aware after these words — as soon as they had drunk of the wine —
24.2068: That here in the house the Holy Christ
24.2069: Had revealed a token. They trusted thereafter
24.2070: The more in His rule: that He had God’s might
24.2071: To wield in this world. So it came widely known
24.2072: Over Galilee-land to the Jewish folk
24.2073: That the Son of the Lord had Himself turned
24.2074: The water to wine. That was of His wonders
24.2075: The first which He showed as a sign to the Jewish folk,
24.2076: As a token in Galilee-land. Nor may anyone tell
24.2077: Nor say forsooth, what hath happed since then
24.2078: In the way of wonders among the folk; for All-Wielding Christ
24.2079: Told His teachings unto the people of Jews
24.2080: The livelong day in the name of Lord God,
24.2081: Promised the kingdom of Heaven; with His words protected them, too,
24.2082: From the press of hell. Hight that they should seek the wardship of God
24.2083: And eternal life. There is the light of the souls,
24.2084: The Lord’s life ever joyous, the glow of the day,
24.2085: The good glory of God. There many guests
24.2086: Dwell to His will, who here have thought well
24.2087: How best they should keep it, the Heaven-King’s commandment

25.2088: With His followers He went forth from the feast,
25.2089: Christ to Capernaum, the Richest of Kings,
25.2090: To that famous town. Much folk was assembled,
25.2091: Was gathered around Him, men of good stock —
25.2092: A blessed following it was. They wanted to hear His word,
25.2093: Which was sweet and holy. There came toward Him a centurion;
25.2094: A good man, he approached Him and bade Him most earnestly,
25.2095: That the Holy One help him. Quoth that at home
25.2096: He had long had a man lame and sickly,
25.2097: In his family a feeble one, “For I tell Thee no one
25.2098: Can heal him with hands. Now I have need of Thy help,
25.2099: Good Lord, my Liege.” Then spake the Peace-Bairn of God
25.2100: And straightway Himself did say unto him,
25.2101: Quoth that He would come and save his young kin
25.2102: From his direst need. Then came nearer
25.2103: The man from the multitude to speak to the Mighty Christ,
25.2104: To exchange words with Him. “I am not worth,” quoth he,
25.2105: “Good Lord, my Liege, that Thou would’st come to my house »
25.2106: Would’st seek out my dwelling, for I am a sinful man
25.2107: With my words and my works. I believe Thou wieldest might,
25.2108: Canst work his healing here in this place,
25.2109: My Wielder and Lord; if Thou speakest Thy word,
25.2110: He is cured of his sickness; clean and bright shining
25.2111: Doth his body become, if Thou wilt but give him Thy help.
25.2112: I am a man holding office and have wealth enough,
25.2113: Have gained goodly things; though I stand governed
25.2114: By an aethling king, yet have I of earls quite a following,
25.2115: Loyal warriors in arms, who listen alone unto me,
25.2116: Who leave of word or of work not a whit undone
25.2117: Of that which I bid them do here in the land;
25.2118: But they fare forth and finish it, do return to their master,
25.2119: Being obedient to me, their lord. Though I do own broad
25.2120: Spreading goods in my house, have servants enough,
25.2121: War-minded men, still may I not dare
25.2122: To bid Thee, God’s Bairn so Holy, to enter my building,
25.2123: To seek our my dwelling, since I am so sinful,
25.2124: So mindful, my Lord, of my misdeeds.” Then spake once more All-Wielding Christ,
25.2125: The Finest of Men, to His followers; quoth that never had He found
25.2126: Anywhere ’mongst the Jews, among the offspring of Israel,
25.2127: The like of this man in the landscape; one who believed
25.2129: More deeply in God, more purely in Heaven — “Now may
25.2130: Ye hear, ye too, what I say at this time with words of truth:
25.2131: That much foreign folk from the East and the West,
25.2132: Many clans of mankind shall come together,
25.2133: God’s holy folk in the Heavenly Kingdom:
25.2134: They will rest right well in the lap of Abraham,
25.2135: Of Isaac himself and of Jacob, good men all, and enjoy
25.2137: Goods and good will and a winsome life
25.2138: And the great light with God. But lo, many Jews,
25.2139: The sons of this realm will then be robbed,
25.2140: Be sundered from such splendor, and shall have to lie
25.2141: In the darkest dales in the farthest distance of all.
25.2142: There one can hear the heroes lamenting
25.2143: And gnashing their teeth in terror and pain.
25.2144: There is furious rage and a hungry fire
25.2145: And the hard pangs of hell, hot and thirsty,
25.2146: Swarthy might, never ending, as payment for sin,
25.2147: For wretched wrong-doing, to all who have not willed to rid
25.2148: Themselves of their wrongs before they relinquish the light,
25.2149: Wend their way from this world. Now if ’tis thy will,
25.2150: Thou mayest go home. In thy house thou wilt find hale
25.2151: And sound the child-young man: he will be joyous of mind.
25.2152: The bairn hath been healed; even so as thou badest Me,
25.2153: All hath been done, even as thou hast belief
25.2154: Firm fixed in thy heart.” Then to the Heaven-King,
25.2155: To the All-Wielding Child of God the centurion gave thanks
25.2156: Before all the folk for this, that He had helped him thus in his anguish.
25.2157: It ws all worked, even as he had wished it
25.2158: And most blessed indeed: he did go on his way,
25.2159: Went as he willed, where he had ownership,
25.2160: A house and a home. There he found hale his bairn,
25.2161: The child-young man. Christ’s word was accomplished, for He had
25.2163: The might to show forth tokens, so that no man could tell,
25.2164: Over he earth could reckon, that He through His own power,
25.2165: Through His strength had made miracles on this mid-world here,
25.2166: Accomplished such marvels. For all things stand in His might,

26.2167: Then the Holy Christ bethought Him
26.2168: To fare on farther. For the bairns of the folk
26.2169: The Master of All, the Almighty, the Good,
26.2170: Every day did accomplish deeds dear and good;
26.2171: With words taught God’s will to the people, had always
26.2172: Followers aplenty about Him, blessed folk of God,
26.2173: A mighty crowd of men, come from many peoples,
26.2174: A holy army and host. He was good in His help,
26.2175: Mild to the men. Then He came with the many:
26.2176: Now the Bairn of God with a noisy crowd came to Nain,
26.2177: The Savior to the high-standing city. There His name
26.2178: Would become famed among men. There mightily
26.2179: The Saving Christ walked along until He came closer,
26.2180: The Best of All Healers. They saw folk bringing a body —
26.2181: They came carrying a corpse without life.
26.2182: On a bier they bore it through the gates of the bastion,
26.2183: A child-young man. The mother did follow,
26.2184: Her heart being heavy; herself did she beat with her hands,
26.2185: Bewailed and lamented the death of her bairn —
26.2186: Unhappy woman was she — it was her only child.
26.2187: She was a widow, in this world had no joy
26.2188: Except this one son, whom Weird had now taken.
26.2189: She had lost all things, has lost joy and happiness;
26.2190: And now fate, ill-famed, had robbed her of him. Many people did follow,
26.2191: A crowd of the burghers, as they carried the bier,
26.2192: The young man to his grave. There the Son of God,
26.2193: The Mighty grew mild; and to the mother He spake;
26.2194: Hight the widow leave off with her weeping,
26.2195: Nor care for her child; “Thou shalt see here the strength,
26.2196: The work of the Wielder: thy will shall be granted thee,
26.2197: Comfort in front of the folk: from now on thy spirit
26.2198: May not bemoan thy bairn.” Then he went to the bier,
26.2199: He Himself did touch it, the Son of the Lord,
26.2200: With His holy hands and to the hero He spake,
26.2201: Hight this child, all too young, to stand up, hight him
26.2202: Arise from his rest. Right away the youth
26.2203: Did sit up, the bairn on the bier; and into his breast came
26.2204: His soul through the strength of God; and he spake unto them,
26.2205: The man to his kith. Christ commended him then to his mother,
26.2206: The Holy One into her hands. Her heart was consoled.
26.2207: Happy the woman, since to her so much grace had happed.
26.2208: She fell to Christ’s feet and praised Him, the Folk-Lord,
26.2209: Master, before all the multitude, since He had here helped
26.2210: Her loved one to live ’gainst the working of Weird. Well she knew that He was
26.2211: The Mighty Lord, the Holy, who governed the Heaven, who could help so many
26.2212: Of earthlings all. then many began to attend
26.2213: The wonder, which had come to pass there ’mid the folk: quoth that the Wielder Himself,
26.2214: The Mighty, had come to teach them, the many, that He had sent
26.2215: A prophet, most wondrous, to the kingdom of world; one who did His will.
26.2216: Then truly many an earl was taken by terror,
26.2217: The folk full of fear, for they saw him again
26.2218: Alive and seeing the light of day; him whom death had but lately taken,
26.2219: Stretched low on his sick-bed. Again he was sound,
26.2220: The young kin quickened; and soon this did spread
26.2221: To the heirs of all Israel. And when evening came,
26.2222: There were gathered about many sick men together,
26.2223: The halt and the lame of hand — whosoever was here
26.2224: And lived ’mid the land-folk; they were led to the place,
26.2225: Were come to the Christ, who through His strength and His craft
26.2226: Helped them and healed them and sent them hale from the place
26.2227: To wend where they willed. Therefore should one praise His words,
26.2229: The Mighty Minder of all mankind,

27.2232: From all the foreign folk for the glory of Christ,
27.2233: For His mighty guardianship. There onto a sea God’s Son
27.2234: Wished to go with His vassals — ’twas on Galilee’s borders —
27.2235: The Wielder onto a wave-tide. There He willed that the other folk
27.2236: Go wandering ahead, and He went with a few
27.2237: Into a small ship, the Savior Christ,
27.2238: Way-weary, to sleep. The weather-wise men
27.2239: Raised high the sail, let the wind drive the sloop
27.2240: Over the sea-tide, until they did come to the center,
27.2241: The Wielder there with His vassals. There began the force of the weather;
27.2242: The storm-wind rose, the waves waxed high,
27.2243: Swarthy clouds swung down in between: the sea was astir,
27.2244: Wind battled water; the men were worried.
27.2245: The sea was so angry, not a man expected
27.2246: To live any longer. The Land-Warden they then
27.2247: Awakened with their words. They told unto Him of the weather’s strength;
27.2248: They bade saving Christ to be gracious and kind, to help
27.2250: Martyred here in the sea.” Then the Good Son of God
27.2251: Arose, Himself from His sleep. To His disciples He spake,
27.2252: Bade them not to dread the weather’s battle one bit.
27.2253: “Why are ye so fearful?” quoth He. “Are your hearts not yet firm,
27.2254: Your belief yet so little. ’Twill not be long now
27.2255: Then the stream shall become stiller
27.2256: And the weather all winsome.” Then He spake to the wind,
27.2257: And to the sea itself. And He said unto them
27.2258: Both, that they should grow still. And they hearkened to His bidding,
27.2259: To the Wielder’s word. The weather grew calm,
27.2260: The flood became fair. There the folk around Him,
27.2261: The world-men did wonder, and with their words some did speak
27.2262: What a Mighty One this Man was indeed,
27.2263: That the wind and the wave would heed His word,
27.2264: Both doing His bidding. The Bairn of God
27.2265: Had there saved them from need. The sloop sailed on farther,
27.2266: The high-horned ship. The heroes did come,
27.2267: The leaders, to land. They all lauded God
27.2268: And praised His great power. Then many people did come
27.2269: To the Son of God. He received them most gladly,
27.2270: Whosoever sought help with a clear, pure heart.
27.2271: He did teach them to believe, and lo, their bodies
27.2272: He healed with His hands; though a man were hard
27.2273: And piteously pressed with plagues through Satan’s
27.2274: Wiley followers, though the force of the Fiend
27.2275: Held him fast in his hands, had destroyed his heart
27.2276: And his wit as well, that he went about
27.2277: Mad among mankind; yet Mighty Christ always,
27.2278: The Healer, gave him back his life, if he were come to His hands,
27.2279: Drove the devils hence with the power of God,
27.2280: With words of truth, and returned him his wit,
27.2281: Let him be healed against the haters
27.2282: Gave him peace ’gainst the foe; and they went forth,
27.2283: Each into his own land, whichever he loved the most.

28.2284: So our Dear Lord’s Son did on each day
28.2285: God’s work with His followers. But the Jews had no faith,
28.2286: Believed not at all in the largeness of His strength:
28.2287: That He was the All-Wielder over all things,
28.2288: Of lands and of people. Their reward is still lasting:
28.2289: ’Tis farflung exile, since they acted so evilly
28.2290: ’Gainst the Lord’s Son Himself. With His retainers He soon went
28.2291: Again into Galilee-land; He did go with His friends,
28.2292: God’s own Bairn, to where He was born,
28.2293: Where as a young child He had waxed with His kin,
28.2294: He, the Healer All Holy. Around Him a host,
28.2295: A great crowd did throng. There was many a thane
28.2296: So blessed ’mid the crowd. There some carried a sick man,
28.2297: Certain earls in their arms. Before Christ’s eyen they would
28.2298: Bring him, before God’s Bairn. Betterment he needed,
28.2299: Needed Heaven’s Wielder to heal him indeed,
28.2300: The Minder of Men. For many a day
28.2301: He had been lamed of limb. Little could he
28.2302: Govern his body at all. There were such great numbers
28.2303: That they could not bring him before God’s Bairn,
28.2304: Could not press through the people to tell Him the plight
28.2305: Of this poor, sick man. There He hied Himself within,
28.2306: To the hall, All Healing Christ — a great crowd was around Him,
28.2307: A multitude of mankind. There the men who had so long
28.2308: Carried with them the weak-limbed cripple
28.2309: Began to speak how they might bear him on the bed before God’s Bairn,
28.2310: Through the world-folk within, so that Wielding Christ
28.2311: Would see him Himself. So his servants went,
28.2312: With their hands they did lift him, climbed high on the house,
28.2313: Slit open the hall from the roof above, and with ropes
28.2314: Let him down in the building where the Rich Lord was,
28.2315: The Strongest of Kings. When He saw him coming
28.2316: Through the house’s rafters, right well He knew from the hearts,
28.2317: From the minds of these men, that mighty indeed
28.2318: Was their faith in Him. And so spake He before all the folk,
28.2319: Quoth that He would absolve the sick man from sin.
28.2320: In answer to this the people did speak,
28.2321: Rage-hardened Jews, quoth how could it be so:
28.2323: God alone can forgive works of crime,
28.2324: The world’s All-Wielder. His word He had ready,
28.2325: God’s Mighty Bairn. “I make manifest,” quoth He, “in this man
28.2326: Who lieth so ill here in this large hall —
28.2327: Most grievously pained — that I have the power
28.2328: To forgive the sins and to heal the sick man
28.2329: Without ever touching My hand to him.”
28.2330: Then our Mighty Lord admonished the man
28.2331: Who lay there lame to rise there before the land-folk,
28.2332: To stand up hale. And He hight him take on his shoulders,
28.2333: On his back the bedding; and he did our Lord’s bidding,
28.2334: Straightway befoe the assemblage, and went away sound,
28.2335: Hale from the house. Then many a heathen,
28.2336: Many a world-man did wonder, quoth that the Wielder Himself,
28.2337: Surely God the Almighty had given unto Him
28.2338: More splendid might that unto any man’s son,
28.2339: The skill and the strength; still they would not acknowledge,
28.2340: That folk of the Jews, that He was God,
28.2341: Nor believed they His lesson, but struggled evilly with Him,
28.2342: Fought against His word. For this they have won weary care,
28.2343: Reaped a grievous return; and right long will that last
28.2344: For those who hear not the Heaven-King’s teachings,
28.2345: The lesson of Christ, which is proclaimed over all,
28.2346: Wide and far in the world; and He let them all see His work,
28.2347: Each day and every look on His deeds,
28.2348: Hear His holy word, which He spake for the help
28.2349: Of the bairns of mankind. And so many and mighty
28.2350: A token He showed, that they trusted Him better,
28.2351: Believed in His word. So many a body
28.2352: He unbound from ills baleful and granted them betterment,
28.2353: Gave life to those destined to die, even if
28.2354: The hero was on hell’s path already. The Healer himself did so —
28.2355: Christ through His might and His power quickened even the dead after death,
28.2356: Let them further enjoy the winsomeness here in the world.

29.2357: So healed He the halt and the lame of hand,
29.2358: Made better the blind, let them see the bright light,
29.2359: See Heaven’s splendor; absolved them from sin,
29.2360: The world-men from wickedness. But the Jews grew no better,
29.2361: This loathsome land-folk, in their belief
29.2362: In the Holy Christ; but they were hardened of heart,
29.2363: Strove very strongly against Him, wanted not to perceive
29.2364: They were well ensnared by the devil’s will,
29.2365: This folk through its faith; for He was not idle,
29.2366: The Son of the Lord; but with His words He said unto them
29.2367: How they could gain the kingdom of Heaven;
29.2368: And through all the land He did teach; a multitude He did turn
29.2369: Unto Him with His words, so that many a world-man,
29.2370: A great crowd of folk, did follow Him. And in figures
29.2371: God’s Bairn spake unto them things which in their breast they could not perceive
29.2372: Nor grasp in their hearts, till the Holy Christ
29.2373: With open words willed to speak
29.2374: To all people through His power and strength,
29.2375: And make clear what He meant. A mighty crowd,
29.2376: A very large one, thronged ’round Him. They longed greatly
29.2377: To hear the true word of the King of Heaven.
29.2378: On the shores of the sea by the water He stood.
29.2379: Because of the great crowd, He cared not to proclaim
29.2380: His lesson to His thanes there on the land;
29.2381: But the Good One did go — and His disciples with Him all gladly —
29.2382: The Peace-Bairn of God did go to a water
29.2383: Unto a ship, hight that it shove off
29.2384: Further from the land so that the folk,
29.2385: The crowd, could not throng quite so close. Many a thane,
29.2386: Much world-folk stood by the water, where All-Wielding Christ
29.2387: Did reveal His lesson to the land-folk there.
29.2388: “Lo, I may say unto you,” quoth He, “My disciples,
29.2389: How an earl began to sow good grain
29.2390: In the soil with his hands. Some fell on hard stones
29.2391: From above, and the grains had not earth enough
29.2392: In which to grow rightly and send down roots,
29.2393: To sprout and cleave fast. And that corn was lost,
29.2394: That lay on those rocks. Some fell on the land,
29.2395: On excellent soil. This soon began
29.2396: To wax winsomely tall and take root right well;
29.2397: And most merrily it grew. The land was so good,
29.2398: So fruitful its kind. Again, some had fallen
29.2399: On a stiff, hard street, where steps did tread,
29.2400: The hoofbeats of horses and the feet of heroes.
29.2401: There was soil for them and indeed they sprouted,
29.2402: Began to wax on the way, but the walking of men did kill them,
29.2403: The wayfaring of folk; and the flying birds picked them up,
29.2404: So that they were not one whit of use
29.2405: To the owner there, those that did fall on the way.
29.2406: Some fell on that day where there stood so many
29.2407: Thickets of thorn. There was soil there for them,
29.2408: And they came up, they spouted and cleaved; but weeds
29.2410: Came between and kept them from growing. The cover
29.2411: Of forest spread out before them, and they could not grow fruitful,
29.2412: Since the thornbush thronged all around them.”
29.2413: Christ’s disciples did sit and were silent all,
29.2414: The word-wise thanes. For they wondered muchly
29.2415: With what goodly pictures the Bairn of God
29.2416: Would begin to say such a true and wise spell.
29.2417: Then one of he earls began to ask
29.2418: The Beloved Lord, bent low before Him
29.2419: Most humbly indeed. “Why,” quoth he, “Thou hast might
29.2420: Both in Heaven and on earth, Holy Master,
29.2421: Above and beneath. Beest Thou All-Wielder
29.2422: Over the souls of men, and we Thy disciples,
29.2423: Given to Thee with all our hearts, O Lord most Good.
29.2424: If that be Thy will, let us hear Thy good word,
29.2426: That we can proclaim it to all Christian folk.
29.2427: We know indeed that upon Thy words
29.2428: Follow true parables; and a need, most great, is in us,
29.2429: That in this land, here with Thee, we may teach
29.2430: Thy word and Thy work — since from such wisdom it cometh.”

30.2431: Then the Best of All Men spake in answer to them.
30.2432: “I did not mean,” quoth He, “to disguise My deeds
30.2434: In any way, either my words or my works; but ye shall know all,
30.2435: Ye disciples Mine; for unto you hath He granted,
30.2436: The Wielder of Worlds, that ye may well know
30.2437: In your hearts and your minds the mysteries of Heaven.
30.2438: Yet one must give unto others the commandments of God
30.2439: With pictures in words. Now will I tell you
30.2440: Most truly what I mean indeed, so that ye may better
30.2441: Understand My teachings over all the landscape.
30.2442: The seed which I spake of is the Word of Himself,
30.2443: The Holy Scripture of the King of Heaven,
30.2444: As one should spread it o’er the mid-earth here,
30.2445: Wide in this world. World-folk, at heart,
30.2446: Men are most different; some are of such mind,
30.2447: So hard of spirit and evil of heart,
30.2448: That it seemeth not worth their while to act by your words
30.2449: Or to be so willed to accomplish My teachings;
30.2450: But My lessons all are indeed lost unto them,
30.2451: And the commandments of God and the teachings of you, My men,
30.2452: On these evil folk; as I earlier said unto you,
30.2453: That the corn did wither, which could not there
30.2454: Strike root with its sprouts upon the stones.
30.2455: So all will be lost, the speech of the aethling,
30.2456: The message of God — whatsoever one telleth
30.2457: To an evil man; and he chooseth the path,
30.2458: The way on the left, on the worse hand to God’s displeasure,
30.2459: To the foe of the folk and the onslaught of fire
30.2460: And the devil’s joy. From that day on
30.2461: He shall heat the broad flames with the heart in his breast.
30.2462: Nonetheless in this land shall ye spread My lesson,
30.2463: Proclaim it with words, if there be many people,
30.2464: Such earls on this eath. Yet another man still may exist
30.2465: Who is young and clever and hath kindness of heart,
30.2466: Is wise in his speech, understandeth your spell,
30.2467: Pondereth it in his heart and heareth it with his ears
30.2468: Very zealously indeed; and stepping closer,
30.2469: Accepteth in his heart the bidding of God,
30.2470: Learning and carrying it out. If his belief is so good,
30.2471: He will then wonder how he can woo another,
30.2472: A wrong-doing man; so that his mind be filled
30.2473: With a loyalty clear for the King of Heaven.
30.2474: The bidding of God groweth broad in his bosom,
30.2475: The willing belief, even as on the land
30.2476: The grain doeth with its sprouts, when it hath right ground,
30.2477: Good soil to suit it, and the changing of weather —
30.2478: The rain and the sun, so that it hath its right.
30.2479: So doeth the teaching of God in a good-souled man
30.2480: Through the day and night; and the devil stayeth far,
30.2481: The wicked wight; and the word of God
30.2482: Is nearer to him in the nights and the days,
30.2483: So that it causeth him to accomplish both —
30.2484: This lesson is a blessing to the bairns of the land —
30.2485: That which cometh from his mouth, and the man becometh of God.
30.2486: So hath he bought with his heart in this hour of world
30.2487: A piece of Heaven’s kingdom, the greatest possession.
30.2488: Into God’s power he fareth, freed from wrong deeds. Faithfulness
30.2490: Is so good for each man. No treasure of gold
30.2491: Is like unto belief. Henceforth teach ye the lesson
30.2492: Mildly to mankind. These are so varied of mind,
30.2493: The heroes of men; some have hard strife,
30.2494: An evil will and a wavering spirit.
30.2495: They are full of deceptions and deeds of wrong.
30.2496: As one beginneth to think, as he standeth there
30.2497: Among the crowd, and harkeneth with great care
30.2498: To the teachings of God; then he thinketh he would gladly
30.2499: Henceforth carry them out. Then the teachings of God
30.2500: Begin to cleave to his heart, until there come once more
30.2501: Through his hands possessions and proud wealth of others;
30.2502: The loathsome wights lead him astray,
30.2503: And avarice doth seize him again
30.2504: And killeth now his belief: thus was it little use unto him
30.2505: That he ever thought in his heart, if he willed not hold it.
30.2506: Even so is the waxing which began on the wayside,
30.2507: Grew fair on the land; there the footsteps of folk could destroy it again.
30.2508: So mighty sins in the soul of that man
30.2509: Do unto God’s teachings, if he take not heed.
30.2510: Otherwise will they follow him down far to the bottom,
30.2511: To the heart of hell. To the King of Heaven
30.2512: He is of no further help, but the Fiend
30.2513: Will punish him direly with pain. Likewise repair ye forth,
30.2514: Teaching with words in the world; I will know the hearts of the folk,
30.2515: Many differences of mind among mankind,
30.2516: Their varied ways as found in the world,
30.2517: Some have turned their spirits entirely to this
30.2518: And come more to keep their hoard than to work the Heaven King’s
30.2519: Will down on earth. Therefore it waxeth not —
30.2520: God’s holy commandment — though it may cleave there
30.2521: And send forth roots. But riches do crowd it
30.2522: Even as the weeds and the thorn entangle the corn
30.2523: And keep it from waxing: so doeth wealth to a man.
30.2524: He fettereth his heart so that he here pondereth not,
30.2525: The man in his mind, what he needeth most:
30.2526: How he will work that indeed as long as he liveth here in this world,
30.2528: That he have Heaven’s Kingdom, through His High Lord’s grace,
30.2530: As no man knoweth them here in the world. Never
30.2531: May he think so widely, the thane in his mind,
30.2532: Nor may the heart of a man hold it and grasp it
30.2533: To know most verily what good All-Wielding God
30.2534: Hath made ready so that for each man
30.2535: All standeth open — for each who loveth Him well
30.2536: And hath kept his soul so turned ever
30.2537: That he will here enter the light of the Lord.”

31.2538: So He taught them with words; and a wide crowd
31.2539: Stood ’round God’s Bairn and busily hearkened,
31.2540: As He told with His words the way of the world through His parables many.
31.2541: He told how an aethling once sowed an acre
31.2542: Of fine corn with his hands, good grain in the field.
31.2543: He wanted to gain the most winsome of growths,
31.2544: The fairest of fruits. But his foe did follow him
31.2545: With treacherous mind; and with tares he sowed over the top,
31.2546: With the worst of weeds. And they waxed there both,
31.2547: The corn and the tares. So came along
31.2548: The husbandman to the house, and told this to him, to their lord,
31.2549: The thanes to the warden with honest words.
31.2550: “Why, thou didst sow fine grain, master most good,
31.2551: Unmixed on this acre. Yet each earl can see
31.2552: Naught but weeds are waxing. Well, how can that be?”
31.2553: There spake again the aethling, the man to his earls,
31.2554: To his vassals the warder; quoth that he could well understand
31.2555: That an unfriendly man had sown after him,
31.2556: That his foe had slyly sown weeds: “These fruits he begrudgeth me so,
31.2557: That for me he hath stamped out this growth.” Then to him spake again
31.2558: His friends, his followers, quoth that they would fare there,
31.2559: Go with force and would uproot the growth,
31.2560: The weeds with their hands. Then their lord spake once more unto them:
31.2561: “I would not that ye weed them,” quoth he, “since ye cannot avoid it,
31.2562: Cannot prevent in your passing, though yet do it ungladly,
31.2563: That ye kill young sprouts and corn aplenty,
31.2564: Fell them under your feet. Henceforth let both
31.2565: Wax together, till the harvet doth come
31.2566: And the fruits are ripe in the fields,
31.2567: Ready all on the acre. Then to that acre
31.2568: Let us fare; with our hands fetch and gather the fair grain,
31.2569: The pure corn cleanly together, keep it stored in my halls,
31.2570: So that not a speck can be spoiled. Take ye the weeds
31.2572: Bind them in bundles and cast them into bitter fire.
31.2573: Let the hot flames fetch them away,
31.2574: The insatiable blaze.” Then many an earl stood silent,
31.2575: Many a thane in thought, pondering what the Glorious Christ,
31.2576: The Mighty, the Master of Men, could mean
31.2577: And proclaim with His parables, the Most Priceless of Bairns.
31.2578: Most eagerly they bade their Master Good
31.2579: To unlock the lesson, so that the land-folk about
31.2580: Might henceforth hear it, His Holy Word. Their Lord here replied unto them —
31.2581: Famed, Mighty Christ. “This is,” quoth He, “the Son of Man.
31.2582: I myself am He Who there soweth; and these blessed men
31.2583: Who hearken closely to me are the fair, clean corn.
31.2584: They do work my will. This world is the field,
31.2585: The broad farmland of the bairns of mankind;
31.2586: And it is Satan himself who soweth after Me
31.2587: Such loathsome lessons. Of the land-folk so many
31.2588: Of the people, so many hath he ruined, so that they wreak much wrong,
31.2589: Working his will. Yet they shall wax henceforth,
31.2590: Those men who are damned, even as do the good,
31.2591: Until the Judgment Day journeyeth on over them —
31.2592: The end of the world. Each field then, each acre,
31.2593: Hath ripened all in the realm. And the children of men will rightly
31.2594: Finish their fore-ordained fate. Earth will explode:
31.2595: That is the broadest of harvests; and the Bright, Glorious Lord
31.2596: Cometh above with the force of His angels; all folk shall gather,
31.2597: Who have seen this light; and shall receive such reward,
31.2598: Both evil and good. Then God’s angels go forth,
31.2599: Heaven’s holy warders; and from the host
31.2600: They shall seek out the sinless men; bring such men to beauty unending,
31.2601: To the high light of Heaven; throwing the others to the grounds of hell,
31.2602: To the surging fire, those who were forfeited.
31.2603: There in bonds shall they suffer the bitter fire,
31.2604: The awful pain, while the others have riches
31.2605: In the kingdom of Heaven, surely giving light on high,
31.2606: Like unto white suns. Such rewards will they reap,
31.2607: Those men for their murderous deeds. Whosoever hath wit in his mind,
31.2608: Thoughts in his heart, who would like to hear —
31.2609: An earl with his ears — let that indeed be his care
31.2610: In his innermost heart, how he will face
31.2611: God the Richest on that renowned Day of Reckoning
31.2612: Of all the words and the works which he hath done in this world.
31.2613: That is the most awful of all things indeed,
31.2614: The most fearful for the folk-bairns: that they must speak face to face with the Lord —
31.2615: The men to their Master Good; there would each man
31.2616: And all most gladly be rid of his misdeeds,
31.2617: His ugly sins. Instead each one should take care earlier,
31.2618: All the land-folk ever, before they must leave this light,
31.2619: That they will have this eternal honor,
31.2620: The high kingdom of Heaven and God’s holy grace.”

32.2621: So I discovered that He Himself, the Son of God,
32.2622: The Best of All Bairns told boldly in parables
32.2623: What there might be in the kingdom of world
32.2624: Among the races of heroes like unto the kingdom of Heaven;
32.2625: Quoth that that which is little often waxeth lighter,
32.2626: So that it riseth on high, “So doeth the realm of Heaven.
32.2627: That is ever more than any one man
32.2628: Can envision here in this world. Also his work is like unto him:
32.2629: That a man doth cast his nets into the sea,
32.2630: Doth fish in the flood, and findeth both in his catch —
32.2631: Both evil and good — toweth both to the shore,
32.2632: Getteth them both onto land, throweth the good on the grit,
32.2633: Letteth the other return again into the sea,
32.2634: To the wide waves there. So doeth All-Wielding God
32.2635: On the best-known Day to the bairns of men.
32.2636: He bringeth the earthlings together all,
32.2637: Picketh then the pure ones for the kingdom of Heaven,
32.2638: Letteth the damned ones fare down to the bottom,
32.2639: To the fire of hell. Nor doth any hero of men
32.2640: Know how to counter the pain, which a person,
32.2641: A man of the folk, must suffer in infernal hell.
32.2642: Likewise can no man find a like reward,
32.2643: Either in riches or rejoicing, as the Right-Wielder granteth,
32.2644: God Himself doth give to each man of goodness
32.2645: Who here keepeth himself so, so that he may enter the kingdom
32.2646: Of Heaven and the light that is long, long lasting.”
32.2647: So with His wiles He did teach them. And the folk wended hence
32.2648: From all Galilee-land to see God’s Bairn.
32.2649: They did so for the wonderment, whence such words came to Him,
32.2650: So sagely spoken; that He could say unto them
32.2651: The Gospel of God in such goodly fashion,
32.2652: Could quote it so cleverly. “He is of these clans here,” quoth they,
32.2653: “This man through His kinships. Here is His mother among us,
32.2654: A wife ’mid this world-folk. What, we all know them here.
32.2655: His kinships are all in our ken; and all of his clans as well.
32.2656: He waxed ’mid this world-folk. Whence cometh such wit,
32.2657: Whence cometh more might than hath any other man?”
32.2658: So the men of the land did scorn Him and spake on their silly words,
32.2659: Despised Him, Who was holy, and would not hear
32.2660: The Gospel of God. Because of their great disbelief
32.2661: He would not make known His parables many,
32.2662: His shining tokens, for He saw the doubt of their minds,
32.2663: Their wrath-harboring hearts: that here never were
32.2664: Men so grim-minded ’mongst the Jews as were in Galilee-land,
32.2665: So hard of heart. Though He was the Holy Christ —
32.2666: As God’s Bairn was He born — they would never believe
32.2667: Nor piously receive the gospel. Now the people began to plot,
32.2668: The world-men to wonder, how worst of all
32.2669: They might torment Mighty Christ. They hight their men,
32.2670: Their companions come together; they would accuse Him
32.2671: Gladly, the Son of God, accuse Him of sin
32.2672: With an evil design; for there was no longing in them
32.2673: For the Word, for the wise spell; but they began to speak ’mongst themselves
32.2674: How they might cast Him, the Clever and Strong, over a cliff,
32.2675: Over a mountain’s wall. The Wielder’s Bairn they would kill,
32.2676: Loose Him from life. Along with His folk
32.2677: He fared happily forth. There was no fear in His heart,
32.2678: For He knew full well that the Jewish folk,
32.2679: That the children of men could do Him no harm
32.2680: Because of His godliness e’er His time was come,
32.2681: Do no loathsome deeds. But with that folk He did go,
32.2682: Climbed high up a cliff, till they came to the place
32.2683: Where they planned to cast Him from the craggy wall,
32.2684: Fell Him to earth, that He would forfeit His life,
32.2685: That His age be ended. But the minds of the earls
32.2686: Up high on that mountain, the bitter thoughts
32.2687: Of those Jews did pass, so that not a one possesed such grimness of mind,
32.2688: Such wrathful spirit, that he could recognize Christ,
32.2690: No one could recognize Him. So could He stand ’mid the crowd,
32.2692: Fare forth through the folk. He found peace for Himself,
32.2693: Found protection ’gainst the host, and went forth through their midst,
32.2694: Through the folk of the foe. He fared, since He willed so,
32.2695: Into a wilderness, the Son of the Wielder,
32.2696: The Strongest of Kings: He had the power to choose
32.2697: Where in this land He would liefer be,

33.2689: With his disciples, the servant of God.
33.2700: He taught the land-folk long-lasting counsel:
33.2701: Said that they should do good, forsaking all sin,
33.2702: All misdeeds and murderous works. To many he was most dear,
33.2703: To good men and kind. There he sought the king of the Jews,
33.2704: The leader of his hosts in his house. Herod he was hight
33.2705: For his elders, this over-proud man.
33.2706: His bride did bide with him — she, who had been his brother’s,
33.2707: His wife in his wide home, until he went forth
33.2708: And changed his abode. Then came the king,
33.2709: Took this woman for his wife. There were children already,
33.2710: The bairns of his brother. He began to blame her —
33.2711: John the Good — said it was repulsive to God,
33.2712: To the Wielder Himself, for any world-man to do so:
33.2713: To take in his bed the bride of his brother
33.2714: And have her as wife. “If thou would’st hear me,
33.2715: Would’st believe in my lesson, thou should’st have her no longer,
33.2716: But in thy mind should’st avoid her: Thou shalt not have such love,
33.2717: Shalt not sin so greatly.” Sorrow did enter
33.2718: The woman’s heart at these words. She feared he would persuade
33.2719: The world-king with his speech and his words of wisdom
33.2720: To leave, to forsake her. Many loathsome things she began
33.2721: To plan and to plot; and she hight her squires,
33.2722: Her earls to take captive the innocent
33.2723: And put him in prison, place him in chains,
33.2724: Lock him in limb-fetters. She dared not deprive him of life
33.2725: Because of the folk, since all were his friends:
33.2726: They knew him as good and as worthy of God,
33.2727: Held him for a soothsayer, as so well they could.
33.2728: There was come the time for the Jew-king’s birthday,
33.2729: As the wise men of the folk had reckoned well,
33.2730: That he had been born and brought to this light.
33.2731: It was the custom that each earl should celebrate,
33.2732: Each man of the Jews mark it with feasting. There was a mighty crowd
33.2733: Of men gathered together in the guest hall,
33.2735: Leaders and dukes in the house, since their lord
33.2736: Was indeed on the king’s throne. Many Jews did come
33.2737: Into the great hall there. Glad-hearted were they,
33.2738: Blithe in their breasts. They beheld their ring-giver,
33.2739: Were really in rapture. Wine was brought to the room,
33.2740: Clear wine in the bowls, and the cup-bearers ran back and forth,
33.2741: Going with golden cups; gladness was there,
33.2742: Loud in the halls. The lords were drinking;
33.2743: The herdsman of Jews bethought him with joy,
33.2744: Pondered how best he might please the people.
33.2745: He hight go forth that gay, young girl,
33.2746: His brother’s bairn, as he sat on his bench
33.2747: Haughty with wine; to the woman he spake,
33.2748: Greeted her before the men-guests and most eagerly bade her,
33.2749: That she begin some merriment here before the guests,
33.2750: Something fair in the feast-hall. “Let the folk see
33.2751: What thou has learned to make joyous the many,
33.2752: Make them blithe on the benches; if thou doest my bidding,
33.2753: My word before this world-folk; then I will verily tell unto thee
33.2754: Loudly before all these landsmen, and thus let it be done,
33.2755: That I will give unto thee all that thou asketh
33.2756: Before these my ring-friends, though thou demandest
33.2757: Half of my realm, half of my kingdom;
33.2758: So shall I do, nor shall any world-men
33.2759: Turn me with words; but truly it shall be accomplished.”
33.2760: The the maid was thereafter inclined in her mind,
33.2761: In her heart, to her lord, so that in the house,
33.2762: In the guest-hall she began much gaiety now,
33.2763: Even as the custom of the folk did command,
33.2764: The way of the people. The maid did play,
33.2765: Most merrily romped through the house. The minds of the many,
33.2766: Their hearts were happy. When the maiden had served
33.2767: The folk-king there for his thanks then,
33.2768: And had served, too, his earlships all, as many as were
33.2769: Of good men present, she would fain claim her gift —
33.2770: The maid in front of the multitude. To her mother she went
33.2771: To speak and asked her forthwith — for she was anxious to know —
33.2772: What she should bid him, bid the bastion’s warden give unto her.
33.2773: Of her own mind her mother did tell her, hight that before the men
33.2774: She should ask for naught else except that he give her
33.2775: There in the hall John’s holy head
33.2776: Bereft of its body. For the folk it was baleful,
33.2777: For the men in their minds, when they heard the maid speaking thus,
33.2778: For the king it was, also; but he could not break it, his pledge,
33.2779: Turn his word away. Therefore he bade the bearers of weapons
33.2780: To go from the guest hall, take the good man
33.2781: And relieve him of life. Not long thereafter they brought
33.2782: The holy man’s head up to the hall, gave it the girl,
33.2784: To the maid before the many. To her mother she took it.
33.2785: And that was the end-day of the wisest of all men,
33.2786: Who ever came to this world as a child born of woman,
33.2788: Of wife from an earl — excepting ever that One,
33.2789: Whom the Maid did bear, she who had known no man
