33.2790: Anywhere in this world; but the All-Wielder so destined it
33.2791: From the fields of Heaven by the Holy Ghost —
33.2792: The Mighty God had so marked it. Never was man like unto him,
33.2793: Neither before nor after. Now the earls turned to him,
33.2794: The men around John, his followers many,
33.2795: His beloved disciples. In the sand they buried
33.2796: His beloved body. But well did they know
33.2797: He could claim God’s light, along with his Lord,
33.2798: Heavenly glory in that home on high —

34.2800: John’s followers went, most woeful of spirit
34.2801: But holy of mind. The death of their master
34.2802: Filled them with sorrow. They repaired then to seek
34.2803: The Son of the Wielder away in the wilderness,
34.2804: Christ the Almighty, and made known unto Him
34.2805: The good man’s demise: how the master of Jews
34.2806: Did heave off the head of the holiest of men
34.2807: With the sword’s edge. The Son of the Lord had no wish
34.2808: To speak of His own pain; for He knew that this soul
34.2809: Was held in all holiness against the haters,
34.2810: In peace ’gainst the foe. Thus He grew famous
34.2811: Across the country, He, the best of those teaching
34.2812: In the wilderness there; world-men did gather;
34.2813: To the folk He did come, for they had great longing
34.2814: For the wisdom of words; and He had long wanted,
34.2815: The Son of the Lord, to lead such a gathering
34.2816: Of the land-folk to the light of the Lord,
34.2817: To turn the folk to His will. The Wielder did teach,
34.2818: The Mighty Lord taught all the long day so many of mankind
34.2819: Folk from all over and from foreign lands, until in the evening
34.2820: The sun did sink to its seat. Then His disciples twelve
34.2821: Did go to God’s Bairn and told their Good Lord
34.2822: In what dire need the men did there dwell; quoth that they did need His help,
34.2823: The world-folk in the wilderness there; “Not well can they hold themselves upright,
34.2824: The heroes, for the pangs of their hunger; now, Lord Good and Most High,
34.2825: Let them go to find lodgings. Nearby lie towns
34.2826: Filled with folk aplenty; there they will find meat to buy,
34.2827: The world-folk there in those bailiwicks.” Thereupon Wielding Christ spake again,
34.2828: The Lord of the Land-folk, quoth that there was little need,
34.2830: Because of their poverty. Give these people enough.
34.2831: Let them come here gladly!” His words had he ready,
34.2832: The wise man named Philip; quoth that there were so many,
34.2833: Such a multitude of mankind, “Though we might have meat
34.2834: Ready to give them, were able to buy it
34.2835: And for that sold together two hundred pieces of silver,
34.2836: Still would I doubt that each would have some.
34.2838: So little were that for these land-folk.” Then again the Land-Warder spake
34.2839: And asked them, anxious for knowledge,
34.2840: The Master of Men, how much of meat,
34.2841: Of food they had gathered. Then again with his words
34.2842: Andrew did speak before the earls to the All-Wielder Himself,
34.2843: And said now to Him that they had naught for the journey,
34.2844: “Naught but five breads of barley among the followers, and fishes twain:
34.2846: How can that serve such a many?” Mighty Christ spake again,
34.2847: The Good Son of God, and hight they divide into groups,
34.2848: The crowd, into sections; and hight they should sit,
34.2849: All the lords, on the ground; the hordes of the land-folk should lie
34.2850: On the green grass; and to His followers goodly he spake,
34.2851: The Best of All Bairns; hight them go bring the bread
34.2852: And fetch forth the fish. the folk bided still —
34.2853: The great crowd was sitting. Through His strength and His power
34.2854: The Lord of Mankind at this moment did bless the meat,
34.2855: The Holy Heaven-King, and with His hands He did break it,
34.2856: And to His disciples He gave it, hight that they should take it and divide it
34.2857: Among the multitude there. Their Master’s word they accomplished.
34.2858: To each man gladly they carried His gift,
34.2859: The holy help. It waxed in their hands,
34.2860: The meat for each man: for the multitude
34.2861: There came a life full of joy; the landsmen all,
34.2862: The folk had their fill — as many as had fared there together
34.2863: From all the wide ways. Then Wielding Christ
34.2864: Hight His disciples go, and hight them watch well,
34.2865: That the leavings left there would not be lost,
34.2866: Commanded them gather the many of mankind
34.2867: When they had had their fill. There was left of the food,
34.2868: Of the bread so much, that they gathered baskets —
34.2869: Twelve of them filled. That was a great token,
34.2870: A great deed of God, since one counted together,
34.2871: Without wife or child, of world-folk there,
34.2872: Fully five thousand. The folk understood,
34.2873: The men in their minds, that it was a Lord Most Mighty
34.2874: Whom they did have. They did laud the Heaven-King,
34.2875: The people did praise Him; said that no wiser prophet
34.2876: Would ever fare in this light or that from God
34.2877: He would have greater might in this mid-world here,
34.2878: A more honest heart. All of them did say
34.2879: That he was worthy of holding all wealth,
34.2880: That indeed He should own all the realms of earth,
34.2881: The wide throne of world, “since He hath such wit,
34.2882: Such great power from God!” The people all thought it meet
34.2883: That they raise Him to the highest of hights,
34.2884: Choose Him their king: to Christ this was worthy of naught,
34.2885: Since He Himself had worked this world-realm all through His power alone,
34.2886: Had made earth and the high heaven, and had held them since,
34.2888: Both the land and the landsmen — but the loathsome foe
34.2889: Believed naught of that: that all stood ’neath His rule —
34.2890: The power over kingdoms and over empires, too,
34.2891: The judgment of man. Still through the speech of these men
34.2892: He cared not to have it, His rule — He, Holy Lord —
34.2893: Have the name of World-King. Therefore He began no further word-strife
34.2894: With these people there; but He went where He willed
34.2895: Up on a mountain; God’s Mighty Bairn fled
34.2896: The insolent talk, and He told His disciples
34.2897: To sail over a sea; and He Himself said
34.2898: Where they should go to greet Him again.

35.2899: The people parted and spread through all lands,
35.2900: A great folk scattered, for their Lord had gone
35.2901: Up on the mountain, the Mightiest of Bairns,
35.2902: Wielding as was His will. On the water’s shore
35.2903: Gathered the disciples of Christ, whom He Himself had chosen,
35.2904: The twelve for their goodly faith; nor felt they doubt;
35.2905: But in God’s service they would gladly go
35.2906: Over the sea. They let the high-horned ship
35.2907: Cut through the strong stream, the clear wave and the water sheer;
35.2909: The light of the day, the sun strode to rest. Night surrounded
35.2910: The seafarers with mist; the earls strove on,
35.2911: Forward in the flood. Now the fourth hour
35.2912: Of night was come. All-Saving Christ
35.2913: Warded the wave-farers: the wind grew great,
35.2915: The sea ’gainst the stem; with trouble they steered it,
35.2916: The ship through the wind. The warriors grew fearful of mind,
35.2917: Their hearts filled with care. The lake-farers indeed
35.2918: Never believed that they would ever reach land
35.2919: Because of the battle of weather. There they beheld Christ,
35.2920: The Wielder, walking over the waves on the sea,
35.2921: Faring on foot. Into the flood he could
35.2922: Not sink, nor sink into the sea; for the power of Him Himself
35.2923: Held Him on high. Their hearts became fearful,
35.2924: The minds of the men. The feared the mighty Fiend
35.2925: Had done this to deceive Him. Then their Dear Lord did speak unto them,
35.2926: The Holy Heaven-King; and said that He was their Lord,
35.2927: Splendid and Mighty. “Now in your minds
35.2928: Shall ye all take courage; nor be ye frightened of spirit.
35.2929: But behave ye boldly: for I am God’s Bairn,
35.2930: The Son of Himself, and against the sea I shall help you,
35.2931: Against these flood-streams.” Then a man did answer
35.2932: From upon the ship, a sage most worthy,
35.2933: Peter the good: that no longer he wished to endure the pain,
35.2934: The woe of the water, “If Thou beest the Wielder,
35.2935: Master Most Good, as I think in my mind,
35.2936: Bid me come unto Thee across the flood of the sea,
35.2937: Dry over the deep water — if Thou art indeed my Lord,
35.2938: The Master of Many.” The Mighty Christ
35.2939: Hight him come unto Him. He was soon ready,
35.2940: Stepped on the stem; and striding, he went
35.2941: Forth to the Lord; the flood held him upright,
35.2942: The man through God’s might, until in his mind he began
35.2943: To dread the deep water, when he saw it driven —
35.2944: The wave — by the wind: The flood wound around him,
35.2945: The billows about him. But even as in his mind he did doubt,
35.2946: So the water grew weak beneath him. And into the wave,
35.2947: Into the sea-stream he sank: and straightway he called
35.2948: To the Bairn of God and eagerly bade Him,
35.2949: That He save him there, since he, His thane, was
35.2950: In distress and in need. The the Lord of the Nations
35.2951: Embraced him with His hands and His arms, and straightway did ask him,
35.2952: Why he was doubtful. “Why, thou should’st trust well
35.2953: And know most verily that the might of the water,
35.2954: Of the sea itself could not hinder thy steps,
35.2955: That of the lake-flood thy feet for as long as thou believest in Me,
35.2956: In thy heart hath a faith steadfast. Now I shall help thee,
35.2957: In thy need shall save thee.” The Almighty so took him,
35.2958: The Holy Man by the hand: here again the clear water
35.2959: Became clear under foot, and they fared together
35.2960: Both step in step, until they came aboard ship,
35.2961: Stepped from the stream. And at the stem
35.2962: Sat the Best of All Bairns. Then the broad water,
35.2963: The stream became stilled; and they came to the shore,
35.2964: The landfarers indeed did come to the land
35.2965: Through the battle of waters; and said thanks to the Wielder,
35.2966: Gave praise to their Dear Lord in deed and in word.
35.2967: They fell to His feet and did speak full many
35.2968: Words of wisdom; quoth that they right well knew
35.2969: That He Himself was verily the Son of the Lord
35.2970: Here in the world and wielded power
35.2971: Over he middle earth; and all men He could help,
35.2972: Whosoever they were, as He had done on the flood

36.2974: Turned His steps from the sea: The Son of the Lord,
36.2975: God’s only Child. Heathens did come to Him,
36.2976: Foreign folk fared to Him there. For from afar
36.2977: They had heard of His good works: that so many true words
36.2979: He did speak; for He longed greatly to further such folk,
36.2980: So that straightway they would serve God gladly,
36.2981: Becoming true vassals of the King of Heaven,
36.2982: The many of mankind. So He made His way across Judea,
36.2983: Sought out the city of Sidon; His disciples He had with Him,
36.2984: Christ’ followers good. There a woman came toward Him
36.2985: From another tribe: of aethling birth was she,
36.2986: From the kith of Canaan-land; she bade the Lord Christ so strong,
36.2987: The Holy One, to grant her His help; quoth that great trouble had come to her,
36.2988: Sorrow for the sake of her daughter; said she was ensnared by sickness,
36.2989: Deceived by treacherous devils. “Now is her death at hand.
36.2990: The wrathful wights have robbed her of wit. Now I beg Thee, my All-Wielding Ruler,
36.2991: Thou Son of David himself, from such sickness release her,
36.2992: That Thou mayest mercifully protect this poor maid
36.2993: From the grievous devils.” But All-Wielding Christ gave
36.2994: Her no answer. Therefore she went after Him,
36.2995: Followed Him boldly, till she came to His feet,
36.2996: And weeping did speak unto Him. The disciples of Christ
36.2997: Bade the Master that He be mild in His heart
36.2998: To the woman. Then had ready His word
36.2999: The Son of the Lord, and unto His disciples He spake:
36.3000: “First shall I be of use to the folkships here,
36.3001: To the people of Israel, so that a pious spirit
36.3002: They shall have for their Lord. For they are in need of help:
36.3003: The land-folk are lost; they have left and forsaken
36.3004: The word of the Wielder; with doubts are they troubled — these people —
36.3005: Harboring treacherous hearts. Nor is the host of Israel
36.3006: Willing to hear their Lord; but they are unbelieving,
36.3007: The men in their Master. Then to the rest of mankind
36.3008: Help shall come later.” Lo, most zealously then
36.3009: The woman begged with her words, that All-Wielding Christ
36.3010: Become mildly inclined, that she might henceforth enjoy
36.3012: Her child, having her hale. Then the Lord spake to her,
36.3013: The Magnificent and Mighty. “No man,” quoth He, “hath the right,
36.3014: No person ever, to do good or give alms in such manner,
36.3015: That his own bairns will be bereft of their bread,
36.3016: Deprived ’gainst their will, so that they suffer great pain,
36.3017: Grim, hateful hunger; and feedeth his hound-dogs with their food.”
36.3018: “True it is, Wielder,” quoth she, “what Thou speakest indeed with Thy words,
36.3019: Most truly dost say. Why, oft ’neath the tables
36.3020: In the halls of the lords, the puppies hop hither
36.3021: And yon for the crumbs, full many of which fall
36.3022: From the board of their master.” The Peace-Bairn of God heard
36.3023: The will of the woman, and with words He did speak:
36.3024: “Well that thou, wife, hast goodness of will.
36.3025: Great is thy faith in the power of God,
36.3026: In the Lord of the Land-folk. Lo, all will be done
36.3027: For the life of thy bairn, even as thou has bidden of Me!”
36.3028: And straightway was she healed, as the Holy Lord had said
36.3029: With words of truth; and the wife was happy
36.3030: That henceforth she would be blessed with joy in her bairn.
36.3031: Christ the Healer had helped her indeed,
36.3032: Had snatched her away from the strength of the Fiend,
36.3033: Guarded her against the loathsome wight. The Wielder went forth.
36.3034: The Best of all Bairns sought Him another borough,
36.3035: Which was so thick with the throngs of the Jews,
36.3036: Settled with south-dwellers. There, I discoverd,
36.3037: He greeted His followers whom in His goodness He had chosen,
36.3038: Disciples who gladly stayed for His wise speech. “I shall ask of you all,
36.3039: With My words,” quoth He, “My followers: What say the Jews,
36.3040: That notorious folk, who I am among men?”
36.3041: Happily His friends gave answer to Him,
36.3042: His disciples: “The Jewish folk,” they said,
36.3043: “The earls are not of one mind. Some say Thou art Elias,
36.3044: The soothsayer wise, who was here long ago,
36.3045: A good earl among these folk; some say Thou art John,
36.3046: Our Dear Lord’s herald, who once did dip
36.3047: The world-folk in water. But with words they all say,
36.3048: That Thou art some sort of noble, some aethling man,
36.3049: Some soothsayer or prophet, who hath taught the people
36.3050: Once before with his words. And once again Thou art come to this light
36.3051: To teach the kith of mankind.” Wielding Christ spake again:
36.3052: “What quoth ye that I be?” quoth He, “My followers,
36.3053: My landsmen beloved?” Then not late with his words was he,
36.3054: Simon Peter; but straightway he spake —
36.3055: One for them all — of good spirit was he:
36.3056: Daring in thought, he was dear to the Lord.

37.3058: The Living God, who created the Light,
37.3059: Christ, King Eternal: so willingly do we quoth,
37.3060: We Thy disciples, that Thou art God Himself,
37.3061: The Best of All Healers.” Then his Lord spake to him,
37.3062: “So blessed art thou, Simon,” quoth He, “Son of Jonas, thou thyself could’st not have
37.3063: Marked such thoughts in thy mind; nor could any man’s tongue
37.3064: Show thee with words. But the Wielder Himself did this for thee,
37.3065: The Father of All Folk-Bairns, that thou spakest so forthright,
37.3066: So deep of thy Liege. Dear shall be thy reward,
37.3067: Limpid and pure thy belief in thy Lord: like unto a stone is thy spirit.
37.3068: So strong art thou like unto a rock; and the children of men shall call thee
37.3069: Saint Peter; and on this stone men shall build My great hall,
37.3070: God’s holy house. There shall His family, His household
37.3071: All gather, blessed, together, and against thy strength,
37.3072: Thy power, the portals of hell cannot stand. To thee I present it,
37.3073: The key to Heaven’s kingdom, so that o’er the Christian folk
37.3074: Thou shalt after Me have the most might; the spirits of men
37.3075: Shall all come to thee; for thou shalt claim great power
37.3076: O’er the bairns of mankind. Whomsoever thou would’st bind
37.3077: Here on this earth: for him both is done,
37.3078: For him the kingdom of heaven is locked and for him hell lieth open,
37.3079: The burning fire; and whomsoever thou would’st again unbind,
37.3080: Whose hands unfetter: for him is Heaven’s kingdom
37.3081: Unlocked, the greatest of lights, and life everlasting,
37.3082: God’s fair, green meadows. With such gifts I would
37.3083: Reward thee thy faith. Still I would not that ye proclaim now to the folk,
37.3084: To the multitude yet, that I be the Mighty Christ,
37.3085: The Own Bairn of God. For the Jews shall still bind Me,
37.3086: In guiltiness tie Me and torture Me most terribly,
37.3088: Do Me great wrongs here in Jerusalem,
37.3089: With spear-point attacking, with the sharp edge against Me,
37.3090: Relieve Me of life. Through the power of the Lord here in this light
37.3092: I shall arise though from death on the third day.”
37.3093: Then in sorrow was he, Simon Peter, the best of all thanes;
37.3094: Most grieved he of mind. And to the Master he spake,
37.3095: The warrior in whispers. “That is not the will of the Wielder,
37.3096: Of Mighty God,” quoth he. “It cannot be that Thou should’st endure
37.3097: Such pain ’mid this people. There is plainly no need,
37.3098: O Holy Master!” The Christ Mighty and Marvelous,
37.3099: The Lord, did reply — he was dear to His heart —
37.3100: “Why,” quoth He, “thou art now opposed to My will,
37.3101: Thou best of My thanes? Thou knowest this folk,
37.3102: Hast ken of the customs of men. But God’s might, which I must accomplish,
37.3103: That wittest thou not. With words of truth
37.3104: I can tell thee much: that here ’mid the people stand
37.3105: Disciples of Mine who shall not die,
37.3106: Not begin the trip hence, before they shall see Heaven’s light,
37.3107: The kingdom of God.” From His disciples He chose
37.3109: Jacob and John, those good men twain,
37.3110: Both of the brothers. And He betook Himself then upon a mountain
37.3111: With His disciples aside from the others — God’s Bairn so blessed
37.3112: With His thanes three; Lord of this Folk,
37.3113: Wielder of World, He would show unto them
37.3114: Wonders a-many, such tokens, so that they should trust and believe
37.3115: That He Himself was the Son of the Lord,
37.3116: The Holy Heaven-King. At a high wall
37.3117: They climbed stone and cliff, till they came to a place,
37.3118: These men, close to the clouds, which All-Wielding Christ,
37.3119: The Strongest of Kings, had Himself chosen,
37.3120: That He would reveal most verily His godliness

38.3122: When He bent low in prayer,
38.3123: Lo, there upon the mountain His whole appearance,
38.3124: His garb became changed. His cheeks became light,
38.3125: Shone like the bright, shimmering sun: so shone God’s Bairn.
38.3126: Light was His body, and long rays shone
38.3127: Radiant around the All-Wielder’s Bairn, His raiment so white
38.3128: To the sight as is snow. Then a marvel was shown
38.3129: Up there on the mountain: Elias and Moses
38.3130: Did come there to Christ to exchange words with Him,
38.3131: The Strongest of Kings. There was winsome conversing,
38.3132: Good words among men; where the Son of God
38.3133: Would fain have talk with those famous men.
38.3134: So blithe it was, up there on the mountain. And the light shone bright,
38.3135: And it was like unto that goodly garden, tht meadow green,
38.3136: Like unto Paradise itself. And Peter there spake,
38.3137: Hero hardy of spirit and to His Lord he did speak,
38.3138: Greeted the Son of God, “Good it is to be here,
38.3139: If Thou hast so chosen, O Christ All-Wielding,
38.3140: That men on these heights build Thee a house,
38.3141: Make it most splendid; and for Moses a second;
38.3142: And a third for Elias. This is the home of joy,
38.3143: The most winsome possession.” Just as he spake these words,
38.3144: The air clove in twain: from the clouds light shone clear,
38.3145: A glistening glow. And the good men
38.3146: Were wrapped in a radiance. Then from the clouds rolled
38.3147: God’s holy voice. And to the heroes there
38.3148: He Himself said that this was His Son,
38.3149: The Most Beloved of the Living: “I like Him well,
38.3150: To My heart He is dear. Ye shall hear Him,
38.3151: Following Him gladly.” Then the followers of Christ,
38.3152: Those men, could not withstand the cloud’s clear light,
38.3153: The word of God and its might, which is great.
38.3154: But they fell forward, and they feared indeed
38.3155: They would lose their lives. Then the Land-Warden did go to them;
38.3156: And with His hand He touched them, the Best of Healers,
38.3157: Hight they should feel no dread: “No harm shall come to you here
38.3158: From these blessed sights which ye have now seen,
38.3159: These marvelous things.” Then the men’s spirits
38.3160: In their hearts were healed, and healed were their minds;
38.3161: In their breasts there was comfort: for they saw God’s Bairn
38.3163: Heaven’s light, was again hidden. Then the Holy Christ
38.3164: Went Him down from the mountain, and He did then bid
38.3165: His followers that they tell not unto the Jewish folk
38.3166: Of the sight they had seen. “Until I myself here
38.3167: In splendor shall stand up from My death,
38.3168: Arise from My rest. Then may ye relate it,
38.3169: Spread it over the mid-earth and its many peoples,

39.3171: Went again to Galilee-land Great Christ sought His landsmen,
39.3172: The home of His kin. With bright, clear pictures
39.3173: He spake much unto them. And the Son of God
39.3174: Concealed not sorrowful tidings from His blessed disciples,
39.3175: But openly He said all things to them,
39.3176: His followers good, how the Jewish folk
39.3177: Would torture Him all terribly. Then troubled were they,
39.3178: The wise men, greatly, and grieved at heart,
39.3179: Saddened of spirit, when they heard their Lord,
39.3180: The Son of the Wielder, telling them with words
39.3181: What He would endure here midst the earth-folk,
39.3182: Willingly all among the people of world. Then All-Wielding Christ,
39.3183: The Man, went from Galilee and sought a city of Jews.
39.3184: They came to Capernaum. There He found a king’s thane,
39.3185: Proud ’mid the people; quoth that he was the trusted courier
39.3186: Of the noble emperor; he greeted thereafter
39.3187: Simon Peter; and said he had been sent here
39.3188: That he remind each man and every
39.3189: Of his head-tax which he must pay as a tithe
39.3190: Here to the court: “Nor can any man hesitate,
39.3191: But he payeth unto him his choicest treasure.
39.3192: Only your Master alone hath omitted His tithe,
39.3193: Hath neglected it. Nor will my lord like this,
39.3195: When they inform him of this, the aethling emperor.”
39.3196: The Simon Peter went straightway. He so wanted
39.3197: To tell this unto His Master. But in His mind
39.3198: Holy Christ already knew; for from Him naught could be hidden,
39.3199: Not even a word; but He well knew indeed
39.3200: The mind of each man; but he admonished His thane,
39.3201: Simon Peter of fame, that into the sea
39.3202: He should cast his hook. “Whatsoever thou dost catch,
39.3203: What fish at the first,” quoth He, “from the flood thou must draw it,
39.3204: Wedge open its jaws: from under its chin mayest thou take
39.3205: Golden guilders, with which thou shalt give
39.3206: The man enough of the tax which he seeketh from us, from Me and from thee.”
39.3207: He needed bid him thereafter no more,
39.3208: Give him no other words: but the Good Fisher did go,
39.3209: Simon Peter; into the sea he did cast
39.3210: His angle, his hook in the wave; and verily then
39.3211: He drew a fish from the flood. Its jaws
39.3212: He tore open with his two hands. And from under its chin took
39.3214: The golden guilders. And all he so did as God’s Son
39.3215: Had told him with words. So was the strength of the Wielder,
39.3216: His might made manifest, how each man and all
39.3217: Should most willingly pay to his world-lord here
39.3218: The taxes and tolls determined against him,
39.3219: And do so gladly; nor should any forget this,
39.3220: Neglect or deny in his mind; but mild in his heart,
39.3221: He should serve him humbly. so should he work
39.3222: The will of God and still gain the grace

40.3224: His disciples good: “If against you,” quoth He, “any man
40.3225: Do act in sin, then take ye this man aside,
40.3226: This warrior, with whispers, and speak ye wise counsel
40.3227: And teach him with words. Should he not be worthy
40.3228: To hear your teachings, then fetch ye hither
40.3229: Other men and good; and with his grim works reproach him,
40.3230: Say them forth most soothly. If then his sins
40.3231: His evil deeds do not grieve him, so make ye them open to others,
40.3232: Most revealed to the multitude, and let many men
40.3233: Know his wrongs. Then easily he will repent his works,
40.3234: In his heart indeed rue them, when he heareth that so many folk,
40.3235: Bairns of mankind have watched them and warded off with their words
40.3236: The works of his evil. If even then he will not change,
40.3237: But scorneth such a many, then let this man fare forth,
40.3238: Believe him a heathen, and let him be loathsome unto you in your hearts.
40.3239: In your minds avoid him, unless God the Mild,
40.3240: The High King of Heaven, grant help unto him,
40.3241: The Father of All Folk-Bairns.” Peter then asked,
40.3242: The best of all thanes then questioned the Lord,
40.3243: “How often shall I absolve from sin this man
40.3244: Who hath done loathsome work against me, Beloved Lord?
40.3245: How many times shall I take from him all his blame
40.3246: For his wicked works, before rewarding the wrongs
40.3247: By wreaking vengeance?” The spake again the Warden of the Land.
40.3248: The Son of God did give answer unto His goodly thane:
40.3249: “I shall never say unto thee: seven, as thou thyself hast spoken,
40.3250: Hast made known with thy mouth. I add more thereto
40.3251: Seven times seventy! So shalt thou absolve each one
40.3252: From evil, from sin. So I would give unto thee
40.3253: Teachings, a word most true. Since to thee I have lent the power,
40.3254: That thou beest the highest one of my household
40.3255: To many of mankind; so shalt thou be mild unto them,
40.3256: Merciful unto the multitude.” Then a young man
40.3257: Came to the Teacher, and Jesus Christ he did question:
40.3258: “Master Most Good,” quoth he, “What must I do,
40.3259: So that I may reach the realms of Heaven?”
40.3260: All goodly riches had he gained indeed,
40.3261: Many a treasure, too, though mildness of heart
40.3262: He bore in his breast. Then spake God’s Bairn unto him:
40.3263: “Why speakest thou of a Good one? There is no man
40.3264: But that One Single One, who shaped this All —
40.3265: This world in its winsomeness. If ’tis thy will,
40.3267: Then shalt thou hold to the holy teachings,
40.3268: Those which the Old Law command thee follow:
40.3269: That thou shalt not slay; nor swear falsely,
40.3270: Neither commit adultery; nor bear thou false witness
40.3271: Nor steal nor cause strife; nor be thou too stubborn of mind,
40.3272: Nor hating nor hateful; commit thou no robbery.
40.3273: Forsake thou all envy; to thine elders show kindness,
40.3274: To thy father and mother. Be thou fair to thy friends,
40.3275: To thy nearest be gracious. Then wilt thou be granted joy
40.3276: In the kingdom of Heaven, if thou wilt keep this
40.3277: And follow God’s teachings.” Again the young man did speak:
40.3278: “All things have I done,” quoth he, “as Thou now dost teach
40.3279: And tellest with words; that I have no whit left undone
40.3280: Since the days of my childhood.” Then Christ did begin
40.3281: To turn His eyes onto him. “One thing,” He told him,
40.3282: “Is still lacking in thy works. If thou hast the will,
40.3283: That thou would’st serve thy Lord most perfectly still,
40.3284: Then shalt thou take thy hoard and thy treasure;
40.3285: Thou shalt rid thyself of thy riches all,
40.3286: Order thy precious jewels to be portioned out
40.3287: And shared with the poor. Then shalt thou have
40.3288: A hoard in Heaven. Come thou then as healed unto me
40.3289: And follow My path. Then shalt thou have peace ever after.”
40.3290: Then the words of the Christ caused great worry and care
40.3291: To the child-young man. His mind was sore,
40.3292: About his heart his spirit. For he had great wealth,
40.3293: Had won great treasure; he again turned away.
40.3294: In his breast he felt burdened indeed,
40.3295: In his heart most heavy. Then Christ looked after him,
40.3296: The All-Wielder, since He so willed,
40.3297: And said to His disciples, who were there, that it was ever so hard
40.3298: For a rich man to reach the realms of Heaven:
40.3299: “More easily may an elephant, though it be unseemly great,
40.3300: Go through a needle’s eye, be that eye so narrow —
40.3301: Slip through more softly, than this soul into Heaven,
40.3303: The soul of this wealthy man, who hath turned his will to world-things entirely,
40.3304: The thoughts of his mind, and mindeth not the great might of God.”

41.3305: Him answered then an aethling most excellent and honored,
41.3306: Simon Peter; and speaking, he bade
41.3307: His Blessed Lord: “What reward shall we look for,
41.3308: What goods to repay us — we, who have forsaken
41.3309: Our lands and our heritage for love of Thy following,
41.3310: Our farmyards and families, and chosen Thee for our Lord,
41.3311: Following Thy footsteps? What good will there be for us,
41.3312: What long-lasting reward?” The Lord of the Land-folk
41.3313: Himself said unto them: “When I shall come to sit,” quoth He
41.3314: “In My might and My power on that most Renowned Day,
41.3315: When I shall deal out the dooms to the people of earth,
41.3316: Then may ye sit with your Master, may wield His affairs —
41.3318: Ye may judge Israel’s aethling folk
41.3319: By its deeds: so honored will ye be up there.
41.3320: For verily I say unto you: whosoever acteth on this earth,
41.3321: So that for My love he leaveth the dear home of his kin,
41.3322: He shall receive a tenfold reward, if he acteth
41.3324: Loyally, with pureness of heart. Above shall he have Heaven’s light.
41.3325: Eternal life will lie open.” Therefore the Lord,
41.3326: The Best of all Bairns, began to speak pictures,
41.3327: Told how a man of great fortune in former days
41.3328: Lived ’monst the land-folk: “He had laid aside wealth,
41.3329: Gathered great treasures unto him; and ever with gold
41.3330: He was decked both with silken stuff and with the sheen
41.3331: Of fine jewels; and so many goods he had stored away
41.3332: In his buildings; and at banquet
41.3333: He sat every day. There was splendid carousing
41.3334: And joy on his benches. There was a beggar-man also:
41.3335: Lame of limb was he and Lazarus hight;
41.3336: And every day he did lie in front of the door,
41.3337: Where he knew the rich man received food in the guest-hall
41.3339: And sat at his banquet; and outside bided
41.3340: The poor man; nor was he ever permitted within,
41.3341: Nor could he bring it about by begging that bread
41.3342: Be brought out to him, such bread as had fallen from the dish
41.3343: Down beneath their feet. Not a thing did he gain
41.3344: From the high man who ruled over the house; but only the hounds of that man
41.3345: Came and licked on his wounds, as he lay there
41.3346: And endured his hunger. Not one whit of help
41.3347: Came from the man of fortune. Then I found out that fate
41.3348: Admonished the poor man most mightily
41.3349: Of his end-days: that he should renounce
41.3350: His life and the tumult of men. The Lord’s angels
41.3351: Did receive his spirit and so led him from there,
41.3352: So that the poor man’s soul did sit in the lap
41.3353: Of Abraham. Ever henceforth he could now dwell
41.3354: In all winsomeness. The Weird came also,
41.3355: That fateful hour, to the man of fortune,
41.3356: So that he should forsake this light; the loathsome wights
41.3357: Lowered his soul, sank it deep into swarthy hell,
41.3358: In the furnace below to the will of the Fiend,
41.3359: Grubbed him deep into the Grim One’s home. There he could gaze on
41.3360: The good man, see Abraham, where he dwelt above
41.3361: In a life of joy; and Lazarus sat
41.3362: Blithe in his bosom; received bright reward
41.3363: For his poverty and wretchedness all. And the rich man there
41.3364: Lay hot in hell, and he did cry up from there:
41.3365: “Father Abraham,” quoth he, “It is fearfully needful for me,
41.3366: That thou becomest mild to me in thy mind,
41.3367: Merciful unto me in this flame. Send Lazarus unto me,
41.3368: That he fetch cold water for me in this furnace.
41.3370: Hotly I burn alive in this hell and I am in need of thy help,
41.3371: That he slake my tongue with his little finger.
41.3372: My tongue hath its token now: woeful torture for my evil counsel,
41.3374: For my sinful speech. Now is come to me such reward!”
41.3375: Abraham answered unto him — he was the ancient father —
41.3376: “Ponder in thy heart,” quoth he, “what thou hast had
41.3377: Of wealth in the world. Why, thou hast wasted thy rapture all,
41.3378: Thy goods in the gardens, and what was to be given
41.3380: Endured wrong in the light; had plenteous grief
41.3381: And pain in the world. For this he shall now have wealth,
41.3382: Living in happiness. But thou shalt suffer hot flames,
41.3383: The burning fire. Nor may any betterment
41.3384: Come hither to hell. So hath Holy God
41.3385: Made it fast with hands and with arms; nor may any one fare,
41.3386: Any thane through the darkness — it is here too thick under us.”
41.3387: The the earl spake again to Abraham:
41.3388: From that hot hell did he beg for help,
41.3389: That he do send Lazarus himself
41.3390: Down to the tumult of men, “so that he may tell
41.3391: Unto those brethren of mine how I here burn
41.3392: And suffer great pain. Among the people,
41.3393: The folk, there are five: I am in great fear
41.3394: That they shall also become sinful and shall suffer such pangs
41.3395: In this great fire.” Then again spake unto him
41.3396: Old Father Abraham, quoth that they ever had had —
41.3397: The folk — the old law there in their land,
41.3398: The commandments of Moses, and from many a prophet
41.3399: Their words also. “If they are willing
41.3400: To hold and to keep them, then need they never enter into hell,
41.3401: To sear in that fire. If they so fulfill that
41.3402: Which those do bid them who read in the books
41.3403: To teach mankind. But if they are unwilling to accomplish that,
41.3404: They will also not listen to Him, who riseth from here,
41.3405: A Man from death. In their minds let them
41.3406: Choose for themselves which seemeth sweeter
41.3407: To win so long as they are still in this world,
41.3408: So that in the hereafter they have evil or good!”

42.3409: So did He teach the land-folk all with His words of light,
42.3410: The Best of All Bairns; and with bright pictures
42.3411: A-many, the Mighty Lord did speak to mankind:
42.3412: Quoth that a blessed man had begun to gather
42.3413: Men in the morning, promised them money —
42.3414: He, the first of his family — a very fine reward:
42.3415: Said that unto each and to all he would give
42.3416: A coin of pure silver. So came together
42.3417: Many men in the winegarden — and he commanded their work —
42.3418: Gathered early at morn. Then also others did come in the forenoon,
42.3419: And some came at the midday — the men to the work;
42.3420: Some came then at nones, that was a late time
42.3421: Of the summer-long day. Some even later did come:
42.3422: At the eleventh hour it was. And the evening arrived
42.3423: And the sun went to rest. Then he himself bade
42.3424: His overseers all, this lord of earls,
42.3425: That they give unto each man his money and pay,
42.3426: To each workman his rightful reward; hight that they were to give first,
42.3427: To those who had been last, the land-folk in coming,
42.3428: The workers to work; and with his words he commended them
42.3429: To give unto those men their mite last of all:
42.3431: To those who had come there first willingly to the work. They weened greatly
42.3432: That they should receive a larger reward,
42.3433: More pay for their work; but to all the people
42.3434: Was equally given. Then were they angered,
42.3435: Were all in a fury, those who came first to that place.
42.3436: “In the morning we came here,” quoth they, “and toiled much of the day
42.3437: In hard work, in labor during the unmeasured heat,
42.3438: In the shining sun. Now thou givest unto us no more of silver
42.3439: Than thou dost to the others, who were here only a while
42.3440: Doing their work.” Then had ready his word
42.3441: The head of the household; quoth that he had not promised them
42.3442: More pay for their work. “What,” quoth he, “I wield here the power
42.3443: To give to each man and all an equal reward,
42.3444: Equal pay for his work.” Thus All-Wielding Christ
42.3445: Meant, however, a mightier thing, when He spake to the men,
42.3446: Gave the folk such a word about the wine-garden,
42.3447: How the workers did come in an unlike way,
42.3448: The men to their work. So shall the bairns of this world,
42.3449: The children of mankind, do in that clear, marvelous light,
42.3450: Men on God’s meadow; some may begin to prepare themselves
42.3451: Already in childhood. Such a spirit is chosen,
42.3452: His will is good, and he avoideth the ways of the world,
42.3453: Leaveth behind him his lusts. He will never let it, his body,
42.3454: Entice him to evil; but eagerly he learneth
42.3455: Wisdom and the law of God, and leaveth behind
42.3456: The will of the devil, the dire foe: so doeth he ever in this world!
42.3457: He is so in this light, until there cometh of life,
42.3458: Of all age the evening; and he fareth thence and up on his way.
42.3459: There his work all will be rewarded,
42.3460: Repaid with good in the realm of God.
42.3461: Thereby was meant those workmen who in the morning
42.3463: Early began with their work, who until evening
42.3464: Did so continue their tasks. Some also came to the work
42.3465: At the midmorn, having squandered the morning
42.3466: And spoiled their day’s duties. So do many dullards,
42.3467: Frivolous folk. For much folly have they done,
42.3468: Varied deeds in their youth. Yea, they have learned wrong,
42.3469: Have learned scornful speech and such words of evil,
42.3471: And after their young years God’s grace doth admonish them
42.3472: Blithe in their breasts. They turn to the better,
42.3473: Both in words and in works, and lead well their lives
42.3474: To their very ends. And rewards come to them
42.3475: For all their good works in the kingdom of God.
42.3476: Some men, however, forsake their sin
42.3477: Not until mid-life, their dire misdeeds, turning their minds
42.3478: To blessed things; and they begin good works through the power of God
42.3479: And repent their wrong talk and rue their bitter deeds
42.3480: Well in their hearts; there cometh to them help from God,
42.3481: So that they believe as long as life keepeth within them:
42.3482: With that they fare forth and receive their reward,
42.3483: A goodly prize from Lord God; nor are there gifts any better.
42.3484: Some begin still later, when they have become old already
42.3485: And their age grows to its end; then their evil works begin to be
42.3486: Loathsome to them in this light; and the learning of God
42.3487: Admonishes them in their minds and their hearts become milder.
42.3488: They do good deeds to the end of their days and reap their reward,
42.3489: The high kingdom of Heaven, when they repair from here,
42.3490: Receive their rewards, as those men did reap theirs
42.3491: Who came to the work in the vineyards there
42.3492: At the none of the day, at the ninth hour indeed.
42.3493: Yet some grow so ancient and still have not atoned for their sins,
42.3494: But increase them with every evil, until their evening doth come unto them,
42.3495: And their world and its winsomeness passeth away; then they begin to dread their reward;
42.3496: Their sins make them sorrowful quite in their hearts. They ponder sadly that they themselves
42.3497: Have done wrongs as long as they possessed their power, nor can they repent,
42.3498: Atone for their deeds by other good deeds done so well — but every day
42.3499: They beat their breasts with their hands and they weep bitter tears,
42.3500: Crying out loud their lament, begging their Holy Lord,
42.3501: The Mighty God that He grow mild; nor doth He permit their minds to despair —
42.3502: So merciful is He, Who wieldeth His might over all. The longing of no man on earth
42.3503: Doth He want to reject; but the Wielder Himself doth grant unto him
42.3504: The holy kingdom of Heaven. Help is come to him later.
42.3505: All shall receive their reward, though they are not come
42.3506: All at one time, the kith of mankind. Still the Lord, mighty and wise,
42.3507: Giveth pay to all people, whosoever receiveth His belief:
42.3508: One kingdom of Heaven: He granteth to all the kith of this earth
42.3509: A reward, to all men. Mighty Christ did mean that,
42.3510: The Best of All Bairns, when He spake His parables
42.3511: Of how the workers came to the wine-gardens,
42.3512: The men, all differently. Yet each did receive
42.3513: Full pay from his liege. Likewise shall the children of earth
42.3514: Receive their reward from Righteous God Himself,
42.3515: Most lovely pay, though some come so late.

43.3516: Then He hight them, His disciples,
43.3517: His followers twelve come closer: they were the truest of men
43.3518: On this earth unto Him. And the Mighty One did explain
43.3519: Unto them one more time what troubles there were
43.3520: Standing before them. “No doubt can there be,” quoth He.
43.3521: Quoth they should go to Jerusalem to the folk of the Jews.
43.3522: “There shall all things be accomplished amid the people
43.3523: And be brought to pass, even as in earlier times
43.3524: Wise men did speak with their words about Me.
43.3525: Among the strong folk there they shall sell Me,
43.3526: The men to the host. Then shall my hands be held bound,
43.3527: My arms and fingers be fettered; full much shall I suffer,
43.3528: Scorn shall I hear, and hurtful speech,
43.3529: Mockery much and many a threat.
43.3530: They will torture Me wounded with the edge of their weapons,
43.3531: Rob me of life. But through the might and the strength of the Lord,
43.3532: I shall arise again on the third day from death to this light.
43.3533: I have not come, however, to the people here,
43.3534: So that the children of men have labor for Me,
43.3535: That the landsmen should serve Me, nor shall I so ask them,
43.3536: Make such demands of the kith of mankind; but I shall be of use
43.3537: Unto them, serving them meekly. And for all those men
43.3538: I shall give My soul. And I Myself
43.3539: Will release them with My life — those who bide here so long —
43.3540: The many of mankind awaiting My help.”
43.3541: Then He fared forward. For He had firmness of spirit
43.3542: Blithe in His breast — the Bairn of the Lord.
43.3543: He would seek in Jerusalem the folk of the Jews:
43.3544: That was his will. Well did He know
43.3545: The hate-raging hearts of the people and the hard strife
43.3546: And their wicked desire. The hordes then went
43.3547: Before Jericho’s bastions, and the Bairn of the Lord
43.3548: Was mighty among the multitude. There men sat by the way;
43.3549: Blind were they both: they had need of betterment —
43.3550: Both these blind men from the Bairn of God,
43.3551: Since for so long they had done without light.
43.3552: They heard the crowd coming and, most curious, did ask —
43.3554: That twain wholly blind — what man, high-born and mighty,
43.3555: Was the first there amind the clans of the folk,
43.3556: The noblest at their head. Then one hero replied unto them,
43.3557: Quoth that Jesus Christ there from Galilee-land,
43.3558: The Best of all Healers, was the highest of all:
43.3559: Foremost was He ’mid His folk. Full joyous were they of heart,
43.3560: Both the blind men, when they knew that God’s Bairn,
43.3561: The Christ, was there ’mid the folk. They called unto Him with their words:
43.3562: Loudly they called Holy Christ, bade that He find them help,
43.3563: “Master and Liege, David’s Son, be Thou mild unto us with Thy deeds.
43.3564: Save us from our distress! As Thou doest for so many
43.3565: Of the kith of mankind; Thou art kind to the multitude!
43.3566: Thou helpest and healest!” Then the host of the people
43.3567: With their words began to forbid them from calling the Wielder,
43.3568: Lord Christ, so loudly. But the two listened not,
43.3569: But ever more and still more over the crowd of the men
43.3570: Did they call most loudly. Christ Healer did stop,
43.3571: The Best of all Bairns, hight that they bring them to Him,
43.3572: Lead them to Him through the land-folk; and spake alike wisely
43.3573: And mildly in front of the many. “Why seek ye help of me here?” quoth He.
43.3574: They bade Him heal them, bade that He make that their eyen be opened,
43.3576: That He lend unto them of this light, that they might see the bustling life
43.3577: Of the folk, might see the shining rays of the sun,
43.3578: This winsome, fair world. And the Wielder did so.
43.3579: And with His hands He did touch them; and He granted His help,
43.3580: That the eyen be opened of the blind men twain,
43.3581: That they might see earth and heaven through God’s holy strength,
43.3583: The light and the land-folk. Then they lauded God,
43.3584: Praised our Lord that they could enjoy the light of this day.
43.3585: And the two went with Him and followed His tracks.
43.3587: A favor was theirs; and the Wielder’s work was made widely known,

44.3589: A token was shown there where the blind men sat
44.3590: By the wayside and endured wicked pain,
44.3591: Most bereft of the light: by that are meant the children of men,
44.3592: All of mankind; how Almighty God
44.3593: In the very beginning through His own great power
44.3595: Adam and Eve. He gave them the upward way,
44.3596: The kingdom of Heaven, but the hated one was yet near,
44.3597: The Fiend with his wiles, and works of wickedness,
44.3598: With sin he deceived them, until they forsook it — the light —
44.3599: Beauty unending. They were banished both
44.3600: To a worse place indeed, to this mid-world here,
44.3601: Endured in the darkness dire human toil,
44.3602: Won unhappy exile, lost their worldly goods.
44.3603: They forgot God’s kingdom, but gave the devils service,
44.3604: The Fiend’s own bairns. Therefore were they blinded of heart,
44.3606: The children of men in this mid-world here,
44.3607: Since they would not know Him, God Mighty and Strong,
44.3608: The Heavenly Lord, who with His hands did create them,
44.3609: Worked them so, as He willed. So was this world cast away,
44.3610: Forced into darkness and into great despair
44.3611: And the dale of death. They did sit along the way
44.3612: Of the Lord, lamenting of heart, begging God’s help;
44.3613: But aid could not be granted unto them before All-Wielding God
44.3614: Would send unto these the True Son of Himself:
44.3615: The Mighty Lord sent Him to this mid-world here
44.3616: To make free the light for the bairns of mankind,
44.3617: Opening for them eternal life, so that they could know
44.3618: The All-Wielding Lord, the God ever Mighty.
44.3619: I may eke tell unto you, if ye are so willed
44.3620: To hope and to hear, so that the Healer’s, the Savior’s strength
44.3621: Ye may recognize well how His coming became
44.3622: Great help to the many in this mid-world here;
44.3623: What He, our Master, did mean — so many a thing
44.3624: With His acts and His deeds, and why that well-known town
44.3625: Is hight Jericho, the one which standeth there in Judea,
44.3626: Made well with its walls. That is named for the moon,
44.3627: For that bright constellation: it cannot escape its time,
44.3628: But on every day it doeth one or the other:
44.3629: It waneth or waxeth. So do in the world,
44.3630: On this mid-earth here, the bairns of mankind.
44.3631: They fare forth and follow, and from them the old die away,
44.3632: And the young come again and are born. And the children of men
44.3633: Wax great until Weird once more taketh them out of the world.
44.3634: This the Bairn of God did mean, as He left the bastions,
44.3635: The Good Christ from Jericho, that the children of men
44.3636: Would not be healed from their blindness, not see the bright beam
44.3637: And beauty eternal, before He Himself had assumed
44.3638: Man’s body and flesh in this mid-world here.
44.3640: Then the children of men, who before sat in sin
44.3641: And in suffering, bereft of their sight,
44.3642: Enduring the darkness — they did perceive and did know
44.3643: That to this folk the Healer was come from the kingdom of Heaven,
44.3644: Christ the Best of All Kings. They could soon recognize Him,
44.3645: Had perceived His path. Then the people cried out so greatly,
44.3646: The men to the Mighty God, that He became mildly inclined,
44.3647: The Wielder, unto them. But their wickedness kept them
44.3648: Most dreadfully, the dire sins, which once they had done,
44.3649: Prevented their believing; but they could not prevent
44.3650: The will of the people. For unto All-Wielding God
44.3651: They did call most loudly, until He did grant unto them wholeness,
44.3652: So that they might see the life never ending,
44.3653: Eternal light open before them and journey on
44.3654: To the bright dwelling above. So did the blind men mean
44.3655: Who at Jericho-burg called to God’s Bairn,
44.3656: Who did cry aloud that He grant them healing,
44.3657: Light in this life. But a great lot of the folk
44.3658: Who stood in His way, both before and behind Him,
44.3659: Kept Him away with their words. So do those weighted with sin
44.3660: Unto the kith of mankind in this mid-world here.
44.3661: Hear ye now how the blind men acted after they had been healed,
44.3662: So that they could see the light of the sun —
44.3663: Hear what they then did: they went along with their Master,
44.3664: Followed in His footsteps, spake full many a word,
44.3665: Lauding the Lord’s Herdsman: so do the bairns of the land-folk still
44.3666: Widely here in this world, since All-Wielding Christ
44.3667: Hath illuminated them with His lesson, granted them light everlasting,
44.3668: Granted the kingdom of God to every good man,
44.3669: The high, heavenly light and His help to that end
44.3670: To whosoever worketh to follow along on His way.

45.3671: Then Christ the Savior the Good One, soon came
45.3672: Near to Jerusalem. And now there approached Him
45.3673: A great multitude all of good mind toward Him.
45.3674: They received Him with joy, and before Him they strewed
45.3675: The way with their garments, their weeds; and with herb-roots,
45.3676: With bright colored blossoms and the branches of trees they did strew it,
45.3677: The field, with fair palms; and it so then came to pass
45.3678: That the Son of God did wish to go
45.3679: To that most hated town. Joyous, the multitude
45.3680: Of the people surrounded Him and raised songs of praise,
45.3681: The folk, all willingly: they said thanks to the Wielder
45.3682: That He Himself was come, He — Son of David —
45.3683: To visit the world-folk. Then Wielding Christ,
45.3684: The Good, saw Jerusalem. The Best of All Men
45.3685: Beheld the town’s bastions and the buildings of Jews,
45.3686: The high-horned halls and God’s house as well,
45.3687: The most winsome of temples. Then within Him welled
45.3688: His thoughts ’gainst His heart. And the Holy Bairn
45.3689: Could not help weeping, but troubled of heart
45.3690: With many words He did speak — for His spirit was sore.
45.3691: “Woe unto thee, Jerusalem,” He wailed, “that the word of thy Weird
45.3692: Thou knowest not, nor what still shall come over thee,
45.3693: How thou shalt be surrounded by the strength of a host,
45.3694: How grim-minded men shall besiege thee mightily —
45.3695: The foe with its folk. For thou shalt never find peace
45.3696: With these men, or protection. Many will bring thee
45.3697: The weapons’s point and its edge, bring thee words of war,
45.3698: Consume thy folk-clans with flames of fire,
45.3699: Lay waste to thy bailiwicks; fell these high walls
45.3700: To the earth itself. Not a rock will stand upright,
45.3701: No stone on another. But all the townships surrounding
45.3702: Jerusalem will be desolation for the folk of the Jews,
45.3703: Since they cannot see that their time draweth nearer;
45.3704: But their souls are in doubt, and they ween not at all,
45.3705: That the strength of the Wielder is visited on them.”
45.3706: Then the Lord of Mankind went with the multitude
45.3707: Into the bright borough. When the Bairn of God
45.3708: Went into Jerusalem with His host of men,
45.3709: Was there with His vassals, there waxed the greatest of all songs:
45.3710: With such loud voices they sang holy words.
45.3711: Lo, the crowds of the folk did laud the word of the Lord,
45.3712: The Best of all Bairns. The burg was astir,
45.3713: The people were frightened and asked first of all
45.3714: Who was that who was come there with the crowd,
45.3715: With that multitude great. Then spake a man in reply:
45.3716: Quoth that this was Jesus Christ from Galilee-land,
45.3717: Who was come as a Savior from the city of Nazareth,
45.3718: Wise Soothsayer and Prophet, as a Help to the people.
45.3719: Then the Jews, who had a grudge against Him already,
45.3720: Became hate-filled of heart and hurting of spirit,
45.3721: Because the people did give unto Him so much praise,
45.3722: Did love so their Master. The dull-minded folk did go forth,
45.3723: So that they might speak words with All-Wielding Christ.
45.3724: Bade that He hight His disciples be silent here,
45.3725: Bade Him not to permit them, the people, to praise Him
45.3726: So much with their words: “It doth worry this folk,” quoth they,
45.3727: “These burghers here.” Then again spake God’s Bairn:
45.3728: “If ye keep the children of men,” quoth He, Lord Christ,
45.3729: “From praising with words the All-Wielder’s might,
45.3730: Then shall the stones still shout it forth
45.3731: To the kinship of men, and the strong, tall cliffs,
45.3732: Before it is left undone; but that He shall be lauded
45.3733: Wide and far in the world.” Then He went into the temple.
45.3734: He entered God’s house. There He found a horde of the Jews:
45.3735: There were countless men, so many together,
45.3736: Who had chosen for themselves a selling-place in there,
45.3737: Haggling o’er multitudes of small matters: and money-changers did sit
45.3738: Within the temple. For transactions daily
45.3739: They held it ready. Then God’s Bairn was enraged,
45.3741: Drove them out of the temple far; quoth that it was a far righter deed,
45.3742: If the children of Israel should come there to pray:
45.3743: “And here in this house let them pray for help,
45.3744: That the Master of Victories make them free from sin —
45.3745: Rather than that thieves should bargain their things in the house,
45.3746: And villainous men make their usurious deals,
45.3747: The worst of all wrongs. No whit of honor
45.3748: Know ye in God’s house, ye folk of the Jews.”
45.3749: So did the Lord All-Powerful empty and order
45.3750: The holy house; and of help this was
45.3751: To the many of mankind, who had heard of His might,
45.3752: Of His strength from afar. And they came there faring
45.3753: Over the long, long way. So many a one weak of limb,
45.3754: So many of the halt were healed, and the crippled of hand,
45.3755: And the blind were made whole. So did the Bairn of God
45.3756: Do unto the willing folk, since He wields might over all,
45.3757: Over the lives of men and their lands as well.

46.3758: Before the temple He stood, Strong Wielding Christ,
46.3759: The Land-Warder Beloved, and lo, He took heed
46.3760: Of the hearts of the people, and their will; He saw a huge host
46.3761: Bringing great treasures to the well-known house,
46.3762: Giving unto it gold, goodly webs of silk,
46.3763: Precious stones and jewels. Wisely perceived He,
46.3764: Our Lord Christ, all this. There did come also a widow,
46.3765: A poor, ill-weirded woman; and she went to the altar,
46.3766: And in that treasure-house she put down just two
46.3767: Small coins of bronze; she was simple of heart,
46.3768: A woman of good will. Then spake All-Wielding Christ,
46.3769: The Man, to His followers; quoth that a far greater gift
46.3770: Had she brought to the altar than any other son of mankind.
46.3771: “If wealthy men,” He did tell them, “bring a treasure-trove,
46.3772: An honor here to the house, still they have left more at home
46.3773: Of the wealth they have won. Not so did this widow,
46.3774: When she gave all she had upon this altar:
46.3775: All the wealth she had won. Not a whit did she leave,
46.3776: No goods in her garden. Therefore is her gift more
46.3777: And worthier to the Wielder, since she gave with such will
46.3778: To the house of God. So shall she receive goodly reward,
46.3779: Most long-lasting return, since she possessed such belief.”
46.3780: So I discovered that All-Wielding Christ
46.3781: Taught them with words each day in the temple,
46.3782: The Master of Mankind. And many stood ’round Him,
46.3783: A great folk of the Jews, and hearkened to the good word,
46.3784: The sweet word He spake. Some were so blessed,
46.3785: Some men from the multitude, that in their minds and their hearts
46.3786: They began to learn and accept the lesson which the Warder of Lands,
46.3787: The Child of the Lord, did speak in His pictures.
46.3788: To some again the lesson of Christ was all loathsome,
46.3789: The All-Wielder’s word. Of hate-willed heart
46.3790: Were all those who were the greatest among those governing,
46.3791: The princes of the people. These evil men did plan
46.3792: Trickery and snares with their words; they had taken adversaries
46.3793: To help them, these men of the highest one;
46.3794: were thanes of Herod — he who was present
46.3795: with an evil intent to overhear all they said —
46.3796: If the people did capture Him, that they might throw Him in chains,
46.3797: Might lay leg-fetters around His limbs —
46.3798: Around Him, the Christ without sin. The crowd did come toward Him,
46.3799: Bitter-minded, to speak unto God’s Bairn,
46.3800: The evil adversaries, to address Him with words.
46.3801: “What, Thou art a sayer of law,” quoth they, “unto all the people?
46.3802: Thou revealest so wonderous much truth. Nor is it of worth unto Thee
46.3803: To conceal aught from a man because of his might;
46.3804: But ever Thou speakest only that which is right,
46.3805: And with Thy teaching Thou leadest the crowds of the land-folk
46.3806: Upon God’s way. Among the people not a whit of reproach
46.3807: Can one find in Thee. Now we shall ask Thee:
46.3808: That rich and great ruler — what right doth he have?
46.3809: Caesar from Rome, who seeketh his tithe
46.3810: From the clansmen here and hath counted out
46.3811: What monies each man of us shall pay every year,
46.3812: How much of the head-tax. Say, what in Thy heart hast Thou thought?
46.3813: Is this right or not? Counsel Thy countrymen well,
46.3814: For we have need of Thy teachings.” They wanted His answer,
46.3815: But well did He know their will. “Why, ye liars all
46.3816: Against truth,” quoth He, “do ye tempt Me so boldly?”
46.3817: But it shall be of no help, no advantage to you.
46.3818: That ye deceivers seek to capture me secretly.”
46.3819: He commanded that they carry forth the coins for the showing,
46.3821: “Which are your duty to give.” The Jews did bring out
46.3822: A coin of silver; and many did see
46.3823: How indeed it was minted; in the middle appeared
46.3824: The image of Caesar that they could clearly recognize,
46.3825: The pictured head of their lord. Then Holy Christ did question them
46.3826: As to whose likeness lay in this picture.
46.3827: They replied that it was the world emperor there
46.3828: From the city of Rome, “who rules o’er this realm,
46.3829: Wielding power here in this world.” “That will I verily,” quoth He,
46.3830: “Say unto you, that ye give unto him his own,
46.3831: To the world-lord his wealth, and to All-Wielding God
46.3832: Bring that which is His. That should be your souls,
46.3833: The spirits of men.” Then the minds of the Jews were made
46.3834: Small in the gathering. The scoundrels assembled
46.3835: Could not win out with their words, as was indeed their will,
46.3836: To ensnare Him, since the Peace-Bairn of God
46.3837: Warded off their wickedness, and He verily
46.3838: Said unto them a soothy thing; still they were not so blessed,
46.3839: That they could receive it and it could then be of benefit unto them.

47.3840: But they would not leave off, but instead ordered a woman led forth
47.3841: In front of the crowd; she had committed sin,
47.3842: Had truly done wrong; the woman had been taken
47.3843: In adultery and had forefeited her life,
47.3844: So that the bairns of mankind could deprive her of breath —
47.3845: Lay claim to her age: for so was the law.
47.3846: They began to question Him; the bold people there —
47.3847: Wicked they with their words: what they should do with this wife:
47.3848: Whether to kill her by torment or leave her quick and alive —
47.3849: Or what judgment He would deal for such a deed as this.
47.3850: “Thou wist,” quoth they, “that Moses commanded these many
47.3851: With words of truth that any woman whosoever
47.3852: Is found in adultery must forfeit her life,
47.3853: And that with their hands the landsmen will unlife her
47.3854: By throwing sharp stones. Now Thou mayest see her here standing,
47.3855: Ensnared in her sin: say what Thou wilt!”
47.3856: His foes had the wish to ensnare Him with words.
47.3857: If he were to say that they should indeed let her live,
47.3858: Should permit her to leave here in peace, then would the people of Jews
47.3859: Say that He had opposed their ancient law,
47.3860: The people’s own land-right. If He hight them rob her of life,
47.3861: The maid before the many; then would they say that no mildness of heart
47.3862: He bore in His breast, such as God’s Bairn should indeed possess.
47.3863: So for whichever word Holy Christ would speak
47.3864: To the people, the many, they would then punish Him,
47.3865: Would deal out His doom. This our Lord Christ did perceive.
47.3866: Right well did He know the turn of mind of these men,
47.3867: Their wicked wills, when He spoke then to the folk,
47.3868: To all the earls gathered around. “Which of you,” quoth He
47.3869: “Standeth here without evil sin? Let him himself go to her
47.3870: And with his hands be the first of the earls here
47.3871: To pelt her with stones.” Then the Jews stood about,
47.3872: Had their thoughts and were silent. Not a single thane
47.3873: Could find opposition unto this speech.
47.3874: And each man was reminded of his own evil-mindedness,
47.3875: Of his own dark sins; not a one was sure enough
47.3876: That after this word he would venture to throw
47.3877: A stone against the woman; but they left her standing alone inside.
47.3879: The grim-minded people of the Jews did go thence,
47.3880: One after another, until there was not a single one
47.3881: Of the folk of the foe standing before them
47.3882: Who would have wanted to rob this woman of her years and her life.
47.3883: Then I discovered that the Peace Bairn of God, the Best of all Men,
47.3884: Did question her. “Whence came this Jewish folk?” quoth He,
47.3885: “Thine opponents here, who have accused thee to Me — ?
47.3886: Those who today have wanted to torment thee most terribly,
47.3887: To bereave thee of life — have they done one whit of harm unto thee?”
47.3888: The the woman gave answer again unto Him,
47.3889: Quoth that through the holy help of the Savior no one had harmed her
47.3890: To reward her sins. Then spake again All-Wielding Christ,
47.3892: The Master of Mankind. “Nor shall I do harm to thee,” He made reply,
47.3893: “But go thou hence, hale and unhurt, and let it be
47.3894: The care of thy heart, that henceforth thou sinnest no more.”
47.3895: The Holy Bairn of the Lord had helped her indeed,
47.3896: Had protected her life. Then the people of Jews stood there,
47.3897: As bent on evil, as they had been in the beginning,
47.3898: Of wicked intent and wanting to continue their word-strife,
47.3899: Pondering, how to pursue it with the Peace-Bairn of God.
47.3900: They had put doubts in the faith of the people:
47.3901: The little folk standing about would far liefer
47.3902: Have accomplished His will, the word of God’s Bairn,
47.3903: Have done even so, as their Lord did bid them.
47.3904: They strove toward right better than those men with riches,
47.3905: Held Him as their Lord; yea, as the Heaven-King even,
47.3906: And followed Him gladly. Then God’s Son did go
47.3907: Within the temple. The people surrounded Him truly,
47.3908: The multitude of he men. He stood in their midst,
47.3909: Taught them, the land-folk, with words of light
47.3910: And in a voice loud and bright: there was great listening,
47.3911: And many a thane stood silent; and He bade them thusly:
47.3912: “Whosoever of the people be oppressed with thirst —
47.3913: Let him come unto Me,” quoth He, “and drink every day
47.3914: From that sweet spring. So may I say unto you,
47.3915: Whosoever of the bairns of mankind hath believed in Me
47.3916: Fast and firmly among the folk — that from him shall flow
47.3917: The living flood, flow from his body
47.3918: The gushing water, the great well-springs
47.3919: That are springs of life coming thence. This word shall come true,
47.3920: Shall be done unto all folk, whosoever hath believed rightly in Me.”
47.3922: The High King of Heaven did mean the Holy Ghost,
47.3923: How the children of men should receive Him,
47.3924: Light and reason and the life everlasting,
47.3925: The high kingdom of Heaven and Holy God’s grace.

48.3926: Then the people began to quarrel about the teachings of Christ
48.3927: And about His words; haughty men stood about,
48.3928: Proud minded Jews — and the spake much mockery,
48.3929: Heaped scorn upon Him, saying that they could hear full well
48.3930: That angry and wicked thought did speak out of Him.
48.3931: “Now He doth teach evil,” quoth they, “with every word.”
48.3932: And again others did speak: “Ye should not reproach
48.3933: Him who teacheth,” quoth they, “for words of life come
48.3934: Mighty out of His mouth, and He worketh many a thing,
48.3935: Many a wonder here in this world: that is no wicked deed,
48.3936: Clearly not the might of the Fiend, else could not such good be accomplished by Him,
48.3937: But surely it cometh from All-Wielding God,
48.3938: From His strength all rightly. That may ye well recognize
48.3939: In His words of truth, that He wieldeth power
48.3940: Over all the earth.” Then His opposers longed
48.3941: To take Him captive straightway or to cast stones on Him,
48.3942: Had they not feared there the multitude of the folk,
48.3943: Been afraid of the people. Then spake the Peace Bairn of God.
48.3944: “Much good have I shown you,” quoth He, “from God Himself,
48.3945: Both in words and in works. Now would ye give me wicked reward
48.3946: With your strong, hard hearts and pelt me with stones
48.3947: And bereave me of life.” Then again the people replied,
48.3948: His dire opponents: “We do this not because of Thy deeds,” quoth they,
48.3949: “That we should want to deprive Thee of life.
48.3950: But we do so because of Thy words, since Thou speakest such wickedness,
48.3951: Since Thou dost praise Thyself and sayest such blasphemy,
48.3952: Proclaiming before these Jews that Thou art God Himself,
48.3953: The Mighty Master and Lord; and Thou art merely a man like us,
48.3954: Art from these clans.” Then All-Wielding Christ
48.3955: No longer wished to list to the scorn of the Jews,
48.3956: The will of these wicked ones. But from the temple He went
48.3957: Over Jordan’s stream. His disciples He had with Him,
48.3958: Those blessed thanes, who forever there tarried
48.3959: To accomplish His will. Another folk He did seek;
48.3960: The Lord Himself did work there, as was ever His wont,
48.3961: Teaching the land-folk: those who so wanted belief
48.3962: In His Holy word. Each man should do well so ever
48.3963: If he accepteth and receiveth it into his heart.
48.3964: Then I did hear there were come to Holy Christ
48.3965: Heralds from Bethany, and they said unto God’s Bairn
48.3966: That women had sent them there on this errand —
48.3967: Mary and Martha, maidens most comely,
48.3968: Such winsome women. Both He knew well.
48.3969: They were sisters twain, whom in His spirit
48.3970: He Himself did love for their mildness of heart,
48.3971: These women for their goodly will. Most verily they sent
48.3972: From Bethany for Him; for their brother was bedfast —
48.3973: Lazarus he — and they feared for his life.
48.3974: They bade that He come, All-Wielding Christ,
48.3975: The Holy, to help them. As soon as He heard them
48.3976: Speak about the sick man, He gave answer straightway,
48.3977: Said that Lazarus’ sickness, though so serious it was,
48.3978: Would not do him to death. “But,” He did say, “the love of the Lord
48.3979: Shall here be accomplished. Nor shall any harm come unto him
48.3980: The Son of the Lord did Himself stay there
48.3981: Two nights and two days. The time then drew near,
48.3982: That He teach these people the power He had,
48.3983: Teach the Jewish folk there in Jerusalem.
48.3984: Then the Son of the Lord did say to His thanes
48.3985: That He would again seek out the Jews across the Jordan.
48.3986: But His disciples did speak to Him in reply:
48.3987: “For what reason, good Master, goest Thou so gladly,”
48.3988: Quoth they, “over there? Was it not recently there,
48.3989: That they thought to kill Thee because of Thy words?
48.3990: Did want to pelt Thee with strong, sharp stones? Now Thou strivest to go again,
48.3991: Among that fight-seeking folk. Thou hast foes enough,
48.3992: Overhaughty earls.” Then one of the twelve,
48.3993: Thomas, did speak — he was truly an excellent man,
48.3994: A loyal thane of his Lord. “Let us never reproach His deeds,”
48.3995: Quoth he, “nor reproach His will. But rather we should remain with Him,
48.3996: Should suffer with our Lord. For that is the choice of a thane:
48.3997: That he standeth steadfast with his Liege together,
48.3998: Doth die with Him at his doom. Let us all do so therefore;
48.3999: Let us follow His path, nor let our lives
48.4000: Be worth aught against His, unless we may die
48.4001: In this host with our Lord. So honor will live after us,
48.4002: A good word before the kinships of men.” So the disciples of Christ,
48.4003: The aethling-born earls, became all of one mind,
48.4004: Holding the will of their Lord. Then Holy Christ Himself
48.4005: Did say to His disciples, that a sleep unto death
48.4006: Lay on Lazarus on his couch. “He hath given up the light,
48.4007: Doth slumber on, on his bedstead. Now we shall fare on the way
48.4008: To awaken him there, so that he may again see this world
48.4009: Alive, see the light: Then your belief will henceforth
48.4010: Be strengthened still more. So went He hence o’er the flood;
48.4011: The Good Son of God did go with His vassals
48.4012: There to Bethany — the Bairn of the Lord
48.4013: Himself with His disciples — there where the sisters twain,
48.4014: Mary and Martha, their minds filled with care,
48.4015: Were sitting most sadly. Here was gathered together
48.4016: Much folk of the Jews from Jerusalem,
48.4017: Who wanted to comfort the women with words,
48.4018: So that they would lament less the death of Lazarus,
48.4019: The loss of the child-young man. Then as the Warder of Lands
48.4020: Did go through the garden, it spread around that God’s Bairn
48.4021: Had now arrived, and that He, so mighty,
48.4022: Did tarry outside the castle. Then the twain, the women,
48.4023: Were most joyous indeed, when they heard that the Wielder,
48.4024: The Peace-Bairn of God, was now come unto them.

49.4025: ’Twas the most wondrous joy for the woman to hear
49.4026: Of the Lord’s coming and of the word of Christ.
49.4028: Her mind filled with care, Martha did go to the One so Mighty,
49.4029: Lamenting, exchanged words and spake with the Wielder,
49.4030: Her heart muchly troubled. “Had you, my Master,”
49.4031: Quoth she, “been nearer, O Best of Saviors,
49.4032: Healer so good, I would never have needed to suffer such hurt,
49.4033: Such bitter care in my breast, and my brother would not now be dead,
49.4034: Lazarus, far from the light; but he would still be alive,
49.4035: Filled with this life. But I, my Lord, do believe
49.4036: Most steadfastly in Thee, Thou Best of all Teachers.
49.4037: If Thou would’st so bid the Bright Lord for aught,
49.4038: He would grant it straightway; Almighty God
49.4039: Would fulfill Thy will.” Then spake again All-Wielding Christ,
49.4040: Answering the woman. “Let not thy heart within thee”
49.4041: Quoth He, “become darkened, but I may make known unto thee
49.4042: In words of truth, that thou shalt have neither worry nor doubt,
49.4043: But that thy brother shall at the bidding of God,
49.4044: Through the might of the Lord arise from the dead
49.4045: In his own body itself.” “So have I believed,” quoth she,
49.4046: That it will thus come to pass when the world doth end,
49.4048: That he shall arise then again from the earth
49.4049: On the day of his doom: then the dead will become quick
49.4050: Through the might of the Lord; and so many of mankind
49.4051: Will arise from their rest.” Then Christ the Ruler did speak,
49.4052: The Almighty did utter open words to the women;
49.4053: That He Himself was the Son of the Lord,
49.4054: For the bairns of mankind both a light and a life
49.4055: For the resurrection. “Never shall he die,
49.4056: Take leave of this life, who believeth in Me.
49.4057: Though the bairns of men do bury him deeply
49.4058: And cover him with earth, he is not yet dead:
49.4059: The flesh is consigned to the soil, but the spirit is saved,
49.4060: And the soul is still sound.” Then the good wife again did speak
49.4061: To Him with her words: “I verily believe,” quoth she,
49.4062: “That Thou are the Christ, the Son of God. Well may one see this,
49.4063: May know from Thy words that Thou wieldest power
49.4064: Through this holy creation over heaven and earth.”
49.4065: Then I discovered that the other woman did come,
49.4066: Mary, with care-filled mind: and behind her came many
49.4067: Of the folk of the Jews gathered together. And to the Bairn of God
49.4068: She, saddened of spirit, did say, why she was sorrowed
49.4069: With such grief in her heart; she lamented with groans
49.4070: The losing of Lazarus, of the beloved man,
49.4071: Giving forth mournful moans, until the Almighty’s Bairn
49.4072: Was indeed moved in His heart; and hot tears streamed,
49.4073: Welling up as He wept. And to the woman He spake,
49.4074: Hight that they should lead Him, there where Lazarus was lying
49.4075: Consigned to the soil. A stone lay above him;
49.4076: A hard boulder did cover him. The Holy Christ hight
49.4077: Them remove the rock so that right well He might see the corpse,
49.4078: Might gaze on the body. Then despite the folk gathered ’round,
49.4079: Martha could not help making known the care of her mind, and to the Mighty One
49.4080: She did speak, “My Lord so Good,” quoth she, “If one taketh away the stone,
49.4081: Removeth this rock, then I ween, it will reek from there.
49.4082: An unsweet stench will come forth, if I may so say
49.4083: Unto Thee with words of truth — that there is no doubt of that —
49.4084: Four days and four nights hath it been, since he was consigned
49.4085: To his grave there.” He gave reply unto her,
49.4086: The All-Wielder unto the woman. “Why, I have verily told thee before,” quoth He,
49.4087: “If thou hast will to believe, then will it not be long
49.4088: Before thou shalt know the strength of the Lord,
49.4089: The great might of God.” Then many did go
49.4090: And hove up the hard stone. Then Holy Christ did gaze
49.4091: Upward with His eyes and said thanks unto Him
49.4092: Who had shaped this world. “Since Thou hearest My word,” quoth He,
49.4093: “Thyself Lord of Victory, I will know that Thou doest so ever.
49.4094: But I do so only for the great folk of the Jews,
49.4095: That they may verily know that Thou hast sent Me into this world
49.4096: To teach them, this land-folk.” Then He called unto Lazarus
49.4097: With a loud, strong voice and hight him stand up
49.4098: And go forth from the grave. And his ghost did return
49.4099: And enter his body. And he began moving his limbs:
49.4100: He stirred ’neath his weeds; but he was still wound in them,
49.4101: Held tight by his shroud. The All-Wielding Christ did hight
49.4102: That they give him help. Then men did go
49.4103: And unwound his weeds. Winsome, he rose
49.4104: Lazarus to this light. His life had been granted him,
49.4105: So that he might spend the fated span of his days
49.4106: Henceforth in peace. The twain rejoiced full well,
49.4107: Mary and Martha; nor may anyone
49.4108: Truly say otherwise than that the sisters twain
49.4109: Were indeed happy of heart. Many did wonder,
49.4110: Those of the Jewish folk, when they did see him
49.4111: Rise sound from his grave — him, whom sickness had taken before
49.4112: And whom they had dug deep down into the earth,
49.4113: Him, cut loose from his life. Henceforth he could live,
49.4114: Hale and sound in his home. So may the Heaven-King’s,
49.4115: May God’s great power protect the life
49.4116: Of so many a man, and may help him ’gainst the hate
49.4117: Of the Fiend — Holy God, to whomsoever He giveth His grace.

50.4118: Then the minds of so many of mankind and their thoughts as well
50.4119: Were won for the Christ, when they themselves did see
50.4120: His holy works, since in this world such wonders
