50.4121: Had never before come to pass. There were also some people,
50.4122: Such strong-minded men — the might of God they had no will
50.4123: To acknowledge openly, but against His great power
50.4124: They fought with their words: for the Wielder’s message,
50.4125: His lesson, was so loathsome to them, that they sought other landsmen
50.4126: In Jerusalem — there where the Jews
50.4127: Had their home and inheritance, their foremost town —
50.4128: There they gathered a great crowd of grim-minded folk,
50.4129: And of Christ’s work they did tell them; quoth that they had seen him quick
50.4130: And alive — with their own eyes had seen the earl who had been in the earth,
50.4131: Consigned to a grave four nights and four days,
50.4132: Had been dead and buried, until He with His deeds,
50.4133: With His words had awakened him to see this world once again.
50.4134: This was so hateful to these haughty men,
50.4135: To the clansmen of Jews, that they commanded their minions,
50.4136: Their people to gather together and to turn the crowd
50.4137: Against Him — the great host; and against Mighty Christ
50.4138: They took counsel in whispers; “That is not good advice,” quoth they,
50.4139: “That we should endure it. Too many indeed of the folk
50.4140: Believe in His lessons. Then the landsmen will come
50.4141: And attack us with horsemen, and our overseers
50.4142: Will be warriors from Rome. Then bereft of our realm,
50.4143: Must we live and suffer the loss of our lives,
50.4144: We heroes, the loss of our heads.” Then spake a hoary man
50.4145: Over the crowd of the men: among the clans
50.4146: Within the borough was he bishop of the people.
50.4147: Kaiphas was he called, and by the kinsmen of Jews
50.4149: He had been chosen this year to take charge of God’s house,
50.4150: Be the warder, then, of the temple. “Methinks ’tis a wonder,” said he,
50.4151: “O praiseworth people — ye are informed of a plenty:
50.4152: Why is it that ye yet do not know, O ye folk of the Jews,
50.4153: That ’tis better counsel for the bairns of mankind
50.4154: That one relieve one man of his life
50.4155: And that he dieth most bloodily through your deeds,
50.4156: Forsaketh this life for the folk-clans here,
50.4157: Than that all the landsmen should forever be lost.”
50.4158: But it was not his will that he verily did speak
50.4159: Forth to the land-folk for the weal of mankind,
50.4160: Proclaimed to the people; but from God’s power it came
50.4161: Through his holy office, since he had to care for God’s house
50.4162: In Jerusalem there — he, the temple’s warder.
50.4164: Therefore the people’s bishop did speak, how the Bairn of God
50.4165: Was to save all the children of earth with His single spirit,
50.4166: With His own very life: and for all the land-folk
50.4167: That was a great gain, for He gathered the heathen,
50.4168: All-Wielding Christ fetched the men, as He willed.
50.4169: Then those most haughty men became of one mind,
50.4170: The clansmen of Jews, and in their crowd they did speak —
50.4171: This far-known people, that they permit no doubt in their minds!
50.4172: But whosoever might find Him here among the folk —
50.4173: He should straightway make Him his Captive, should bring Him
50.4174: Forth to the diet of clans; quoth that they no longer cared
50.4175: To suffer that one man should thus seduce them,
50.4176: The world-folk all. But All-Wielding Christ knew full well
50.4177: Even the thoughts in the minds of these men there,
50.4178: Their hate-angry hearts; for nothing is ever hidden
50.4179: To Him in this mid-world here; thereafter He had no wish
50.4180: To appear in the open among the many, among the earls
50.4181: Of the folk, among the Jews. For the Son of God
50.4182: Was biding that bright, glorious time which would be unto Him,
50.4183: When He would endure great pain for these peoples,
50.4184: Torment indeed for the folk of the earth. For the time of His doom
50.4185: He knew full well. Thereupon our Lord went forth.
50.4186: All-Wielding Christ did abide in Ephraim.
50.4187: The Holy Lord did dwell in the high-walled city
50.4188: with His vassals there; until it was His will
50.4189: To return to Bethany once more with His mighty host,
50.4190: With His disciples good. The Jews did discuss
50.4192: His every word: “This bodeth no good,” quoth they,
50.4193: “For the council of our realm. Though we do speak rightly,
50.4194: Still our cause cannot thrive one whit, since He can turn them,
50.4195: The folk to His will; and all the world followeth Him,
50.4196: The landsmen for His lesson, so that we may do no whit
50.4197: Of harm unto Him, here in front of the folk.”

51.4198: Thus the Bairn of God did go into Bethany
51.4199: Six nights before it should hap — that gathering there
51.4200: In Jerusalem of the Jewish folk.
51.4201: For the hallowed day they should keep for the holy tide,
51.4203: The Passover of Jews. God’s Son did tarry
51.4204: Mighty among the many. A great crowd of men,
51.4205: Of folk did wait for His words. There two women approached Him,
51.4206: Mary and Martha; with mildness of spirit
51.4207: They served Him most humbly. The Master of Peoples
51.4208: Gave them long-lasting reward. He released them from all that is loathsome,
51.4209: Absolved them from sin; and He Himself did bid
51.4210: That they should fare forth in peace against the Foe,
51.4211: The women with His good permission; To His will had they turned
51.4212: Ever their service. Then All-Wielding Christ
51.4213: Fared forth with His people, the Lord of the Folk,
51.4214: To Jerusalem, where dwelt the Jews,
51.4215: All those hate-filled leaders, who there spent the holy time
51.4216: Warding the temple. There were there many world-folk
51.4217: Of most mighty clans; and they cared not to hear
51.4218: The word of the Christ, nor had they a whit
51.4219: Of love in their breasts for the Bairn of God;
51.4220: But rather they were a proud, a wrath-filled people,
51.4221: An angry minded clan of mankind; and they had murderous thoughts
51.4222: And evil within them: all wrongly they understood
51.4223: The teachings of Christ, wanted to kill Him, the All-Strong,
51.4224: Because of His words. But there were so many of the world-folk,
51.4225: So many of the earlships about Him all the day long.
51.4226: The small folk did surround Him for the sake of His sweet word,
51.4227: With so many people all the day, so that His enemies
51.4228: Among the folk-clans feared to make Him their captive,
51.4229: Avoiding Him there amid the many. Now Mighty Christ
51.4230: Did stand inside of the temple and said many a word
51.4231: All the day long, until the light,
51.4232: Till the sun went to rest. Then many did wend there way
51.4233: Homeward, that kith of mankind. There was there a famous mountain
51.4234: Outside near the city — so broad it was and so high,
51.4235: Green and so fair: it was hight by the Jewish folk
51.4236: The Mountain of Olives. Upon that did He go,
51.4237: The Savior Christ, where the night did surround Him.
51.4238: He was there with His disciples, though not one of the Jews
51.4239: Did actually know this, since already He had entered the temple —
51.4240: The Lord of the Land-folk — when the light came up from the east,
51.4241: Received the clanships and said much unto them
51.4242: In words of truth, so that not one in this world,
51.4243: On this mid-earth here — not a single man is so wise,
51.4244: Not one of the bairns of mankind, that he could repeat to the end
51.4245: All the teachings He told in the temple there,
51.4246: Did speak in the holy house; and with His words He hight them
51.4247: To make themselves ready for the realm of God,
51.4248: All men everywhere whosoever they be, so that on that best-known day
51.4249: They may receive the love of their Lord.
51.4250: He told them the sins they had committed and straightway commanded
51.4251: That they atone for their deeds. Told them that in their hearts
51.4252: They should love God’s light and leave behind them all wrongs,
51.4255: And take it into their hearts. Quoth that the kingdom of Heaven,
51.4256: The richest of goods was really for them. Then right many of the men
51.4257: Were turned to His will, when they heard God’s word,
51.4258: Heard the Holy Message of the King of Heaven,
51.4259: Acknowledged great power and the Master’s coming
51.4260: And the help of the Lord; yea, that the heavenly kingdom,
51.4261: That salvation was grown nearer, and the grace of God
51.4262: For the bairns of mankind. But some were so angered —
51.4263: Some of the Jewish folk had such grimness of mind,
51.4264: Such hate-filled hearts cared not for his teaching ,
51.4265: They wanted not to believe His word, but waged great battle
51.4266: Against Christ’s might: because of their wretched contention
51.4267: The folk could not find it — belief in Him, clear and firm.
51.4268: The grace was not granted them to be given the kingdom of Heaven.
51.4270: Then God’s Son did go, and His disciples all gladly with Him;
51.4271: The Wielder went from the temple, as He so willed it.
51.4272: And again the Bairn of God did go up on the mountain,
51.4273: And He sat with His disciples and said much unto them
51.4274: In words of truth. They began to talk with Him about the temple,
51.4275: The men about God’s house, quoth that no goodlier
51.4276: Building had ever been builded by the hands of earls,
51.4277: By the efforts of man, never such temple erected
51.4278: With such great power. Then the Rich Prince did speak,
51.4279: The High King of Heaven — and the others did hear Him —
51.4280: “I can yet tell unto you,” quoth He, “that the time shall soon come
51.4281: That no stone shall be left standing upon any other,
51.4282: But it shall fall to the earth and fire shall devour it,
51.4283: The greedy flames, though it be so goodly,
51.4284: So wisely worked. And that is the Weird of the world:
51.4285: The green meads shall pass away.” Then His followers did go to Him,
51.4286: And they asked Him softly: “How long shall it stand here?” quoth they,
51.4287: “The world in its winsomeness, before the great turning will come,
51.4288: Until the last day of light shineth through
51.4289: Its covering of clouds; or when can we hope for Thy coming
51.4290: To this mid-world again to judge mankind and its dead and its quick,
51.4292: O my Lord most Good? We have longing to know,
51.4293: O All-Wielding Christ, when that time shall come.”

52.4294: Then All-Wielding Christ did give answer,
52.4295: The Goodly Man, Himself, to the many.
52.4296: “That hath the Good Lord so bidden,” quoth He,
52.4297: “The Father of Heaven’s kingdom hath so concealed it,
52.4298: The Wielder over the World, so that not a one
52.4299: Of the children of men can tell when this noted time
52.4300: Shall come to the world; nor in truth can they know
52.4301: Either, God’s angels, who are ever beside Him
52.4302: And stand in His sight, nor can they say it,
52.4303: With their words tell all truly, when it shall hap,
52.4304: That from the mid-world here the Mighty Lord
52.4305: Shall choose to call the children of men. He alone knows,
52.4306: The Father, Holy in Heaven. From all others ’tis hidden:
52.4307: From the quick and the dead, when that coming shall be.
52.4308: Yet I may tell unto you what wonderous token
52.4309: Shall happen here before He shall come to this world
52.4310: On that famous day. For it shall be revealed in the moon
52.4311: And in the sun as well; both shall turn swarthy,
52.4312: Be surrounded in darkness, and the stars shall fall,
52.4313: The white, heavenly beacons; this broad earth shall tremble,
52.4314: This wide world shake. And many such signs shall there be:
52.4315: The great sea shall rage grimly and the ocean tide grow
52.4316: To bring dread with its waves to the dwellers of earth.
52.4317: Mankind will shrivel and die in its mighty distress.
52.4318: People will pass away in their fears; and in no place will there be peace.
52.4319: But wars so many will rise over the earth,
52.4320: Filled with hatred all; and one clan shall lead a host
52.4321: Against another. The battle of kings will arise,
52.4322: Mighty wanderings of host: and many a murder will there be —
52.4323: There open war-death — that is a terrible thing
52.4324: That man should ever commit such murders.
52.4325: Great ruination will spread awide over all the world —
52.4326: The most farflung dying of men that was ever upon this mid-earth here
52.4327: Through plagues and through pestilence. People lie sick;
52.4328: They do drop and die; and their day endeth.
52.4329: With their life they fulfill it; a famine immeasurable,
52.4330: A grim, hot hunger fares huge o’er the bairns of all men,
52.4331: The greatest of starving; and that is not the slightest
52.4332: Of the torments which shall hap here in this world
52.4333: Before the day of all doom. Whenever ye see such deeds
52.4334: Being done in this world, then may ye verily know
52.4335: That the last day draweth nigh for the land-folk all,
52.4336: That most noted day, and the might of God
52.4337: And the stirring of heavenly strength and the Savior’s coming
52.4338: The Lord’s, in His glory. Lo, for these deeds
52.4339: Ye may know a token in the very trees:
52.4340: When they make buds and bloom and show forth leaf-blades,
52.4341: When they unfold their foliage, the children of men may know full well
52.4342: That soon after this the summer draweth near,
52.4343: The warm and the winsome, and the weather is fair:
52.4344: So know ye also by this token which I have told unto you,
52.4345: When the last day of life draweth near for the land-folk.
52.4346: Now will I say unto you most verily that this folk,
52.4347: This people shall not pass away before this be fulfilled
52.4348: And My word becometh truth. Yet cometh the turning
52.4349: Of heaven and earth, and My Holy Word standeth
52.4350: In firmness henceforth, and all will be so fulfilled,
52.4351: Come to pass in this light, as I have said to these people.
52.4352: Verily, wake ye all: for the well-known day,
52.4353: The day of your doom cometh most certainly, and so doeth the strength,
52.4354: The might immense of your Lord, and that most known of times,
52.4355: The turn of this world. Against this be ye watchful,
52.4356: That He find you not suddenly asleep and stretched out
52.4357: On a couch of ease with all of your evil deeds,
52.4358: And filled with your sins. For the reckoning day
52.4359: Doth come in the deep, dark night, as doeth a thief
52.4360: Furtively all with his deeds: so fareth that day to mankind,
52.4361: The last of this light, so that the land-folk know it not before,
52.4362: Even as was the flood in former days,
52.4363: Which destroyed mankind with its streams of water
52.4364: In time of Noah; but now God saved him only,
52.4365: Him with his family, the Holy Lord,
52.4366: From the flood’s fierce onslaught; so did come also the fire
52.4367: Hot down from heaven which surrounded the cities
52.4369: Greedy indeed and grim, so that no man did go forth
52.4370: Still alive except Lot alone; him the Lord’s angels
52.4371: Did lead from there with his daughters twain
52.4372: High onto a mountain; all others, both land and landsmen,
52.4373: The burning fire, the flames destroyed.
52.4374: So suddenly did come the fire, and so also was the flood before:
52.4375: So, too, shall be the end-day of earth. All men whosoever
52.4376: Should think ahead toward this thing. That is a great need
52.4377: For every man; there let each keep this care firm in his heart.”

53.4378: When ever it shall come to pass, that All-Wielding Christ,
53.4379: Man’s Glorious Son, shall come with God’s might,
53.4380: Shall come with the strength of the Richest of Kings,
53.4381: Sit on high in His own great might; and together with Him,
53.4382: All the angels, too, which are above holy in Heaven;
53.4383: Then shall the children of men and with them the heathen
53.4384: Come all together; all the living kith of the land-folk come,
53.4385: Whosoever was born, hath lived here indeed in this light
53.4386: Of the children of men. To all of mankind,
53.4387: To the folk here all, shall the Lord Most Famous
53.4388: Deal judgments, as were their deeds. The doomed men He shall sort out,
53.4389: The sinful, the lost men, to his left hand;
53.4390: So He shall place the holy and blessed on His right side also,
53.4391: Greeting the good then and speaking most gladly to them:
53.4392: “Come ye,” quoth He, “Ye who are chosen, and receive ye the good kingdom,
53.4393: The mighty, which standeth ready, made for the children of men
53.4394: From the world’s beginning. The Father of Mankind’s Bairns
53.4395: Himself hath hallowed it; ye may enjoy its blessings,
53.4396: Rule o’er this wide realm; since right often ye accomplished My will,
53.4397: Followed Me gladly, and were mild in your giving,
53.4398: When I was plagued here with hunger and thirst,
53.4399: Surrounded by frost; when I lay fettered
53.4400: And oppressed in prison; oft there came to Me in My pain
53.4401: Help from your hands: ye were mild in your hearts
53.4402: And visited Me worthily.” Then verily the crowd addressed Him again.
53.4403: “My Lord most Good,” quoth they. “When didst Thou languish in chains,
53.4404: Oppressed by such needs, as Thou now tellest these people,
53.4405: As Thou, Mighty Master, dost mention? When hath any man seen Thee
53.4406: Oppressed by such needs? Why, Thou hast power over all peoples,
53.4407: Over all treasures as well, whatever the children of men
53.4408: Have won in this world.” Then spake All-Wielding God to them once again.
53.4409: “Whatever ye have done here,” quoth He, “In the name of your Lord,
53.4410: In honor of God, have given of your goods
53.4411: To the men who are the least of those standing here ’mid the many,
53.4412: To such persons indeed poor for their humbleness,
53.4413: Since they accomplished My will — whatsoever ye gave unto them of your wealth,
53.4414: Ye have done for honor of Me. Your Lord Himself hath received it,
53.4415: The help did come to the Heaven-King. Therefore the Holy Lord
53.4416: Will reward your belief: He giveth life everlasting unto you.”
53.4417: Then the Wielder, the Lord, will turn to those at His left hand,
53.4418: To those men who are damned, saying that they must pay for their deeds,
53.4419: These folk for their wrongs; “Now shall ye fare
53.4420: From Me,” quoth He, accursed to eternal fire,
53.4421: Fare to the fire made ready for foes of the Lord,
53.4422: For the folk of the Fiend for their foul works of sin,
53.4423: Since ye have not helped Me, when hunger and thirst
53.4424: Did torment Me most terribly; tortured My mind,
53.4425: I went without clothing: so great was My need,
53.4426: For I had naught of help when I was held bound,
53.4427: Locked into limb-fetters, and lay taken in illness,
53.4428: By serious plagues; for in My sickness ye never
53.4429: Did will to visit Me — nor was I of such worth unto you,
53.4430: That ye thought of Me ever. Therefore will ye suffer
53.4431: In hell in the darkness there.” Then the horde of the people again spake to Him:
53.4432: “Well, All-Wielding God,” quoth they, “Why wilt Thou speak so ’gainst the folk?
53.4433: Say such words ’gainst the many? When hast Thou ever had need of men
53.4434: Or of the goods of mankind? Through Thy giving alone do they own it,
53.4435: The wealth of this world.” Then All-Wielding God speaketh again.
53.4436: “When ye have scorned,” quoth He, “the poorest of the children of earth,
53.4437: The least among men; have considered little
53.4438: These men in your hearts; in your hearts have let them be hated,
53.4439: Have denied them your love: then yet did likewise unto your Lord,
53.4440: Denied Him your wealth; therefore All-Wielding God,
53.4441: Your Father, refuseth to take you; but ye must fare into the fire,
53.4442: Go down into the deep death and there serve the devil,
53.4443: The evil Fiend, since thus ye acted before.”
53.4444: After these words He parted the people in twain,
53.4445: The good and the evil; and the damned ones did go
53.4446: Down into hot hell — they were troubled of heart —
53.4447: There they were punished, received pain never ending,
53.4448: These men who were damned. He doth lead them thence,
53.4449: The High King of Heaven, leadeth the purified host
53.4450: Into long-lasting light — there is life everlasting;
53.4451: God’s realm is made ready for all of the good.

54.4452: So I found out that with His words the All-Wielding God
54.4453: Did tell unto His warriors about the turn of the world,
54.4454: How it fareth on, as long as the bairns of the folk
54.4455: May dwell therein, but how in the end it shall
54.4456: Glide away and be lost. He also said unto His disciples
54.4457: In words of truth: “Why, ye all wit,” quoth He,
54.4458: “That two nights from today the time will come,
54.4459: The paschaltide of the Jews, when the people must serve their God,
54.4460: These men in the temple. It cannot be turned aside,
54.4461: That the Son of Man be sold to the multitude,
54.4462: Full of strength though He be; and be struck to the cross,
54.4463: Enduring tortures most monsterious.” Many thanes were there, too — men
54.4464: From the south gathered together, a grim-minded folk,
54.4465: Clanships of Jews who were come to give service to God.
54.4466: Those learned in writing, the rabbis were come
54.4467: Among the crowd of the men: they were considered the wisest
54.4468: Among the multitude of mankind assembled,
54.4469: A strong clanship. There was Kaiphas, too —
54.4470: Bishop was he among the folk. They spake about God’s Bairn,
54.4471: How they would slay Him, who was free from sin,
54.4472: Told how they could not touch Him on this holy day
54.4473: Among the multitude of men, “Lest the many people,
54.4474: The hordes be aroused, since the host is willing
54.4475: To stand and to battle for Him. In stillness we should
54.4476: Entrap Him, His life, so that the folk of the Jews
54.4477: Will not rise up in rebellion on this holy day.”
54.4478: Then Judas came forward to him, the disciple of Christ,
54.4479: One of the twelve, to where the aethlings did tarry,
54.4480: The clanships of Jews; quoth that he indeed
54.4481: Could give them good counsel, “What will ye pay me?” quoth He,
54.4482: “What treasure, reward, if I should turn that Man over to you
54.4483: Without rebellion or battle?” Then the hearts of the men became
54.4484: Joyous, those of the folk: “If thou would’st do so,” quoth they,
54.4485: “And keep well thy word, then hast thou the right
54.4486: To ask for whatsoever of goodly wealth
54.4487: Thou dost wish from this folk.” Then the men who were there
54.4488: Put at his disposal pieces of silver,
54.4489: Thirty together; and he to the gathering did speak
54.4490: Insolent words: that for this he would yield his Master unto them.
54.4491: Then he turned from the men; evil of mind was he, and disloyal.
54.4492: He did calculate when the time would come unto him,
54.4493: That he might betray Him to the evil men,
54.4494: To the folk of the foe. For the Peace-Bairn of God,
54.4495: The True Wielding Christ well knew He must leave this world,
54.4496: Give up the dwellings of men and return to the realms of God,
54.4497: Fare to the ancient fief of His Father. Never have
54.4498: The children of men seen more love than He bore to those men,
54.4499: To His disciples good. He prepared a guest meal for them
54.4500: And sweetly did bid them sit, and said unto them
54.4501: Many a word most true. The day strode to the west,
54.4502: The sun to its setting. Then He Himself did bid them,
54.4503: The Wielder with His words, that they bring Him water,
54.4504: For His hands clear water; and there the Holy Christ did rise
54.4505: At the feast, the Good Lord, and the feet of His followers
54.4506: He washed with His hands, and wiped them thereafter with towels,
54.4507: Dried them most carefully. Then unto his Lord Christ
54.4508: Simon Peter did speak. “Methinks ’tis no seemly thing,” quoth he,
54.4509: “For Thee, my Master so Good, that Thou should’st be washing my feet
54.4510: With those, Thy most holy hands.” The Lord gave reply unto him,
54.4511: The Wielder then with His words. “If thou has not the will,” quoth He,
54.4512: “To accept this thing, that I wash thy feet
54.4513: With such love indeed, as I do for the others,
54.4514: These men, through My love, then mayest thou not share with Me
54.4515: The kingdom of Heaven.” His heart was then changed
54.4516: For Simon Peter. “Thou Thyself wieldest power,” said he,
54.4517: “My Lord so good, lo, over my feet and my hands
54.4518: O Ruler, if henceforth I may have Thy grace
54.4519: And such part of Thy kingdom of Heaven as Thou, Lord Christ,
54.4521: Would’st grant unto me in Thy goodness.”
54.4522: The disciples of Christ, those earls, suffered His service
54.4523: With patience, those thanes, whatsoever Mighty Christ,
54.4524: Their Liege, would do unto them, out of love, and He thought to do

55.4526: Did go to sit once again among the people and gave unto them
55.4527: Much long-lasting counsel. Then was the light come,
55.4528: The morning come to mankind. Almighty Christ
55.4529: The greeted His subjects and asked them where they intended
55.4530: To prepare for the feast on this festive day,
55.4531: Where He would hold, would keep this holy tide
55.4532: Himself with His disciples. Then He hight them, His men,
55.4533: Seek out Jerusalem: “When ye come there,” quoth He,
55.4534: “Within the city itself, there will be great confusion,
55.4535: A mighty seething of men — ye will see a man
55.4536: Carrying there in his hand a cup of clear water.
55.4538: We shall follow him into whatsoever garden ye do see him go;
55.4539: And unto that lord who owneth this house
55.4540: Ye yourselves shall say that I have sent you hence
55.4541: To make ready My feast. Then will he show you
55.4542: A goodly house, a high upper hall
55.4543: Hung over with brightest array. There shall ye busy
55.4544: Yourselves with My meal. There I shall most certainly come,
55.4545: Myself and My disciples, too.” Then straightway thereafter
55.4546: The servants of Christ set out on the way to Jerusalem,
55.4547: And they did find there all things even as He had said
55.4548: With true word-tokens. Nor was aught truly changed.
55.4549: They made ready the feast there, and right soon the Son of God,
55.4550: The Holy Christ was come to the house
55.4551: Where they should accomplish the custom there of the land,
55.4552: Following the bidding of God, as it was for the Jewish folk
55.4553: Ancient custom and law from time immemorial.
55.4554: On the evening All-Wielding Christ did go
55.4555: To take His seat in the hall; and He bade His disciples
55.4556: Come unto Him, the twelve who were truest to Him,
55.4557: These men most loyal to Him in their minds
55.4558: Both in words and in ways. Well did He know
55.4559: The thoughts in their hearts, our Holy Lord —
55.4560: He greeted them over the banquet. “I yearn indeed,”
55.4561: He said, “to sit together with you
55.4562: And partake of the feast, share the Passover
55.4563: Of Jews with you, My beloved. Now must I tell unto you
55.4564: The will of the Lord, that in this world no longer
55.4565: May I enjoy meat with mankind before it must be fulfilled,
55.4567: The kingdom of Heaven. For Me there is at hand
55.4568: Both torment and torture, which I must truly endure
55.4569: For the people, this land-folk here.” So did He speak to His thanes,
55.4570: The Holy Lord, and His heart was grieved,
55.4571: His spirit darkened with sorrow, and to His disciples He spake,
55.4572: The Good Man to His faithful: “Why, I give unto you the kingdom of God,
55.4573: Give you the light of Heaven, and ye give unto Me
55.4574: Most sweetly your thaneship. But now ye wish not to fulfill this,
55.4575: But waver far from the word. Now verily I say unto you
55.4576: That one of your twelve will become untrue,
55.4577: One will sell Me among the kinship of Jews,
55.4578: Will sell Me for silver, and will take such riches,
55.4579: Such precious treasure; and give his Lord in return,
55.4580: His sweet, his beloved Liege. But great sorrow shall come unto him
55.4581: From that deed, and much pain. For he shall perceive them,
55.4582: The Weird Sisters, and shall see the end of his care.
55.4583: He shall know most truly that it would be a far sweeter thing,
55.4584: A far better one, if he had never been born
55.4585: To live in this light, than that he take pay
55.4586: For evil deeds and wrongful advice.”
55.4587: Then each earl began to look around at the others,
55.4588: To gaze about sorrowfully, for they were sore of soul
55.4589: And troubled indeed of heart; they heard their Lord there
55.4590: Speaking words of lament. They were worried
55.4591: To which of the twelve He would now tell
55.4592: That he was the miscreant, the man who had bargained
55.4593: With the people for the pieces of silver. Nor was it simple for any person,
55.4594: For any thane to confess such a crime,
55.4595: Such a sinful mind; but each man denied it —
55.4596: And all became fearful and dared not ask
55.4597: Until Simon Peter, though he himself dared not speak —
55.4598: This worthy man did make motion
55.4599: To John the good: to the Bairn of God
55.4600: He was in these days the dearest one,
55.4601: The one most beloved, and Holy Christ gave him leave
55.4602: To rest in His lap, to lie against His breast,
55.4603: And on it to lean his head; there heard he so many a holy mysery,
55.4604: So many deep thoughts; and to his dear Lord he did speak
55.4605: And began to question Him. “Who shall that be, my Liege?”
55.4606: Quoth he, “Who would sell Thee, the Richest of Kings,
55.4607: To the folk of the foe? Full anxious we are,
55.4608: O Wielder, to know.” He had ready His words,
55.4609: The Holy Christ: “See thou into whose hands I here
55.4610: Give of My meat before these men: he hath most wicked thoughts,
55.4611: Beareth great bitterness of mind: he shall deliver Me into bonds,
55.4612: Into the power of the foe, where they shall deprive Me of My age,
55.4613: Shall destroy My life.” Thereafter He did take
55.4614: The meat before the men and gave of the meat unto that mean scoundrel,
55.4615: Into Judas’ hand, and He spoke unto him,
55.4616: He Himself before His disciples, and He straightway commanded
55.4617: That he fare far away from the folk. “Do as thou thinkest,” quoth He,
55.4618: “Do as thou need’st must do; no longer mayest thou
55.4619: Hide thy will and intent — thy Weird is at hand,
55.4620: Thy time draweth near.” When the troth-breaker
55.4621: Did take of the meat and with his mouth did eat thereof,
55.4622: The power of God did forsake him, and the Fiend did enter
55.4623: Into his body then, that loathsome wight;
55.4624: And Satan was bound more sorely to him,
55.4625: Bound hard ’round his heart, since the help of God
55.4626: Had left him here in this light. To those who change lords
55.4627: Under this heaven: to such woe will indeed come.

56.4628: Then setting out from there and thinking up evil,
56.4629: Judas did leave; against his Liege this thane
56.4630: Harbored great grimness of heart. It had grown very dark,
56.4631: It was deep in the night. Now the Son of the Lord
56.4632: Tarried still at the feast; and for His disciples there
56.4633: The Wielder did bless both the wine and the bread,
56.4634: The Holy King of the Heavens; and with His hands He did break it
56.4635: And gave it to His disciples and gave thanks unto God,
56.4636: Grateful unto Him, who created all that was there,
56.4637: The world and its winsomeness; and He spake many a word:
56.4638: “Believe ye this clearly,” quoth He, “that this is My body
56.4639: And My blood as well. I give both unto you
56.4640: To eat and to drink. This I shall give on earth,
56.4641: Shall spill and spread onto it, and shall ransom you
56.4642: To the realms of the Lord and to life everlasting
56.4643: In the light of Heaven. Remember ye ever
56.4644: And follow ye that which I give unto you at this feast.
56.4645: Make it known unto the many, for this is a mighty thing.
56.4646: With it ye shall honor Him, who is your Lord.
56.4647: Hold this to My memory as a holy token,
56.4648: So that the children of men will cherish and keep it,
56.4650: All men in this mid-world: that through My love I have done so,
56.4651: Through the grace of the Lord. And think ye ever
56.4652: How I have bidden you to keep firm this brotherhood,
56.4654: To have fastness of mind, much love in your hearts, so that the children of men
56.4655: Over the whole of the earth will all understand
56.4656: That ye are most truly the disciples Mine.
56.4657: I shall also make known unto you how a fierce, wily Fiend,
56.4658: A word-strong foe shall tempt your spirits,
56.4659: Satan himself. He cometh to ensnare
56.4660: Your souls most boldly. Straightway must ye make steadfast
56.4661: The thoughts in your breasts. By your prayers shall I stand,
56.4662: So that the mighty Fiend may not cause your minds to become doubtful,
56.4663: So that I may help you against the foe. Once he came hither to tempt Me;
56.4664: But his desire sufficed not one whit,
56.4665: His lust for My body. Nor will I longer conceal from you
56.4666: What trials now lie straight ahead for you:
56.4667: Ye shall be disloyal to Me, ye disciples Mine,
56.4668: Disloyal to your thaneship before this dark night
56.4669: Leaveth the land-folk and the light cometh once more,
56.4670: The morning to mankind.” Then the minds of the men
56.4671: Became dreary, their hearts sore indeed.
56.4672: They were troubled of spirit, and for their Lord’s words
56.4673: Most sorrowed and grieved. But Simon Peter,
56.4674: The thane, did speak words of solace to the folk,
56.4675: For love of his Lord. “Though all this land-folk,” quoth he,
56.4676: “Though all Thy disciples deny Thee, still do I gladly
56.4677: Suffer all pain, all sorrow for Thee.
56.4678: I am ever prepared, if God doth permit me,
56.4679: To stand straight and firm as a shield unto Thee.
56.4680: Though they close Thee deep in their dungeons,
56.4681: Though the land-folk lock Thee away, there is doubt so little
56.4682: But that I would bide with Thee in thy bonds,
56.4683: Lie with Thee, my so beloved Lord, if they lie in wait
56.4684: To snuff out Thy life with the hate of the sword’s edge,
56.4685: O my Master most Good; then shall I gladly give up my life
56.4686: For Thee in the play of weapons, nor verily shall I
56.4687: Ever avoid it, as long as mind
56.4688: And strength of hand are still mine.” Then His Lord spake again unto him.
56.4689: “Why, thou presumest in thyself,” quoth He, “an unswerving loyalty.
56.4690: A steadfastness so great! Oh, thou hast the soul of a hero
56.4691: And good will as well. Yet may I tell unto thee how it will hap,
56.4692: That thou shalt become so wavering of heart, as thou now canst not ween:
56.4693: That thou shalt deny Me, thy Lord, three times,
56.4694: Before the crow of the cock, acknowledging Me not as thy Liege,
56.4695: But thou shalt renounce My protection.” Then again the man did reply.
56.4696: “If in this world,” quoth he, “it will ever so come to pass,
56.4697: That I should have to face death together with Thee,
56.4698: Have to die in splendor, still that day will never arrive
56.4699: When I would deny Thee, my most dearly loved Lord,
56.4700: Of my own will before these, the Jews.” All the disciples spake likewise,
56.4701: That they would suffer with him at the tribunal there.

57.4702: Then the Wielder Himself bade them with His words,
57.4703: The High King of Heaven, that they let not their hearts doubt,
57.4704: Hight that they not want to drag up deep thought
57.4705: “Let not your hearts be laid low by the word of your Lord,
57.4706: Nor fear ye too much. I shall seek Our Father Myself
57.4708: And shall send the Holy Ghost from the kingdom of Heaven.
57.4709: He shall be consolation and succor both unto you,
57.4710: Reminding you in His speech of the many things I have taught
57.4711: Unto you with My words. Wisdom He will give unto you
57.4712: In your hearts, a joyous teaching, so that ye shall henceforth accomplish
57.4713: The word and the work which I have shown unto you in this world.”
57.4714: The Mighty Son then rose, Christ Savior,
57.4715: In the temple there, and with His thanes He fared forth,
57.4716: He Himself on that very same night. Christ’s disciples
57.4717: Went sorrowing and grieving most sadly,
57.4718: Troubled of heart. Then He climbed up a hill —
57.4719: The Olive Mount was it called: there ’twas His custom
57.4720: To go with His followers. Full well did Judas know this,
57.4721: The man with his mind aimed to ruin: for on this mount he was often with Him.
57.4722: Then God’s Son did indeed greet His disciples.
57.4723: “Ye are now so saddened,” quoth He, “since ye know of My death.
57.4724: Now ye are grieving and groaning, while the Jews are gay,
57.4725: While the many are merry and happy of mind,
57.4726: While the world is in rapture. Yet this will all come to an end,
57.4727: Will cease most swiftly. Then will they be sore of heart,
57.4728: Grow mournful of mind, and ye may rejoice
57.4729: Until that day everlasting; for your end and a turn
57.4730: Of your fortune never cometh: therefore may ye henceforth
57.4732: Not regret My words nor rue My coming.” Then He bade His retainers
57.4733: Come on the mountain; quoth that He wished them to climb
57.4734: Higher up with Him upon the hill-cliff,
57.4735: And He hight that three of His thanes go with Him,
57.4736: Jacob and John and Peter the Good,
57.4737: Loyal thanes three. And they did so go
57.4738: With their Liege most gladly. Then the Son of God,
57.4739: Upon the hill, did bid them bend their knees in prayer,
57.4740: Bade that they greet God and entreat Him greatly
57.4741: That He hold in check the strength of the Tempter
57.4742: The will of the wicked, so that the worker of wrong,
57.4743: The devil, could not bring their minds to doubt.
57.4744: And also the Lord Himself for prayer
57.4745: Did bow with bent knee, the Brightest of Kings,
57.4746: Kneeling forward to earth; and to the Father of all Earth-folk
57.4747: He cried aloud, spake lamenting words
57.4748: In His sorrow; for His spirit was grieved
57.4749: And His heart was moved by His humanness.
57.4750: His flesh feared indeed; tears fell from Him,
57.4751: His dear, precious sweat did drip, even as blood doth drip,
57.4752: Doth well from a wound. Within God’s Bairn
57.4753: A battle was raging between body and spirit.
57.4754: The one was ready for the road beyond,
57.4755: The spirit for the kingdom of God, while the other stood yammering,
57.4756: The flesh of Christ; and fearful of death,
57.4757: It sought not to give up the light. Ever He cried to the Lord,
57.4758: Ever more did He call unto the Almighty,
57.4759: To the High Father of Heaven, to the Holy God,
57.4760: To the All-Wielder ever with His words. “If mankind,” quoth He,
57.4761: “Cannot be saved except that I give
57.4762: My own precious blood to the bairns of the people
57.4763: To torture most terribly — if this be truly Thy will,
57.4764: Then will I choose to drain it: I take in my hands the chalice,
57.4765: Drink it down to the dregs, my Lord, dear Liege,
57.4766: Mighty Master and Shielder. Look Thou not now down on me,
57.4767: On the good of My flesh. But I shall fulfill
57.4768: Whatsoever Thy will be: for Thou wieldest power over all.”
57.4769: Then He went to that place, where He had left His disciples
57.4770: Biding upon the mountain; and the Bairn of God
57.4771: Did find them in troubled sleep; for their hearts were sore,
57.4772: That they should be parted from their beloved Liege.
57.4773: Such should be the mind-sorrow of every man
57.4774: Who must forsake and leave his beloved lord,
57.4775: Giving up one so good. Then He did go to His disciples, spake unto them;
57.4776: The Wielder did wake them and greet them with words.
57.4777: “Why do ye wish to sleep?” quoth He. “Why do ye not watch
57.4778: But a little time here with Me? That Weird is at hand,
57.4779: That it shall come to pass, even as He, God the Father,
57.4780: The Mighty, hath marked it. There is no doubt in My mind;
57.4781: My spirit is most ready to make done God’s will,
57.4782: Is prepared to fare on His way. But My flesh is still troubled,
57.4783: My body still holds Me bound. It is loath to bear,
57.4784: To endure such suffering. But I shall accomplish
57.4785: My Father’s will. Have ye firmness of heart!”
57.4786: He did go then up on the other side
57.4787: Of the mountain in order to pray —
57.4788: The Glorious Lord — and many a good word
57.4789: He did indeed speak there. God’s angel then came
57.4790: Holy from heaven and made firm His heart,
57.4791: Made Him bold for the bonds. He bided there ever,
57.4792: Zealous in prayer, and to His Father He cried,
57.4793: To the Wielder with His words. “If it cannot be otherwise, quoth He,
57.4794: O Lord most splendid, except that I suffer
57.4795: Great torture and torment for the folk of mankind, I shall truly
57.4796: Await then Thy will.” And He went again thence
57.4797: To seek His disciples. He found them sleeping
57.4798: And called to them curtly. And again He went thence
57.4799: A third time to pray. And the King of All peoples,
57.4800: The Son of the Lord, spake with the selfsame words
57.4801: To His All-Wielding Father, as He had done before.
57.4803: Remind the Mighty One of the good of mankind;
57.4804: And went then again to His disciples, and straightway He spake unto them.
57.4805: “Sleep ye and rest,” said He. “Now will he straightway come,
57.4806: Come with a force, he who hath sold Me, sinless as I am,
57.4807: And hath received silver therefore.” The disciples of Christ
57.4808: Awakened after these words, and they beheld war-men coming,
57.4809: Climbing up the mountain with a great commotion,

58.4811: Man hate-filled of heart. After him the Jews did go marching,
58.4812: The folk-clans of the foe. In their midst they carried fire,
58.4813: Lights in lamp-vessels; and they led forth torches,
58.4814: Bright burning down from the city, as they began most earnestly
58.4815: To stride up the mountain. This spot Judas knew well,
58.4816: The one to which he should lead the land-folk all.
58.4817: As they now fared to the spot in front of the folk,
58.4818: He said unto them as a sign, lest they seize by mistake
58.4819: Some other man: “I shall first go to Him,” quoth he,
58.4820: “Shall kiss Him and say: ‘That is Christ Himself!’
58.4821: Then shall ye seize Him with the strength of the crowd;
58.4822: Shall bind Him up there on the mount and bring Him down to the bastion,
58.4823: Lead Him down ’mid the land-folk: His life hath he forfeited
58.4824: With His words full well.” And the people went,
58.4825: Until they were come to the Christ Himself —
58.4826: The grim folk of the Jews, to where He stood with His followers,
58.4827: The Lord Most Glorious, biding his god-sent fate,
58.4828: The wonderous time. Then Judas went toward Him,
58.4829: Man without troth, and unto God’s Bairn
58.4830: He nodded his head and here spake to his Lord,
58.4831: Kissed Him, Mighty Christ, carried out his word,
58.4832: Pointed Him out to the people, as he had promised before.
58.4833: The Lord of All Peoples bore all with His patience,
58.4834: The Wielder of World; and with His words He did speak unto Him,
58.4835: Asked him most boldly: “Why hast thou come to Me with this host?
58.4836: Why dost thou lead this land-folk to Me? And to this loathsome crowd
58.4837: Thou sellest Me with thy kiss, among the clans of the Jews
58.4838: Betrayest Me to these many?” He went to speak to the many,
58.4839: To the other people, and to ask with His words
58.4840: Why they were come to seek Him so zealously here
58.4841: With their thralls in the night. “To whom do you wish to bring need and distress,
58.4842: To some one of mankind?” Then once more the many did speak unto Him
58.4843: And said that they had been told that the Savior did tarrry
58.4844: Here high on the hillside. “He who hath caused this unrest
58.4845: Amid the Jewish folk and calleth Himself
58.4846: The Son of God. We came here to seek Him,
58.4847: Are most anxious to find Him: He is from Galilee-land
58.4848: From the city of Nazareth.” When Saving Christ
58.4849: Said unto them in sooth that it was He Himself,
58.4850: The folk of the Jews became sore afraid.
58.4851: Frightened and shocked were they, so that they straightway fell back,
58.4852: Each and all, and sought the earth: at the same time
58.4853: All the host did retreat. They could not resist
58.4854: The word and the voice of the Lord; yet were there some warlike men.
58.4855: These ran up the hillock; made firm their hearts,
58.4856: Bound fast the thoughts in their breasts; and bitterly raging,
58.4858: They surrounded Christ Savior. There stood the wise men
58.4860: Before this most dreadful deed; and to their Dear Lord they did speak:
58.4861: “Were it now Thy will,” quoth they, “My Wielder, My Liege,
58.4862: That they shall slay us with the spear-point here,
58.4863: Shall wound us with weapons, then would naught be one whit as good,
58.4864: But that we might die here for our Dear Lord,
58.4865: Pale in expiring.” Then plenteously wroth grew he,
58.4867: It welled up with his heart, so that not a word could he speak,
58.4868: So sorrowed his soul, since they were about to enchain
58.4869: His Beloved Lord there Bloated with anger, the bold-minded
58.4870: Thane strode ahead, stood before his Liege,
58.4871: Hard by his Lord; nor was his heart e’er in doubt,
58.4872: Fearful within his breast, but he drew his bill,
58.4873: The sword at his side, and with the strength of his arm
58.4874: He struck the first of the foe standing before him,
58.4875: So that Malchus was marked by the knife
58.4876: On his right side, slashed by the sword’s edge.
58.4877: His hearing had been hewn: sore was the hurt ’round his head,
58.4878: So that, sword-gory, cheek and ear in mortal wound
58.4879: Burst asunder, and blood did spring forth,
58.4880: Welling up from the wound. Then was the cheek indeed scarred
58.4881: Of the enemy’s leader. Those around stood away,
58.4882: Dreading the bite of the bill. Then spake God’s Bairn
58.4883: Himself to Simon Peter, said that he should put his sword,
58.4884: The sharp one, back in its scabbard. “If I truly cared,” said He
58.4885: “To wage conflict against this crowd of the warriors,
58.4886: Then would I remind Him, the Glorious, the Almighty God,
58.4887: The Holy Father in the Kingdom of Heaven,
58.4888: That He send hither to Me a host of His angels,
58.4889: Wise in warfaring; these men could indeed not withstand
58.4890: Their weapon-strength ever. Nor could such a host of warriors
58.4891: Stand against them, though gathered together in groups.
58.4892: Still could they not save their lives. But the All-Wielding Lord,
58.4893: The Father Almighty, hath marked it otherwise:
58.4894: We are to bear all the bitterness, whatsoever these people bring unto us,
58.4895: Nor shall we be angry nor rage ’gainst their strife:
58.4896: For he who doth practice the hatred of weapons,
58.4897: Who gladly partaketh in grim spear-grudges —
58.4898: He again is slain by the sword’s edge,
58.4899: Doth die in his own blood. We must not destroy
58.4900: One whit with our deeds.” Then He went to the wounded man.
58.4901: With skill He set the flesh-seams together,
58.4902: The head-wounds all, so that it was healed straightway,
58.4903: The bite of the bill. And the Bairn of God
58.4904: Spake to the angry throng. “Methinks ’tis a wonder great,” quoth He,
58.4905: “If ye have wanted to do harm unto Me,
58.4906: Why did ye then not take Me, when I stood in the temple,
58.4907: Among your folk and did tell them full many true words?
58.4909: The sun shone, the day’s dear beam, and ye did want to do
58.4910: Naught to harm there in this light; but now ye lead your landsmen
58.4911: To Me in the night, as one doeth unto a thief
58.4912: Whom one wishes to seize — some scoundrel and wretch
58.4913: Who hath forfeited life.” Then the folk of the Jews
58.4914: Grasped at God’s Son, the grim-minded host,
58.4915: The persecuting crowd. The people piled ’round Him,
58.4916: The enraged horde of men — they saw not their wrongs —
58.4917: They held Him fast, threw His hands in chains,
58.4918: His arms and fingers in fetters. Such frightful torment
58.4919: He needed not have stood, nor such grievous suffering,
58.4920: Nor have endured such anguish. But He did so for this host,
58.4921: Since He wanted to save the children of men,
58.4922: To fetch them from hell to the kingdom of Heaven,
58.4923: To the wide-flung wealth; therefore He reproached them no whit
58.4924: For that which they would do unto Him in their hatred and anger.

59.4925: Then the angry folk of the Jews did become insolent,
59.4926: The host most haughty, since they had Holy Christ
59.4927: And could lead Him away in limb-bondage,
59.4928: Take Him forth in their fetters. And the foe went again
59.4929: From the mount to the town. And God’s Mighty Bairn
59.4930: Did go ’mid the host with His hands all bound,
59.4931: Drear and sad, down to the dale. For His dearest thanes
59.4932: Had broken their troth, as He Himself had foretold.
59.4933: But it was not for fear that they forsook Him,
59.4934: God’s Bairn, their Beloved, but so long before there had been
59.4935: The word of the prophet, that it would indeed be thus.
59.4936: Therefore they could not avoid their own deeds. And after the crowd
59.4937: Went Peter and John, those two men well-known,
59.4938: And followed from afar. Full anxious were they
59.4939: To know what the grim-minded Jews meant to do with God’s Bairn
59.4940: To their Lord most Dear. When they were come down to the dale
59.4941: From the hill to the burg in which was their bishop,
59.4942: The temple’s holder, these haughty men did lead Him
59.4943: These earls, behind a fence. A great fire was there,
59.4944: There were flames in the foreyard, made nearby for the folk,
59.4945: For the warrior crowd. They went there to warm them,
59.4946: The landsmen of Jews, and they left God’s Bairn
59.4947: Waiting in chains. There was a great racket,
59.4948: The noise of the insolent. Since John was known
59.4949: To the highest one there, he could push inside with the host,
59.4950: With the throng through the yard; but the best of all thanes
59.4951: Peter, still stood outside. The portal’s warder would not permit him
59.4952: To follow His Lord, till he begged a friend,
59.4953: Until John begged of a Jew to let Peter go
59.4954: Forth to the foreyard. A woman full of deceit
59.4955: Did slip up to him there: she was a handmaid
59.4956: Of one of the Jews, of her lord; and this unlovely girl
59.4957: Did speak to the thane. “What, thou mightest be,” quoth she, “a man
59.4958: From Galilee, disciple of Him standing yonder
59.4959: With His arms firmly fettered.” The fear overtook
59.4960: Simon Peter straighway, and his mind became slack,
59.4961: And he said that not one word of the wife had he understood,
59.4962: Nor was He a thane of that Leader ever, of that Lord.
59.4963: He avoided Him in view of the many, said verily he knew not that Man.
59.4964: “Thy talk is senseless to me,” said he. Then God’s strength,
59.4965: The Lord’s power did leave his heart. And leaving, he did go
59.4966: Forth amid the folk, until he came to the fires;
59.4967: He went there to warm him. There also a woman began
59.4968: To load loathsome words unto him. “Here may ye look on your foe,” cried she,
59.4969: “This is all clearly a retainer of Christ,
59.4970: A disciple of Him Himself.” Then straightway there did come nearer
59.4971: To him men of the foe. And the bairns of the Fiend
59.4972: Did question him of what clan he was:
59.4973: “Thou art not of these burghers,” quoth they. “From thy bearing we see that,
59.4974: From thy words and thy ways, that thou art not of this world-folk,
59.4975: But art from Galilee come.” Yet he would not admit it,
59.4976: But stood there denying and swore a strong oath
59.4977: By all that is true that he was not of that tribe.
59.4978: His words had no power: it was to come to this pass,
59.4979: As He who rules mankind had so marked it indeed
59.4980: In this world. Then came to him also a cousin
59.4981: Of him whom he had hewn with his bill,
59.4982: With his sword’s sharpness; and said that he had seen him there
59.4983: “High on the hillock, there where we bound the hands
59.4984: Of thy Lord in the grove, in the tree-garden there,
59.4985: Fastened His arms with the fetters.” Then for the fear in his heart
59.4986: He again denied his dear Liege, quoth that indeed he would forfeit his life,
59.4987: If there was any man here on this earth
59.4988: Who can say in truth that he was of that tribe,
59.4989: That he followed His path. There for the first time
59.4990: The crow of the cock did commence. And Holy Christ,
59.4991: The Best of All Bairns, who stood there bound,
59.4992: The Son of the Lord Himself, did look to Simon Peter,
59.4993: Saw that earl over His shoulder. Then Simon Peter
59.4994: Felt sadness within him and his spirit was sore.
59.4995: Filled with hurt was his heart, and most grieved was he.
59.4996: So troubled was he, that he himself had so spoken before,
59.4997: And he remembered the words then which All-Wielding Christ
59.4998: Had said unto him; that in this swarthy, dark night,
59.4999: He was to deny Him, his Lord, three times,
59.5000: Before the crow of the cock. Bitterly this came up in his breast,
59.5001: Welled up with him; and angry of heart he went away:
59.5002: The man left the many. With care in his mind
59.5003: And deeply sorrowed, he wept at his sinfulness,
59.5004: At his own words, and there came welling up
59.5005: Hot tears from within him for the grief in his heart,
59.5006: Bloodily bursting up from his breast. For he thought
59.5007: Never to atone for his sins nor come again to his Master,
59.5008: To the grace of his Lord. No one hath since grown so old
59.5009: Who ever did see a man rue more sorely
59.5010: His own words and his sins and to bewail them so,
59.5011: Lamenting most loudly. “Woe, Mighty God, O my Lord,” quoth he,
59.5012: “Woe that I have forfeited myself, so that for this world,
59.5013: This life I may no longer be thankful. If in my old age
59.5014: I must renounce Thy grace and the realms of Heaven,
59.5015: Then, my Ruler, my King, be there no thanks unto me,
59.5016: My Beloved Liege, that I was born to this light.
59.5017: I am now unworthy, O Thou, my Wielder,
59.5018: That I may thus fare along with Thy followers,
59.5019: Sinful amid Thy disciples. I myself shall avoid them
59.5020: In my heart and my soul, since I have spoken such sin.”
59.5021: Thus the best of all men grieved bitterly indeed.
59.5022: He rued most deeply that he had denied Him there,
59.5023: His Beloved Lord. But the bairns of the land-folk,
59.5024: Of mankind should not wonder why God so willed it,
59.5025: That such a beloved man should suffer such sorrow,
59.5026: That he should deny his Lord so disgracefully
59.5027: For the word of a servant maid — he, this swiftest of warriors
59.5028: Deny his Dear Liege; it was done for all those of mankind,
59.5029: For the good of the children of men. He wanted to make them the first,
59.5030: The highest over His household — He the Lord Holy:
59.5031: He let it be known how little strength hath
59.5032: The heart of man without God’s might.
59.5033: He let him sin so that later he might
59.5034: Better believe them, the people, how precious it is
59.5035: For each man indeed, when he hath done evil,
59.5036: That he be absolved from his wicked deeds,
59.5037: From his wrongs and his sins, as he is absolved by God Himself,
59.5038: The Ruler of Heaven’s Realms, from his hurtful wrong.

60.5039: Therefore is a man’s boasting of but little avail —
60.5040: The pride of his youth: if then God’s help doth forsake him,
60.5041: Because of his sins, then is that man straightway
60.5042: Fearful of thought, though he first uttered threats
60.5043: And boasted of his battles and of the broad strength of his hand —
60.5044: This man, of his might. This was marked in that marvelous,
60.5045: That best of all thanes, when at that time the holy help
60.5046: Of His Master forsook him. Therefore no man should boast
60.5047: All too much of himself, since then often hope
60.5048: And will do forsake him, if All-Wielding God,
60.5049: The High King of Heaven, doth not strengthen his heart.
60.5050: But the Best of All Bairns did wait and did bear His bonds
60.5051: For the sake of mankind. Many of the Jewish folk
60.5052: Did come and surround Him and speak such mockery
60.5053: And held Him to scorn, as He stood there chained
60.5054: And enduring most patiently what the people did unto Him,
60.5055: What loathsome grief these land-folk. Then was the light come again,
60.5056: The morning to mankind. Many were gathered,
60.5057: Wide hosts of the Jews. Wolf-minds had they,
60.5058: Evil hearts as well. Their book-learned ones,
60.5059: Many men together, gathered at morning-tide,
60.5060: Angry and hardened and longing for evil,
60.5061: Wishing for wrong. They went in groups together,
60.5062: The men to consult; and they began to consider
60.5063: How they would accuse the Mighty Christ of sin
60.5064: With false witnesses and with faithless men —
60.5065: Accuse Him indeed through His own spoken word,
60.5066: So that they might torment Him with tortures most great,
60.5067: Dealing out death unto Him. But on that day they could
60.5068: Find no false witnesses, ones who feared not
60.5069: To deal out such pain, and to condemn Him to death,
60.5070: Release Him from life. Then at last there came forth
60.5072: From the crowd two men without truth and began to tell against Him,
60.5073: Said that they had heard Him Himself say
60.5074: That He could tear down the temple of God,
60.5075: The highest of all houses, through the strength of His hands;
60.5076: And through His craft and His might could erect it again
60.5077: On the third day hence, as no other man could ever thus do.
60.5078: He was silent and suffered. Never could a folk speak,
60.5079: A people utter such lies, that He would verily
60.5080: Have avenged them with words of evil. Then there arose from the host
60.5081: A man baleful of thought: bishop among the folk,
60.5082: A prince of this people — and put such question to Christ,
60.5083: Exhorted Him strongly with solemn oath,
60.5084: Greeted Him thus in the name of God and bade Him eagerly
60.5085: To say unto him, whether He were the Son
60.5086: Of the Living God: He who created the light,
60.5087: Christ, King eternal. “We cannot see one whit of this
60.5088: From Thy words or Thy works.” Then verily again the True,
60.5089: The Good Son of God did reply: “Thou sayest it now before these Jews,
60.5090: Sayest it truly, that it is I Myself.
60.5091: But these landsmen do not believe Me; and hence will they not release Me,
60.5092: Nor are they worthy of My word. Now verily I say unto you
60.5093: That ye shall still see Me sitting on the right side of God,
60.5094: Radiant the Son of Man in the might and strength
60.5095: Of the All-Wielding Father, and coming again down here
60.5096: Through the clouds of Heaven and dealing unto all the kith of mankind
60.5097: Such judgments with His words, even as they worked and are worthy thereof.”
60.5098: Then was the bishop wrathful and bitter of heart,
60.5099: Sorely enraged at these words; and he rent his raiments,
60.5100: Tore them before his breast; “Now need ye bide no longer,” quoth he,
60.5101: “Ye people, wait for a witness, now that such words,
60.5102: Such blasphemy hath come from His mouth. Many men have now heard it:
60.5103: Warriors here in the temple, that He told of His mightiness,
60.5104: Said that He was the God. Well then, ye Jews,
60.5105: What doom will ye deal Him? Is He now worthy of death

61.5107: The folk of the Jews, that He had forfeited life,
61.5108: Was worthy of punishment. Yet not for His works was it done,
61.5109: That the Jewish folk there in Jerusalem
61.5110: Condemned Him to His death, Him who had done no sin,
61.5111: The Son of the Lord. Then the land-folk of Jews
61.5112: Did boast of their deeds, how they could do God’s Bairn,
61.5113: Him held in bonds, the most harm indeed.
61.5114: The crowd surrounded Him and struck His cheeks, the side
61.5115: Of His head with their hands: unto Him they did this in mockery and scorn,
61.5116: The crowd of the foe; covered Him with their malice
61.5117: And their blasphemous speech. And the Bairn of God
61.5118: Stood firmly amid His foe. His arms were in fetters;
61.5119: He endured most patiently what the people
61.5120: Brought unto Him of bitterness there. He bore no anger
61.5121: Against this riot of men. Then wrathful men
61.5122: Did take Him so bound, that Bairn of God,
61.5123: And they led Him there to where the folk-throng’s,
61.5124: The people’s, judging-place was. There thanes aplenty
61.5125: Surrounded their leader. He was the envoy of that lord
61.5126: Of the city of Rome, who ruled over all realms;
61.5127: He was come from Caesar, was sent to the clans of the Jews,
61.5128: To govern their kingdom: he gave them counsel.
61.5129: Pilate was he called, and he was a man from Pontus,
61.5130: Born of that clan. He had collected a great crowd,
61.5131: A multitude of the people at the judging place.
61.5132: This faithless horde of the Jewish host
61.5133: Did give Him up — Him, Son of God,
61.5134: To the folk of the foe; quoth that He had forfeited His life
61.5135: And that one should reward Him with the weapon’s edge,
61.5136: With the sword’s sharpness. Still the crowd of the Jews cared not
61.5137: To throng into the law-house itself; but the land-folk did remain without,
61.5138: And spake from there to the many within. Into this mob they wished not to go,
61.5139: Not go to that foreign man, so that they need not hear these unrighteous words
61.5140: On that day, nor hear one whit of the wrong being dealt.
61.5141: But said it was their wont to hold the holiest of times,
61.5142: The purest, their Passover. Pilate received
61.5143: The Wielder’s Bairn from the wicked sinners,
61.5144: Received Him, the Sinless. Then sorely troubled
61.5145: Was Judas of mind, when he saw His Master
61.5146: Surrounded to death; and his deed he now began
61.5147: To rue in his heart, that he had sold Him,
61.5148: His Lord without Sin. He took the silver,
61.5149: Took there the thirty pieces that they had given to him in return for his Liege.
61.5150: And he went with them to the Jews and told them his grim, wicked deed,
61.5151: Said unto them his sin; and the silver he offered
61.5152: To give back gladly. “So grievously,” quoth he,
61.5153: “Have I sold it, the blood of my Liege, my Beloved,
61.5154: That I ween that to me it will be of no worth.”
61.5155: But the host of the Jews would not take it, but hight him henceforth
61.5156: To let such a sin be his own care and concern,
61.5157: That e’er he had done against his Lord.
61.5158: “Thou thyself look to that,” quoth they. “What hast thou to seek among us?
61.5159: Do not thou place shame on these people.” Then presently Judas
61.5160: Did again go thence to the temple of God
61.5161: Most sorely grieved, and he threw the silver
61.5162: Inside on the altar, nor dared he own it for long.
61.5163: He fared forth in fear and the bairns of the Fiend
61.5164: Admonished him fiercely: the devil had seized
61.5165: The mind of this man; and the Mighty God was enraged,
61.5166: So that he, that wretch, did fashion a rope;
61.5167: And in order to hang him, did incline his head
61.5168: Through the death-choking noose, and chose his reward,
61.5169: The hard pangs of hell, those hot and most dark,
61.5170: The deep dale of death; since unto his Liege he had indeed been disloyal.

62.5171: Suffering His bonds, God’s Bairn still did bide,
62.5172: Did wait at the law-house until the land-folk
62.5173: About Him became all of one mind
62.5174: As to what terrible torture they intended for Him.
62.5175: Then the envoy of Caesar arose from the bench —
62.5176: He, come from Rome; and he went to speak angrily
62.5177: To the crowd of the Jews, there where in the courtyard
62.5178: The many were milling about. The multitude would not come
62.5179: Into the house on the Paschal day. Pilate began
62.5180: To question boldly about the folk of the Jews,
62.5181: Why this Man indeed did deserve His murder,
62.5182: Had reaped such punishment. “Why now are ye wroth,
62.5183: So hostile of mind to this Man?” They said that He had harmed them muchly,
62.5184: Had done them great wrong. “The folk would not give Him over to thee,
62.5185: If they knew not already that noxious He was and evil:
62.5186: He hath forfeited His life with His words. Full many a one of the folk
62.5187: Hath He seduced with His teachings, hath distressed these people,
62.5188: Caused their minds to doubt: that to Caesar’s court
62.5189: We need pay no tithe. That may we tell of Him
62.5190: With truthful witness. Great words speaketh He also:
62.5191: Doth say He is the Christ, King over that realm.
62.5192: With His bigness is He bloated.” But then Caesar’s envoy
62.5193: Did speak again unto them. “If He hath so openly
62.5194: Done deeds of evil,” quoth he, “among the multitude,
62.5195: Then take Him back among your folk; and if He hath forfeited His life,
62.5196: Deal ye His doom, if He is deserving of death,
62.5197: As your age-old laws do order you.”
62.5198: Still at this time on this hallowed day,
62.5199: Quoth they, they could not kill with their weapons,
62.5200: Become murderers of any man whatsoever.
62.5201: Then he turned away from the horde — that man, evil-hearted,
62.5202: The thane of Caesar, who was over his throngs,
62.5203: The envoy from Rome — and he ordered right quickly
62.5204: That the Bairn of God be brought closer to him; and bluntly
62.5205: And carefully questioned Him, whether He were King of this crowd,
62.5206: Of this land-folk here. And the Son of the Lord
62.5207: Had ready His word, asking “Whether thou speakest that for thyself,
62.5208: Or whether for others, the earls here, have
62.5209: Told of My kingdom?” Then truly the envoy of Caesar
62.5210: Spake again, evil and insolent of mind, as he wrangled
62.5211: With Christ Wielder there in the temple. “I am not,” quoth he,
62.5212: “Of this kingdom, of he Jews, am no kin of Thine,
62.5213: No kith of these men, but the many have consigned Thee to me,
62.5214: Thy landsmen, the folk of the Jews have given Thee fettered
62.5215: Into my hands. What harm hast Thou done,
62.5216: That so bitterly Thou must suffer Thy bondage?
62.5217: Torture from Thine own true kin?” Then Christ did tell him again,
62.5218: The Best of All Saviors, as He stood there bound
62.5219: Inside the temple. “My kingdom,” quoth He, “is not
62.5220: Of this hour, of this earthly life. If it were thus,
62.5221: My disciples would be standing strong against the strife-minded,
62.5222: My followers, thanes resisting the throng.
62.5223: Nor fettered, would I be given o’er to the folk
62.5224: Of the hating, the Jews, into their hands
62.5225: To be tortured most terribly. Truly was I born to this world
62.5226: To make known unto you a testimony of truth
62.5227: Through My coming. And that they well may acknowledge,
62.5228: Those men who have strayed from the truth: they may hear my word,
62.5229: Understand and believe My lesson.” Then the envoy of Caesar
62.5230: Could not find a whit of fault with God’s Bairn,
62.5231: Not a word of deceit for which He was worthy
62.5232: Of paying His life. Then he repaired once more to the people of Jews
62.5233: To speak with them angrily. And he said to the many
62.5234: Who hearkened most carefully, that he could find
62.5235: No blasphemous speech, that He should pay with His life,
62.5237: Be worthy of death. Then dull-minded,
62.5238: The Jewish folk did stand and accused God’s Son
62.5239: With their words and said that He had first stirred insurrection
62.5240: And unrest in Galilee-land; and from there had repaired
62.5241: Hither over Judea; and He caused hearts to doubt,
62.5242: The minds of men, “and for that He deserves to be murdered,
62.5243: is worthy of death with the weapon’s edge,
62.5244: If ever a man was deserving of death for such deeds.”

63.5245: The landsmen of Jews lamented loudly to him with their words,
63.5246: Their hearts all hate-filled; then the high lord,
63.5247: The sly-minded man, heard them say unto him
63.5248: From which of the clanships Christ had been born,
63.5249: The Best of All men: He belonged to a glorious band
63.5250: From Galilee-land — Christ the Good. There dwelt a great crowd,
63.5251: A host of aethling-born men. Herod held there
63.5252: A strong, goodly kingdom, which Caesar had given unto him,
63.5253: The mighty from Rome; and there he dealt justice,
63.5254: Practiced right ’mid the people, keeping the peace
63.5255: And dealing out dooms. On that day also
63.5256: He was there in Jerusalem with his thanes and retainers
63.5257: And came to the temple: that was their custom
63.5258: That they held sacred the holy tide
63.5259: The Passover of Jews. Pilate then bade
63.5260: That the soldiers take that Man in His chains,
63.5261: Take Him in His bonds, the Bairn of God,
63.5262: Hight that the earls bring Him to Herod,
63.5263: His hands held in fetters, since He was of that folk
63.5264: Over which Herod wielded power. The warriors accomplished
63.5265: The word of their lord. They led Holy Christ
63.5266: Forth in His fetters in front of the folk-leader.
63.5267: The Best of All Bairns who had ever been born
63.5268: To the light of the land-folk. In His limb-bonds he went,
63.5269: Until they did bring Him there where he sat on his bench —
63.5270: Herod the king. A crowd of people surrounded him,
63.5271: Proud-minded warriors; a great will was within them
63.5272: To see Christ Himself, for they weened He would show them
63.5273: Some token, as indeed He had done through His godliness
63.5275: Before the crowd of the Jews: He, Christ Great and Mighty;
63.5276: Then the folk-king did question Him — full envious was he,
63.5277: Asked many a word and wanted to fathom
63.5278: How His spirit inclined, what He minded to do
63.5279: For the weal of men. There stood Mighty Christ,
63.5280: Was silent and suffered. He chose not to answer him,
63.5281: Herod, the folk-king, nor the earls of his following,
63.5282: Not with one single word. Then the wicked throng,
63.5283: The folk of the Jews stood there, and the Son of God.
63.5284: They did worry and accuse Him wildly, until the world-king
63.5285: Became enraged of heart, and his retainers as well:
63.5286: In their spirits they scorned Him; for they saw the great might of God,
63.5287: Of the Lord of All Heaven; and in their heart there was darkness
63.5288: In the grip of sin. But the Son of the Lord
63.5289: Endured their direful works, their words and their deeds,
63.5290: Suffered them all with a humble soul,
63.5291: All the wrongs they longed to do unto Him.
63.5292: They ordered white robes wrapped around Him, ’round His limbs
63.5293: In mockery; all the more He became for the men there,
63.5294: For the young ones, a jest; and the Jews did rejoice,
63.5295: When they saw how those held Him in scorn,
63.5296: Those earls overweening. Then Herod again,
63.5297: The king, sent Him thence to the other clanships.
63.5298: He hight that a strong man should lead Him hence; and they spake
63.5299: To Him sinfully, heaped blasphemy on Him as He went in His bonds,
63.5300: And they laughed in mockery. But His mind never doubted,
63.5301: But He suffered all with a humble spirit;
63.5302: He wished not to repay them for their wicked words,
63.5303: For their mocking speech and their scorn. They brought Him inside the house,
63.5304: Up in the palace, where Pilate was
63.5305: In the judging place there. The thralls then did give
63.5306: The Best of All Bairns into the hands of the baleful,
63.5307: The murderers — Him without sin, as He Himself chose.
63.5308: He wanted to free the bairns of mankind from the bonds of death,
63.5309: To save them from suffering. The foe stood around,
63.5310: Jews before the guest halls: the bairns of the devil
63.5311: Had stirred up the horde, so that they did not hold back
63.5312: From these grim, wicked deeds. Then he went forth,
63.5313: The thane of Caesar, and to the folk he did speak,
63.5314: The harsh leader of hosts. “What, ye have sent Him here to the hall,
63.5315: Sent this Man unto me in His bonds, have yourselves blamed Him,
63.5316: That He hath brought ruin to right many folk,
63.5317: With His lesson hath led them all wrongly. Now from these landsmen,
63.5318: From this folk, I cannot find that He hath forfeited
63.5319: His life, is guilty of aught. That was indeed clear all these day:
63.5320: Herod, who knoweth your laws, your people, your landways,
63.5321: Could not in anger end His life on this day,
63.5322: Would not say He should die for any sin of His —
63.5323: Should take leave of this life. Now before this land-folk
63.5324: Shall I threaten Him with the law, shall urge Him with words,
63.5325: Shall better the thought in His breast, so that henceforth
63.5326: He may enjoy life among man.” But the multitude
63.5327: Of Jews cried together, called with loud voices
63.5328: And eagerly hight that He be robbed of His life —
63.5329: Christ killed with torture and struck on the cross,
63.5330: Tormented to death. “With His words He hath done it,
63.5331: Hath forfeited life! He sayeth He is the Lord,
63.5332: Truly God’s Son. He shall now pay
63.5333: For His evil speech; so our law is indeed writ:
63.5334: That one buyeth with one’s life such blasphemous speech.”

64.5335: Then he who held sway o’er the folk became sore afraid,
64.5336: In his mind did fear mightily, when he heard the men say
64.5337: That they had heard Him speak thus themselves,
64.5338: Proclaiming in front of the clanships that He was God’s Son.
64.5339: Then the leader of hosts went back in the house,
64.5340: Into the judging hall and hailed God’s Son
64.5341: With confident words and questioned what He was ’mid the clans;
64.5342: “What kind of man art Thou?” quoth he. “Why concealest Thou Thy mind,
64.5343: Hidest Thy deepest thoughts? Wist Thou that Thy life’s destiny
64.5344: Standeth so, even as I shall decide? Unto me have these folk,
64.5345: These people of the Jews given Thee to wield such power o’er Thee,
64.5346: Either to slay Thee with the point of the spear,
64.5347: To torture Thee unto the cross, or to leave Thee quick and alive,
64.5348: Even as I myself deem it better
64.5349: To act for my people.” Then the Peace-Bairn of God spake again:
64.5350: “Thou wist most verily,” quoth He, “that thou would’st wield,
64.5351: Would’st have no might over Me, bu that Holy God Himself
64.5352: Hath granted it unto thee. And those, too, have sinned more,
64.5353: Those who have sent Me to thee in their hatred,
64.5354: Have sold Me, bound fast in these snares.” There straightway thereafter
64.5355: The grim-souled man would gladly have released Him,
64.5356: The thane of the emperor in front of the throng, if he could have but done so.
64.5357: But they denied him his will with their every word —
64.5358: The clan-folk of Jews. “Thou art not,” quoth they, “Caesar’s friend,
64.5359: The beloved of thy lord, if thou leavest Him
64.5360: To go hence sound and unharmed. That may still bring thee sorrow
64.5361: And reprisal, too, if a one speaketh such words,
64.5362: Raiseth himself so high, and sayeth that he here holdeth
64.5363: The name of a kingdom, though Caesar ne’er gave it,
64.5364: He confuseth his world-realms and bringeth scorn to his word,
64.5365: Mocking him in his mind. Therefore must thou avenge such wrongs,
64.5366: These insolent words, if thou hast worry for thy master’s,
64.5367: For thy liege-lord’s friendship. Then should’st thou reft Him of life.”
64.5368: The duke now heard, how the aethlings of the Jews
64.5369: Threatened him with his liege; therefore he went himself
64.5370: And sat at the judging place, where a great host of people
64.5371: Was gathered together, and hight Christ the Wielder
64.5372: Be brought there in front of the folk. The Jews then demanded
64.5373: To see the Holy Bairn first hanging in torment
64.5374: There on the cross; quoth that no other king
64.5375: Would they have to oversee them, except for high Caesar
64.5376: From the city of Rome. “He hath here his rule over us.
64.5377: Therefore shalt thou not release Him; He hath spoken much harm unto us,
64.5378: Hath done in His life through His deeds. Death shall He suffer here,
64.5379: Punishment and the pangs of torture.” The people of Jews
64.5380: Accused Mighty Christ of so many,
64.5381: Of such varied sins. He stood silent
64.5382: There in His humbleness, and not a thing did He answer
64.5383: To the wicked words. He wanted to ransom
64.5384: All men with His life. Therefore He let the loathsome mob
64.5385: Torment Him most terribly, as was truly His will.
64.5386: Yet He had no wish to reveal all things openly
64.5387: To the people of Jews: that He Himself was indeed God.
64.5388: For if they verily knew that He wielded such might
64.5389: Over the mid-world here, then their minds would grow fearful,
64.5390: Be afraid in their breasts; then God’s Bairn they’d not dare
64.5391: To touch with their hands; and the kingdom of Heaven,
64.5392: The greatest of lights, would never be unlocked to the bairns of mankind.
64.5393: Therefore He hid it well in His mind and let not the children of men
64.5394: Know what they were working. Then Weird came nearer,
64.5395: God’s glorious might, and that great midday
64.5396: When they would cause to be done those death-torments.
64.5397: There lay also in bonds within the bastion
64.5398: A notorious robber: in the realm he had
64.5399: Committed murders aplenty and done manslaughter.
64.5400: He was known as a mighty thief. Nor was there his like anywhere.
64.5401: He was in chains because of his sins.
64.5402: Barrabas was he hight, and here in the burg
64.5403: This man was far known for his many misdeeds.
64.5404: That was the land-custom of the kinfolk of Jews
64.5405: That each year for God’s love they could ask amnesty
64.5406: On that holy day for some man doomed to die;
64.5407: And that the leader, warder of bastions, would give him his life.
64.5409: Then the duke began to question the gathering,
64.5410: The folk of the Jews who stood there before him
64.5411: Which of the two they wanted to have freed,
64.5412: To beg for his life: “which are in bonds here,
64.5413: In fetters in front of the clanships.” Then the folk of the Jews
64.5414: Had stirred up all the poorer, the smaller men,
64.5415: So that they asked for the life of the land-robber:
64.5416: They demanded the thief, who in darkness of night
64.5417: Had committed his crimes; and All-Wielding Christ
64.5418: They tortured onto the cross. Then it became truly known unto all
64.5419: How the people had dealt out their dooms. Then had they to accomplish this deed
64.5420: And to hang Him, the Holy Bairn. In times hence that would bring
