64.5421: To the duke great trouble, when he truly knew
64.5422: That the folk of the Jews loathed Christ Savior as their foe,
64.5423: That they hated Him; and that he, Pilate, had hearkened unto them
64.5424: And had granted their will; for this he had evil reward,
64.5425: Punishment here in this light and for long ages after.
64.5426: He won great woe, when he later gave up this world.

65.5427: The Wrong-Doer soon grew aware of this, the greatest of scoundrels,
65.5428: Satan himself, when the soul of Judas
65.5429: Came down to the ground of grim, hot hell.
65.5430: Then most verily he knew that it was All-Wielding Christ,
65.5431: The Bairn of the Lord, who stood there bound;
65.5432: And most verily he knew that He wished to release
65.5433: The whole world and its people From the pangs of hell
65.5434: Through His hanging, leading them all to the light of the Lord.
65.5435: Then was Satan indeed sore of heart,
65.5436: Most troubled of mind; truly he hoped
65.5437: To bring it about that the bairns of mankind
65.5438: Would not rob Christ of life, nor torture Him on the cross.
65.5439: So that the children of men would not be safe from hell,
65.5440: Safe from their sins. Satan hied himself hence
65.5441: To where was the house of the host’s leader
65.5442: Within the bastions. To the bride here openly,
65.5443: To the wife within the weird Fiend began
65.5444: To reveal great wonders, so that with her word-help
65.5445: She would cause it to be that Christ, Lord of Men,
65.5446: Could remain ’mid the quick — for already He was destined to die —
65.5447: For he knew most truly that He would take from him the power
65.5448: So that he would no longer own so much in this mid-world here,
65.5449: O’er this wide, wide earth. The wife became fearful.
65.5450: Sorely troubled was she, since these visions did come unto here
65.5451: In the full light of day through the doing of him
65.5452: Who was hidden by a helmet of magic to make him unseen.
65.5453: With words did she plead with her husband: the wife did hight
65.5454: He be told most truly what visions had come unto her
65.5455: From the Holy Man; and she bade him for help
65.5456: To save His life. “I have seen here so much through Him,
65.5457: So many strange things, that well do I know that the sins
65.5458: Shall thrive indeed of any aethling
65.5459: Who so recklessly hopes to rob Him of life.”
65.5460: The messenger went on his way, until he did find the folk-warden,
65.5461: The duke sitting there among the throng of the people
65.5462: On the stony way, there where the street
65.5463: Is fused together with rocks. And he fared to his lord
65.5464: And told the word of the wife unto him. And the folk-warden
65.5465: Became troubled of soul, and he went inside.
65.5466: The thoughts in his breast grew fearful, for both were grievous for him:
65.5467: That they should slay Him, who was free of sin,
65.5468: And that before this crowd he dared not leave that task undone
65.5469: Because of the people’s word. But then it was turned,
65.5470: The heart in his breast, as the host of the Jews did so want it
65.5471: To work their will. He warded from himself
65.5472: Not a single, dire sin, which he himself there did.
65.5473: He hight them bring him a clear fount for his hands,
65.5474: Bring him water in a vessel, as he verily sat in front of the folk
65.5475: And the thane of Caesar washed himself ’fore the throng,
65.5476: The harsh leader of hosts, and to the horde he did speak,
65.5477: Said that he was freeing himself from such sinful deeds,
65.5478: Such wrongful works; “Nor will I be responsible,” quoth he,
65.5479: “Even one whit for this Holy Man; but yet alone shall carry out all
65.5480: With your words and your works — all which ye do Him here to His woe.”
65.5481: Then all the clanships of Jews cried out togther,
65.5482: The mighty multitude; quoth that against this man
65.5483: They would carry out sentence for His evil deeds. “Let His gore drip down —
65.5484: His blood over us, and the bane of death — and over our bairns as well —
65.5485: O’er our children’s children coming thereafter — we shall still be responsible
65.5486: For the slaying itself — supposing we commit thereby a sin!”
65.5487: There before the throng of the Jews the Best of All Men was then given
65.5488: Into the hand of the haters, held tightly by chains,
65.5489: Forced into fetters — so the foe did receive Him —
65.5490: Those who did loathe Him: the land-folk encircled Him,
65.5491: The churls evil-minded. The Mighty Lord
65.5492: Suffered patiently all that the people did unto Him.
65.5493: They hight He be flogged before they would rob Him
65.5494: Of His life, of His age; and under His eyes they spat at Him.
65.5495: They held Him up to their scorn, and with their hands they did strike Him,
65.5496: The men, ’gainst His cheeks and of His garments they stripped Him,
65.5497: And then renegades robbed Him and took His red robe,
65.5498: And gave Him another — ungracious were they —
65.5499: And a wonderous headband, a crown of hard thorns
65.5500: They hight wound round, and hight it be set on All-Wielding Christ,
65.5501: On Him there, Himself. And the thralls went to Him,
65.5502: In kingly way did address Him, and fell on their knees,
65.5503: And bowed their heads unto Him: in mockery of Him they so did.
65.5504: But all patiently He bore it, the Lord of the Peoples,
65.5505: The Mighty One, for His love for the children of men.
65.5506: They then hight that the men work with the weapon’s edge,
65.5507: Make with their hands out of the hard wood
65.5508: A great, strong cross, and they hight that Christ,
65.5509: God’s Blessed Bairn be brought there Himself;
65.5510: Hight that they lead Him, our Lord, where He was to bleed
65.5511: And to die — He without sin. And the Jews all went,
65.5512: The world-men, all willingly and led All-Wielding Christ,
65.5513: The Dear Lord to His death. Dire things one could hear,
65.5514: Grievous and wrong; groaning, the women did go,
65.5515: Did follow with weeping, and the men were wailing,
65.5516: Those come from Galilee, who did go with them,
65.5517: Faring from far-off ways. For the death of their Fair Lord
65.5518: They were sorrowing sorely. But He Himself, looking back, did see them,
65.5520: Hight that they weep not, “Nor may ye sorrow one whit
65.5521: For My wayfaring hence, but your wicked words
65.5522: Ye may bewail and lament with your weeping,
65.5523: With your bitter tears. For the time will come
65.5524: When the mothers will rejoice, the maids of Judea, that in their lives
65.5525: No bairn was e’er born unto them. For then will ye bitterly pay
65.5527: For your wrongs, right grimly. Then would ye be glad
65.5528: If the high mountains did hide you down here,
65.5529: And bury you deeply. Death would be dearer,
65.5530: Lovelier for all in the land, than to suffer the loathsome
65.5531: Murder of mankind, which will come here to the kinships of men.”

66.5532: Then they set up the gallows on the sandy ground,
66.5533: High on the field, the folk of the Jews:
66.5534: The beam on the hillside; and God’s Bairn was tormented
66.5535: Thereon, on the cross. They struck cold iron
66.5536: Now in their eagerness, nails sharp and new,
66.5537: Hard with their hammers, through His hands and His feet:
66.5538: Bitter bonds were they. His blood ran to earth,
66.5539: The gore of our Good Lord. But this grim deed He cared not
66.5540: To avenge ’gainst the Jews, but He bade God the Father,
66.5541: The Almighty Lord, that He be not wrathful
66.5542: ’Gainst these men, this world-folk, “Since they wit not what they do,” quoth He.
66.5543: Then the war-men dealt out the weeds of the Lord,
66.5544: Divided Christ’s clothing — coarse men of the foe —
66.5545: His fair, rich robes. But the men could not rightly
66.5546: Agree together about the same tunic
66.5547: Until in their crowd they had cast down lots,
66.5548: Which of them was to have this holy garment,
66.5549: The most winsome of weeds. The world-folk’s herdsman,
66.5550: The duke himself, hight that over the head
66.5551: Of Christ on the cross there be writ that this be the true king of Jews,
66.5552: Jesus of Nazareth-burg, who stood there nailed
66.5553: On the new gallows because of grim hatred —
66.5554: On the beam of the rood. Then the folk bade him
66.5555: To change that word, quoth that He Himself had so said as He wished,
66.5556: Had spoken so of Himself, that He wielded power over the people,
66.5557: Was King over the Jews. Then Caesar’s envoy spake once again,
66.5558: The harsh leader of hosts: “Over His head it is now so writ,
66.5559: So wisely inscribed, and I choose not to change it.”
66.5560: The people of Jews then put on each side
66.5561: Of Christ on the cross two men condemned for their crimes
66.5562: And left them there tortured on the gallows-tree as reward
66.5563: For their works, for their loathsome deeds. And the land-folk did speak
66.5565: Many harsh words of scorn unto Holy Christ,
66.5566: And with yelps they did greet Him; they saw the Best of all Men
66.5567: Tormented there on the cross: “If Thou beest King over all,” quoth they,
66.5568: “The Son of the Lord, as Thou Thyself hast spoken,
66.5569: Save Thou Thyself from Thy suffering. Make Thyself free of such hate!
66.5570: Go hence hail and well. Then will this host,
66.5571: The bairns of the folk believe Thee.” So also spake blasphemy
66.5572: A most arrogant Jew who stood at the gallows.
66.5573: “Woe to the world,” quoth he, “if Thou didst wield power over it!
66.5574: Thou sayest Thou canst cast down in one day
66.5575: The high, noble house of the King of Heaven,
66.5576: The greatest of stoneworks, and make it stand once more
66.5577: On the third day. Up to this time no man of the people
66.5578: Hath dared to bring such to pass. But see, how Thou now standest in fetters
66.5579: And in sore distress; nor canst Thou save e’en Thyself
66.5580: One whit from this pain.” Then, too, one of the thieves
66.5581: In fetters did speak — when he heard the folk
66.5582: Uttering wicked words — for his will was ne’er good,
66.5583: The thoughts of this thrall. “If Thou beest King of this folk,” quoth he,
66.5584: “Christ, Son of God, go Thou down from the cross,
66.5585: Slip loose from these snares and save us all,
66.5586: Help us together. If Thou beest the Heaven-King,
66.5587: Wielder over this world, make it known through Thy works,
66.5588: Reveal Thyself to these many!” Then spake the other man
66.5589: Hanging there who stood held in his fetters.
66.5590: Suffering great pain. “Wherefore wilt thou speak such a word,
66.5591: Greetest thou Him with such scorn? Thou standest here held to the gallows,
66.5592: Broken on the beam. We both suffer sorely
66.5593: Because of our sin: our own deeds themselves
66.5594: Have brought us our pain. But He standeth there,
66.5595: Faultless and free of all sin; for He Himself
66.5596: Hath committed no crime; but for the hate of the crowd
66.5597: He willingly endureth dire pain in this world.
66.5598: I shall most willingly believe,” quoth he, “and shall eagerly bid Him,
66.5599: The Son of the Lord, the Warder of Lands,
66.5600: That Thou thinkest of me and that Thou beest my help,
66.5601: O Best of All Rulers, when Thou reachest Thy realm —
66.5602: Have mercy on me!” Then Christ Savior did speak
66.5603: Unto him with His words. “Verily I say unto thee,” quoth He,
66.5604: “That still on this day thou shalt see God’s light
66.5605: Together with Me in the kingdom of Heaven,
66.5606: In Paradise, though thou art now in such pain.”
66.5607: There stood also Mary, the mother of Christ,
66.5608: Bleached pale ’neath the beam, and beheld her Bairn tortured,
66.5609: Suffering such agony. And there were also women there come
66.5610: With her for love of Him, Who was the Almighty.
66.5611: And John stood there, too, the disciple of Christ,
66.5612: Sadly beneath His Lord; and his spirit was sore,
66.5613: Grieved for this death. Then Christ the Great Lord did speak,
66.5614: The Mighty One to His mother: “To My disciple
66.5615: I hereby consign thee, to him who standeth here before Me.
66.5616: Enter thou into his household. Thou shalt have him for a son.”
66.5617: Then He greeted John there, hight that he care for her well,
66.5618: Love her so mildly, as one should one’s mother,
66.5619: This maid without stain. Pure of mind, he received her
66.5620: Into his care, as his Lord had commanded.

67.5621: Then at the mid-hour of day a mighty token
67.5622: Was wonderously revealed over the whole of the world,
67.5623: When they had raised God’s Son onto the gallows,
67.5624: Christ onto the cross: then it became known everywhere
67.5625: How the sun was made swarthy, nor could its fair shimmering light
67.5626: Shine down any longer, but its rays were surrounded
67.5627: With darkness and gloom, and dim fogs did o’ercast it.
67.5628: Thus came the dreariest day, the greatest darkness
67.5629: Over the whole, wide world, as long as the All-Wielder
67.5630: Christ, suffered pain on the cross, the Richest of Kings,
67.5631: Till the ninth hour of the day. Then the mists did divide,
67.5632: The swarthiness scattered, and the light of the sun
67.5633: Appeared clear in the heaven. Then the Strongest of Kings,
67.5634: The Greatest, cried up to God, as He stood on the cross,
67.5635: Fingers and arms fast bound in their fetters. “Father Almighty,” cried He,
67.5636: “Wherefore hast Thou so forsaken Me, Thou My Dear Lord,
67.5637: Thou Holy Heaven-King? And leavest Thy help,
67.5638: Thy support so far? I stand ’mid the foe
67.5639: So terribly tortured.” Then truly the folk of the Jews
67.5640: Laughed to revile Him. They heard Holy Christ,
67.5641: The Lord, before His death, ask for a drink,
67.5642: Heard Him say that He thirsted; but the throng could not cease their harrying,
67.5643: His wicked foes. But there was in them a great wish
67.5644: To bring unto Him still something more of bitterness,
67.5645: And the sin-minded folk had mixed for Him
67.5646: Vinegar, unsweet, and gall, and a man stood ready —
67.5647: A right guilty scoundrel whom they had chosen for this,
67.5648: Had enticed with their speech, so that he took a sponge
67.5649: Loaded with the most loathsome of wines; on a long shaft he put it,
67.5650: Bound to a beam; and to God’s Bairn he did give it,
67.5651: Into the mouth of the Mighty One. Christ saw through this murky deed,
67.5652: Felt well its treachery — He no longer cared to taste
67.5653: Of such bitterness; but the Bairn of God cried aloud
67.5654: To His Father in Heaven. “Into Thy hands I commend Myself,” quoth He,
67.5655: “My ghost, My spirit unto God’s will. It is now good,
67.5656: It is ready to come unto Thee.” The Lord of All Peoples
67.5657: Inclined His head, and His holy breath
67.5658: Escaped from His body. As now the Warder of Lands
67.5659: Died in His ropes, there was straightway revealed
67.5660: A right wonderous token: so that the Wielder’s death
67.5661: Would be made known to the speechless many
67.5662: And His end-day fulfilled. The earth did tremble,
67.5663: And the high mountains shook, and the hard stone split open,
67.5664: The crags on the fields; and the fair curtain was rent,
67.5665: Was torn in two down the middle — that veil in the temple
67.5666: Which had hung there unharmed and most wonderously
67.5667: Broidered for many a day — for the bairns of mankind,
67.5668: The people were never permitted to see what holy things
67.5669: Hung hidden behind that veil. Now they could see the hoard:
67.5670: The Jewish folk could now gaze on it. And the graves of dead men
67.5671: Burst open and wide; and in their bodies
67.5672: They rose up living out of the earth —
67.5673: All through the strength of the Lord — and were there revealed
67.5674: As a marvel to me. This was a mighty thing,
67.5675: That so much should feel, should recognize, too,
67.5676: The death of the Christ: so many a thing that had never spoken
67.5677: One word to any man in this world. Verily the folk of the Jews
67.5678: Saw many strange things; but their cruel spirits
67.5679: Had grown so hard in their hearts, that there was no holy sign,
67.5680: No token revealed unto them, which made them trust more
67.5681: In Christ’s might and strength: that He was the King
67.5682: Over all the peoples of world. But some spake with their words,
67.5683: Some who were set guarding the bodies there in the ground,
67.5684: That this was truly the Son of the All-Wielder,
67.5685: The Best of All Bairns. Some beat their breasts sorely —
67.5686: Some weeping women; wonderous pain they felt,
67.5687: Much hurt in their hearts, at their High Lord’s death,
67.5688: And they were sorely grieved. Now it was the custom of the Jews,
67.5689: That they did not leave any prisoner hanging there longer
67.5690: On a holy day, except just as long, until life had glided away,
67.5692: Till his soul had sunk from him; and the sly, grim-minded men
67.5693: In their hatred came closer to where, along with the Christ,
67.5694: The two thieves were nailed, both suffering torture
67.5695: Along with Him. They were both still alive,
67.5696: Until the loathsome folk of the Jews
67.5697: Broke their leg-bones, and both together
67.5698: Took leave of life, seeking another light.
67.5699: But they needed not drive Lord Christ to His death
67.5700: With further sins of that sort; but they found He had fared thence,
67.5701: His soul had repaired from here on to the right path,
67.5702: To long-lasting light. His limbs had grown cold,
67.5703: The fire had gone from His flesh; then one of the folk went up to Him
67.5704: With hatred of heart; and in his hand he did bear
67.5705: A spear, sharp and nailed. And with sword-strength he did thrust it,
67.5706: Let the point of the weapon cut deep in the wound,
67.5707: So that on one side Christ’s body itself
67.5708: Was laid open. The landsmen there saw
67.5709: That the blood and the water — both did spring forth,
67.5710: Did well from the wound, as was His will,
67.5711: And as before He had marked it for the kinship of men,
67.5712: For the good of the folk-bairns, and so indeed ’twas fulfilled.

68.5713: The bright, shining sun with its beacon of beams
68.5714: Had sunk down further close to its seat —
68.5715: On that gloomy day there did come a thane of our Lord:
68.5716: A clever man was he, a disciple of Christ
68.5717: For a long time already, although not many a man
68.5718: Had ken thereof, since with his words he had concealed it indeed
68.5719: From the people of Jews. Joseph was he hight;
68.5720: He was his Lord’s disciple in secret, and he wished not to follow this sinful folk
68.5721: In their works of wickedness; but amid the Jewish folk he awaited
68.5722: The holy kingdom of Heaven. He went hence to speak to the duke,
68.5723: To make issue with the envoy of Caesar; and he urged him muchly
68.5724: To release Christ’s body from the cross, where it stood in torture
68.5726: To let the Good Man be lowered from the gallows and laid in a grave,
68.5727: Consigned to earth’s folds. And the leader of the folk
68.5728: Did not wish to deny him his will, but did grant him the right
68.5729: To accomplish his deed. Then he did go forth from there,
68.5730: Did go to the gallows, where he knew God’s Bairn,
68.5731: Where he knew the body of his Lord was hanging.
68.5732: From the new rood he did take it and from the nails he freed it,
68.5733: And into his arms he received it — as one should do for one’s dear lord —
68.5734: He took the loved body and wound it with linen
68.5735: And carried it carefully — for his Lord was clearly worthy thereof —
68.5736: To where they had hewn a place with their hands,
68.5737: A spot in the stone, where still no child of mankind,
68.5738: No person had ever been buried. There they placed God’s Bairn,
68.5739: Committed the holiest of corpses, as was their custom,
68.5740: Into the folds of the earth. And with a rock they did close
68.5741: The goodliest of graves. Grieving, there sat
68.5742: Women there in their misery, those who had witnessed all,
68.5743: The grim death of the Man. They started to go thence,
68.5744: The weeping women, watching most carefully
68.5745: On what path they should again go back to the grave.
68.5746: They had seen sadness and sorrow aplenty,
68.5747: Much grief of their minds: Mary were they both hight,
68.5748: These women in misery. Then was the evening come,
68.5749: The night with its darkness. The dire, hating Jews
68.5750: Gathered again in the morning, many together,
68.5751: Speaking in secret: “What, thou knowest surely,
68.5752: That through this One Man thy realm was indeed doubt-rent,
68.5753: The people confused. Now lieth He wound-pierced
68.5754: And buried all deeply. He ever did say that He would arise
68.5755: From the dead on the third day. This many folk do believe.
68.5756: Many people do mark His words. Now order thou a watch,
68.5757: A guard at His grave, lest His disciples
68.5758: Steal Him away from the stone, and say then that He,
68.5759: Rich and mighty, had risen from His rest. Then the warrior-folk
68.5760: Will be angered still more, if they begin to announce that about.”
68.5761: Then there were people appointed from the horde of the Jews,
68.5762: War-men for the watch. They went hence with their weapons:
68.5763: They did go to the grave. There were they to guard
68.5764: The body of God’s Bairn. So passed by the holy day
68.5765: Of the Jews and was gone. They sat over the grave,
68.5766: The warriors on watch in the wide, sparkling night,
68.5767: Biding under their shield-boards, until the bright day
68.5768: Came to mankind over the mid-world here,
68.5769: Bringing light to the land-folk. It was not long thereafter
68.5770: That through God’s strength the spirit returned
68.5771: Under the hard stone. The Holy breath
68.5772: Returned to the body. The light was revealed
68.5773: For the boon of mankind, and many a bolt
68.5774: Was unlatched on hell’s doors, and the way to Heaven
68.5775: From the world was fashioned. Full radiant arose
68.5776: The Peace-Bairn of God, and He did go as He willed,
68.5777: So that the wardens of the grave could not recognize Him even one whit
68.5778: That ruthless rabble — when He rose from the dead,
68.5779: Arose from His rest. Outside ’round the grave
68.5780: The warriors did sit, the host with their shields,
68.5781: The folk of the Jews. The fair sun strode forward,
68.5782: The clear, winsome light. And the women went forth,
68.5783: Going to the grave, wives of good clan,
68.5784: The Marys most lovely. They had sold much treasure
68.5785: Of silver and gold to buy salves, had sold
68.5786: Much of wealth for herbs and for worts. Whatsoever they could gain,
68.5787: So that they could embalm the body of their beloved Lord,
68.5788: The Almighty’s Son, with their herbs and salves,
68.5789: Him slashed with wounds. The women sorrowed
68.5790: So greatly in spirit, and some of them spake:
68.5791: Who would roll it aside, the great stone from the grave
68.5792: For them, the stone which they had seen
68.5793: The men lay over the corpse, when they had consigned it
68.5794: Into its nook in the rocks. When verily now the women
68.5795: Had gone to the garden, so that they might see the grave itself,
68.5797: The Almighty’s angel did come from the sky above,
68.5798: Faring down from the firmament in a shroud of feathers,
68.5799: So that the world, the earth did echo and the men
68.5800: Became weak in their spirits, the watchmen of Jews,
68.5801: And fell down in fright. They feared they would have

69.5803: The thralls, as though dead; then straightway came uncovered
69.5804: The great stone from the grave; for God’s angel
69.5805: Did roll it aside; and the Lord’s radiant herald
69.5806: Did sit him there on the stone; in his face, in his deeds —
69.5807: So that all and each might see with their eyes —
69.5808: He was as bright and blithe as a bolt of lightning.
69.5809: And his weeds, his vestments were as the winter-cold snow,
69.5810: Then they did see him, sitting there on the stone that was turned —
69.5811: The women beheld him; and from the brightness
69.5812: Great fear struck the wives; they were sore afraid
69.5813: And mightily frightened and dared go no further,
69.5814: Dared not go to the grave, until the angel of God,
69.5815: The Wielder’s herald, did greet them with words,
69.5816: Quoth that he knew well what their errand,
69.5817: Their work and their will, and the mind of these good wives;
69.5818: Hight that they fear not, “For I know ye seek Him,
69.5819: Your Lord, Savior Christ, from the city of Nazareth,
69.5820: Him whom the clans of the Jews did torture and nail to the cross,
69.5821: Him sinless they laid in the grave. He Himself is not there,
69.5823: But He hath arisen, and this place is empty,
69.5824: This grave in the grotto. Now may ye go nearer,
69.5825: May come much closer; clearly I know that ye long
69.5826: To see inside of the stone; here still is the spot
69.5827: Where His body was laid.” In their breasts the women, wan though they were
69.5828: And pale, began to be greatly comforted,
69.5829: The winsome, fair wives. A most welcome message
69.5830: They had heard here — that which the herald of God,
69.5831: The All-Wielder’s angel, had said. He hight that they again
69.5832: Go hence from the grave; and go to Christ’s followers
69.5833: And say unto His thanes this word most sooth:
69.5834: That their Lord Most Beloved, lo, had arisen from death
69.5835: Most especially he hight that unto Simon Peter
69.5836: Be told with words this most welcome spell
69.5837: Of the coming of the Lord: that Christ Himself
69.5838: Was in Galilee-land, and there again His retainers,
69.5839: Disciples shall see Him, as He Himself did say
69.5840: With His words of truth. Just as the wives
69.5841: Were about to go thence, there stood before them
69.5842: Two angels clad all in garments of white,
69.5843: In weeds, shining and winsome, and with their words
69.5844: They spake unto them holy things; and the hearts of the women
69.5845: Were made anxious with fright, for they feared to look at God’s angels,
69.5846: Could not gaze into the brightness; for the glory of them was too great,
69.5847: Was too strong to see. Then the Wielder’s heralds spake
69.5848: Again unto them and did ask the women
69.5849: Why they were come to seek Christ the Quick
69.5850: Here ’mid the dead, the Son of the Master,
69.5851: Him filled with life. “Ye shall not find Him
69.5852: Here in this stony grave. But He hath arisen
69.5853: In His body hence; and this shall ye believe;
69.5854: And remember these words, which most verily
69.5855: He Himself hath oft said, when He was with you
69.5856: In Galilee-land: how He would be given over and betrayed,
69.5857: How He would be sold to sinful mankind
69.5858: Into the hand of the hater — the Most Holy Lord —
69.5859: So that they would torment Him, and tack Him to the cross,
69.5860: Would do Him to death, and that on the third day
69.5861: Through the might of Lord God and for the good of all men,
69.5862: He would arise, once more living. That verily hath been done now,
69.5863: Brought to pass ’mid the people. Repair ye swiftly —
69.5864: Haste ye hence, and make this known to the followers of Him.

70.5865: He hath gone on ahead and is away
70.5866: In Galilee-land, and His retainers shall see Him again,
70.5867: His disciples there. And straightway this was joy,
70.5868: Was winsomeness for the women, when they heard such words spoken,
70.5869: Making known God’s might — yet much frightened were they still,
70.5870: Filled with a fear of Him; and they set them forth
70.5871: To go from the grave; and unto Christ’s disciples they gladly
70.5872: Did speak of the wonderous sight, while sorrowing still
70.5873: They bided such bettering. To the bastions were come
70.5874: The Jewish guardsmen, too, who had sat by the grave
70.5875: All the long, long night, had lain in watch o’er the corpse,
70.5876: O’er the body there buried; and while they there bided —
70.5877: They said unto the host of the Jews — what shock, what fright,
70.5878: What strange sight came unto them; and they said also with their words,
70.5879: How it was all so done with the might of the Lord;
70.5880: Nor kept they it hidden within their hearts. And the host of the Jews
70.5881: Offered to them great treasures both of silver and of gold,
70.5882: Bought from them with bright jewels the promise that they would not tell,
70.5883: Nor make this known to the many; “But say ye that with weary minds
70.5884: Ye did fall asleep; and there did come His disciples
70.5885: And stole Him away from behind the stone. Do ye this ever with zeal,
70.5886: Go on in eagerness; and if the folk-leader doth gain knowledge thereof,
70.5887: We shall help you against that high lord, so that no whit of harm,
70.5888: No grief shall o’ertake you” Then they took great treasures,
70.5889: Precious jewels from the people, but pursued the course they had begun
70.5890: For they had no power o’er their will; but they broadcast it widely
70.5891: To the folk in the land, that such lies were here spread
70.5892: About the Holy Lord. Then were the hearts once more healed
70.5893: For the disciples of Christ, when they did hear the good wives
70.5894: Give praise unto God’s power. Then their hearts grew joyous,
70.5895: And both of them ran — John and Peter — right away to the grave,
70.5897: John the good, and stood over the grave,
70.5898: Until soon after Simon Peter did come,
70.5899: Earl famed for his strength; and he went on
70.5900: Going straight to the grave; and he saw there the garments
70.5901: Of God’s Bairn, of His Lord, the linen lying there,
70.5902: The beautiful shroud with which His body
70.5903: Had been bound so fairly. Far from that lay the cloth
70.5904: With which Holy Christ’s head had been covered,
70.5905: Our Mighty Lord’s face, when He lay in this rest.
70.5906: Then John also did go inside the grave
70.5907: To see this strange thing; and straightway thereafter
70.5908: His belief was unlocked, so that he knew that He would again come to this light —
70.5909: His Lord most dear, would arise from the dead
70.5910: Up out of this earth. Then they again went away,
70.5911: The twain, Peter and John, and the retainers, disciples
70.5912: Of Christ came together. With care-filled heart
70.5913: One of the women stood for a second time
70.5914: Groaning over the grave — her spirit was grieved —
70.5915: It was Mary Magdalen — the thoughts of her mind,
70.5916: Of her soul were seized with sorrow, nor knew she where she should seek Him,
70.5917: The Lord who would grant her help. She could not leave off her lamenting;
70.5918: The woman could not cease her weeping. Nor knew she where she could turn.
70.5919: The thoughts of her mind were distracted. Then she saw Mighty Christ
70.5920: Standing there — although she could not perceive Him
70.5921: Until He would say who He was. He asked what she was bemoaning so sorely,
70.5922: So terribly there with her hot tears. She told Him she verily knew not
70.5923: Where they had taken her Lord. “If Thou can’st show me,
70.5924: O my Lord, if I may ask Thee, if Thou hast taken Him away, from behind these rocks,
70.5925: Then instruct me with words — that would be my greatest wish:
70.5926: That I could see Him myself.” She knew not ’twas the Son of the Lord
70.5927: Whom she was greeting with her good speech. She weened ’twas a gardener,
70.5928: Yard-guardian of his master. Then the Holy Lord did greet her
70.5929: By name, the Best of All Saviors. And straightway she came closer,
70.5930: The wife, with good will, and recognized her Savior Himself.
70.5931: In her love she could not refrain, but with her hands she longed to hold Him,
70.5932: The woman to touch the World-Lord. Except that the Peace-Bairn of God
70.5933: Warded her off with His words said that she must not touch Him
70.5934: With her hands. “Not yet,” quoth He, “have I risen to Him, the Heavenly Father.
70.5935: But haste thou now swiftly, and make it known to the earls,
70.5936: To My brethren here, that I will see Him,
70.5937: The All-Wielder, Father of us both,
70.5938: Yours and Mine, too, Mighty God, true and fast.”

71.5939: The woman was in raptures that she could proclaim such joy,
71.5940: Could say of Him, that He was sound and was well. Straightway the woman
71.5941: Was eager to announce this message, and to the earls she did bring it,
71.5942: Welcome tidings to the warriors: that All-Wielding Christ
71.5943: She had seen well and sound; and she said that He Himself
71.5944: Had granted unto her this glorious day. They still wished not to trust
71.5945: The woman’s word, that she brought such a message so welcome
71.5946: Verily from the Son of God, and they sat grieved of heart,
71.5947: The heroes lamenting. Then Holy Christ,
71.5948: The Lord, revealed Himself openly another time
71.5949: Since He rose from the dead. He did so do this
71.5950: For the sake of the woman, that He met them on the way.
71.5951: He spake to them as One whom they knew, and they bent their knee before Him,
71.5952: Fell at His feet. He hight that no fear
71.5953: Should they bear in their breast. “But unto My brethren
71.5954: Shall ye make known My message, that they shall follow
71.5955: Into Galilee-land. There shall I meet them again.”
71.5956: On that selfsame day of the disciples
71.5957: Two earls early already that morn
71.5958: Were faring on business. They wished to find them the fortress
71.5959: Of Emmaus, the castle. Among the men many
71.5960: A word did begin to wax, as they fared on their way,
71.5961: About their Holy Lord. Then they were joined by the Hallowed One,
71.5962: God’s Son, going that way. Still not a whit could they grasp,
71.5963: Could recognize the Mighty One. He did not want to manifest Himself to them yet;
71.5964: Still He went along with them, and He asked about what they were speaking:
71.5965: “Why go ye so groaning,” quoth He, “Ye twain with such grieving hearts
71.5966: And souls filled with sorrow?” They straightway replied unto Him,
71.5967: The earls then gave answer: “Why dost Thou ask so?” quoth they.
71.5968: “Art Thou from Jerusalem from the folk of the Jews?”
71.5969: “… The Holy Ghost from the fields of Heaven
71.5970: With the great strength of Lord God.” Now He took those good earls,
71.5971: His disciples there and He did lead them out,
71.5972: Until He brought them to Bethany.
71.5973: There He held up His hands and hallowed them all;
71.5974: With His words He did bless them. Then He went Him hence,
71.5975: Sought the high realm of Heaven and His holy throne.
71.5976: And there He doth sit on the right side of God,
71.5977: The Father Almighty. And from there All-Wielding Christ
71.5978: Gazeth down and seeth what power doth surround the world.
71.5979: Then on the same spot the disciples good
71.5980: Fell down in prayer, and the followers of Christ
71.5982: To the city they hastened, and their hearts were joyous.
71.5983: In the temple they tarried. Truly the strength of the Wielder …
